title: Bill Belichick on Louisville-UNC brawl: "That's not what we're here for"
summary: Saturday's game between Louisville and North Carolina ended in a brawl, sparked apparently by the Tar Heels being a little too aggressive in defending a victory-formation play.
full_text: Saturday's game between Louisville and North Carolina ended in a brawl , sparked apparently by the Tar Heels being a little too aggressive in defending a victory-formation play. After UNC's 16-14 loss to the Cardinals, Carolina coach Bill Belichick addressed the brouhaha. "You play the game between the whistles, that’s not what we’re here for ," Belichick said, via the Associated Press. "We got out there and got everybody out as quickly as possible." Footage from WRAL shows Belichick involved in the effort to clean up the mess, pulling several of his players away from the fray. It started when North Carolina defensive tackle Xavier Lewis and Louisville offensive lineman Johnnie Brown III got engaged in some pushing and shoving. The situation spread into various confrontations as the benches emptied. The next question is whether discipline will be issued, by the individual teams or the ACC. No penalties were enforced, because the game ended in the early stages of the altercation. At 5-5, the Tar Heels need a full roster next weekend, if they hope to become bowl-eligible with a win over Virginia. The season ends with a game against NC State.
author: Mike Florio

title: Starting with Patriots-Lions, Fox has three windows on Sunday
summary: The last of the early-morning 2026 kickoffs happens today, with the Patriots playing the Lions in Germany.
full_text: ' The last of the early-morning 2026 kickoffs happens today, with the Patriots playing the Lions in Germany. Unlike the others, which were televised by NFL Network, the Week 10 European game will be carried by Fox. That gives Fox three windows in one day, with the morning game followed by the usual 1:00 p.m. ET window and the every-other-week 4:25 p.m. ET window. Most of the country will see Vikings-Packers, featuring the return of Kirk Cousins, on Fox at 1:00 p.m. ET. The only Fox game at 4:25 p.m. ET will be 49ers at Cowboys. With the Fox pregame show starting at 9:00 a.m. ET, it gives Fox more than 10 hours of continuous NFL broadcasting on Sunday. And with five of the six teams having winning records (and the sixth being the Cowboys), the numbers should start large and keep growing — culminating in a very large audience for the late-afternoon window, which has become the biggest of the NFL week .
author: Mike Florio

title: With trade offers rejected, Titans' plans for Tony Pollard come into question
summary: All the factors had lined up for a Tony Pollard trade.
full_text: All the factors had lined up for a Tony Pollard trade. With a trade not happening, the Titans' future plans for Pollard come into question. At 1-7, the Titans aren't contenders. Pollard is in the final year of his contract. While a compensatory draft pick becomes possible in 2028 (depending on Tennessee's 2027 free-agent acquisitions and losses), the Titans could have gotten a draft pick in 2027 if they'd traded him. What could they have gotten? As we hear it, they turned down a fourth-round pick and a player. (The Packers and the Broncos were the two teams linked to Pollard .) So what's the plan for Pollard? Maybe they want to keep Pollard beyond 2026. He's in the last season of a three-year, $21.75 million deal. He's making $7.25 million this year. And Pollard is on track for his fifth straight 1,000-yard season. He's not even in the top 20 highest-paid running backs by annual average. The franchise tag at the position for 2027 is expected to be in the range of $15 million. Pollard will be 30 in April. That makes it harder to put a proper number on his next contract. But if the Titans weren't willing to take the best offer they could get for him, it suggests that they have a plan premised on potentially signing him to a new contract. The decision to keep Pollard could be as simple as the Titans not being confident in their alternatives. Pollard has 147 touches in eight games. His backup, Tajae Spears, has 33 in six games. Rookie Nick Singleton has seven in four games. Julius Chestnut has no touches in eight games. The answer could be that simple. The Titans had insufficient confidence in their other options if Pollard was traded. Which would have complicated the ongoing effort to develop quarterback Cam Ward. Regardless, the Titans had a chance to get something now (we don't know the name of the player that was offered; it could have been a running back) and a 2027 draft pick by trading Pollard. They decided not to. Pollard will now keep going, and quite possibly finish with more than 1,000 yards again. Which could result in Pollard leaving in 2027 — possibly with the Titans not getting a compensatory draft pick in 2028.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers will fly to Colorado tonight to begin acclimating to altitude for Mexico City game
summary: The 49ers won't fly home after today's game in Dallas.
full_text: The 49ers won't fly home after today's game in Dallas. Instead, they'll immediately begin preparation for next Sunday night's game in Mexico City. The team plane will fly to Colorado Springs tonight, as coach Kyle Shanahan believes spending a week at altitude will help the 49ers' chances against the Vikings next week at Estadio Azteca, the highest stadium the NFL ever plays in. "I think it helps," Shanahan said. "I grew up mainly in Denver, and I know how bad it would be for me. No matter how good of shape you're in, you come home from college and you run up the stairs and you're out of breath. It takes some time to get used to altitude. I know when you go to play in Denver it's always a challenge, and Mexico City is higher than Denver. It's not make or break, but I do think it makes you a couple percent better." Shanahan thanked Air Force head coach Troy Calhoun for allowing the 49ers to use his team's practice facility in Colorado Springs, as he did before the 49ers' Mexico City game in 2022. Air Force's Falcon Stadium is at 6,621 feet. Estadio Azteca has an altitude of 7,280 feet — exactly 2,000 feet higher than Denver's Mile High elevation. Next Sunday night will be the 49ers' second international game of the season. They opened the season in Australia, where their decision to arrive a week early to get used to the time difference was credited as one of the reasons for their impressive performance against the Rams. Now they hope another weeklong preparation will yield similar results.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Arch Manning shakes off 3 interceptions, throws game-winning TD pass as Texas beats LSU
summary: As he has been throughout his college football career, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was a mixed bag on Saturday.
full_text: As he has been throughout his college football career, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was a mixed bag on Saturday. But Manning and Texas came out on top. After throwing three interceptions and seeing his team fall behind LSU 21-10, Manning turned it on late, culminating in a 12-play, 58-yard drive that saw Manning throw the game-winning touchdown pass with three seconds remaining as Texas won 22-21. "That's what college football is all about," Manning said after the game. Manning's numbers were not impressive: 19-of-35 for 174 yards and one touchdown with three interceptions and four sacks, plus 35 yards and a touchdown running. But when Texas needed him to march the offense down the field at the end of the game, he did it. His touchdown pass to Raleek Brown was a perfectly placed ball, and he also ran for two first downs on the game-winning drive. For No. 6 Texas, the win means they'll almost certainly be in the College Football Playoff, as they'll be heavy favorites the next two weeks against Arkansas and Texas A&M. For LSU, the loss knocks first-year coach Lane Kiffin out of playoff contention. Manning, the scion of the first family of quarterbacks, will have an opportunity do what neither his grandfather Archie nor his uncles Peyton and Eli ever did: Win a national championship.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Lions, Jets renegotiated Andre Cisco trade after concerns arose about his physical
summary: The Broncos-Chargers Daiyan Henley trade wasn't the only one affected by the player's physical.
full_text: ' A controversy arose after the NFL trade deadline when the Broncos demanded to change the terms of their trade with the Chargers after linebacker Daiyan Henley's physical. But Henley wasn't the only traded player whose physical raised concerns. The Lions also told the Jets they wanted to change the terms of their trade for safety Andre Cisco after concerns about his physical. But unlike the Chargers, the Jets agreed to it, and the Lions ultimately sent the Jets a 2029 sixth-round pick for Cisco after initially agreeing to give up a 2028 sixth-round pick. Tom Pelissero reports that the modified terms were based on medical concerns. There's no word on what those concerns were, but Lions coach Dan Campbell said the plan is for Cisco to play on Sunday against the Patriots. The Jets went along with the Lions' request, and in the scheme of things the difference between a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 sixth-round pick is minor. Still, it points to an inherent flaw in the NFL's trade rules: The team acquiring a player has the ability to go back on the trade, or negotiate better terms, after the trade deadline. That puts the team trading the player in a difficult position: After you've already told a player you're trading him, and told another player you're signing him or bringing him up from the practice squad to take his place, you don't want to go back on that. So if the team you're trading with tells you, "We didn't like his physical, so we'll back out of the trade unless you take less compensation," you may feel you have no choice but to accept. The NFL could resolve that by not allowing trades to be renegotiated after the deadline: Either the player passes the physical and the trade goes through, or the player fails the physical and the trade does not go through. No more half measures like, "We failed him on his physical, but we'll pass the physical if you agree to take a lesser draft pick for him." Another solution could be that physicals for traded players are conducted by an independent, league-appointed doctor, rather than the team's medical staff. If that doctor says the player passes the physical, the team trading for the player can't back out. The Jets and Chargers had different reactions to their trade partners asking to renegotiate the trades, but the situation both teams were faced with highlights potential problems that can arise with the NFL allowing teams to change the terms of trades after the trade deadline.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Three referees will be working in other roles on Sunday, due to the ground stop
summary: The full scope of the adjustments to the usual officiating crews isn't officially known.
full_text: The full scope of the adjustments to the usual officiating crews isn't officially known. It's clear, however, that Friday's nationwide ground stop will result in significant changes to the usual groupings of officiating crews. On Saturday morning, the NFL announced that three non-referees will serve as referees for four Week 10 games, with one of them — Don Willard — working as the referee for the 1:00 p.m. ET game between the Dolphins and Colts before traveling to Cincinnati for Sunday night's Steelers-Bengals game. Via Ben Austro of FootballZebras.com, three referees will be working in other roles on Sunday. Referee Carl Cheffers and referee Alex Kemp will work as umpires. Referee Shawn Hochuli (pictured) will work as a back judge. The reconfiguration resulted from the NFL's decision to assign officials to games within driving distance of their homes. Austro also notes that the replay officials for all Sunday games will work out of NFL headquarters. They were in Detroit on Friday for an all-day, in-person training session. Instead of fanning out to the various game locations, they all went to New York. It sets the stage for a potentially strange day, with any mistakes inevitably being blamed on the inability of the NFL to get the officials where they needed to be. If it works, however, it could prompt the NFL to reconsider the overall staffing plan, if there's a way to do it that reduces expenses. I think that's a tongue-in-cheek remark. I hope it's a tongue-in-cheek remark. Either way, Sunday could get interesting. The players and coaches have gotten to where they're supposed to be. The officials haven't, and the deck has been dramatically reshuffled in order to ensure that each game will be properly staffed.
author: Mike Florio

title: Game between Bill Belichick's UNC and Louisville ends in a brawl
summary: Saturday's not alright for fighting.
full_text: Saturday's not alright for fighting. But a fight nevertheless happened at the end of the game between Louisville and Bill Belichick's North Carolina Tar Hells. The Cardinals led, 16-14, with time ticking away. (UNC had a timeout remaining but hadn't used it on the final Louisville drive, after a game-sealing interception.) Louisville received the snap and took a knee as the clock hit 15 seconds. North Carolina, despite not using its final timeout, deployed the Schiano-style effort to blow up victory formation. Which sparked a shoving match match between opposing lineman. Which eventually became a full-blown brawl. Through it all, time expired and the game ended. It will be interesting to see whether the ACC or the individual schools hand out suspensions as a result of the fracas. The loss dropped North Carolina to 5-5. The Tar Heels need one win in remaining games against Virginia and NC State to become bowl-eligible in Belichick's second season on the job. And that could be harder to do against Virginia next week, if one or more UNC players end up being required to sit out.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chris Jones rejoins Chiefs after traveling on his own to Atlanta
summary: On Saturday afternoon, the Chiefs announced that defensive tackle Chris Jones would travel on his own to Atlanta for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
full_text: On Saturday afternoon, the Chiefs announced that defensive tackle Chris Jones would travel on his own to Atlanta for Sunday's game against the Falcons. On Saturday night, the Chiefs announced that Jones had arrived. "Chris Jones has rejoined the team in Atlanta," the team said. " He will play tomorrow ." The situation was not injury related; the team attributed it to a personal matter . It's generally unusual for players to travel on their own to road games. This weekend particularly, individual travel became even more complicated, given the aftermath of Friday's nationwide ground stop. Regardless, Jones got to where he needed to be, and he'll be playing for the 6-2 Chiefs as they try to match the Broncos, who are on a bye, at 7-2 atop the AFC West.
author: Mike Florio

title: Steelers activate DT Derrick Harmon
summary: Defensive tackle Derrick Harmon is set to return to the Steelers lineup against the Bengals on Sunday night.
full_text: '' Defensive tackle Derrick Harmon is set to return to the Steelers lineup against the Bengals on Sunday night. The Steelers announced that they have activated Harmon from injured reserve on Saturday. Harmon returned to practice this week after missing the last four games with a foot injury. Harmon had 12 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and a forced fumble in the first four games of the season. The 2025 first-round pick had 27 tackles, three sacks and a fumble recovery during his rookie season. The Steelers released defensive back Terrell Smith in a corresponding move. He was signed off the Commanders' practice squad in October and made one tackle in his lone appearance for Pittsburgh.
author: Josh Alper

title: Rex Ryan will appear on ESPN's Sunday pregame show, despite arrest
summary: ESPN hasn't said much about analyst Rex Ryan following his recent arrest in Nashville for running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck.
full_text: ESPN hasn't said much about analyst Rex Ryan following his recent arrest in Nashville for running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck. It has sparked a question as to whether Ryan will appear on ESPN's Sunday morning pregame show. “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown,” ESPN said on Saturday night. It's not believed that Ryan will be addressing the matter on the air. He faces six misdemeanors as a result of the November 4 incident. He's due in court next month. Video of the incident reportedly exists . It has yet to be released. It probably will emerge at some point. Of course, Ryan's presence (or not) may not have even been noticed; with the Patriots and Lions playing at 9:30 a.m. ET, who'll be watching the ESPN pregame show?
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers-Saints game won't have a replay assistant, due to ground stop
summary: Travel issues will leave at least one game short-staffed.
full_text: The nationwide ground stop that shut down the aviation system has impacted the NFL's officiating assignments for Sunday games. And while the league has announced the specific changes that will result in non-referees serving as referees for four games on Sunday (with side judge Don Willard working two games in the same day ), other adjustments have not been officially announced. There surely will be others. For now, one game will be shorthanded. Via Tom Pelissero of Netflix, the Panthers-Saints game won’t have a replay assistant . Those duties will be handled by the league office. Which will put a strain on the usual resources there, especially in the cluster of 1:00 p.m. ET games. (Panthers-Saints is one of the seven games to be played in that window.) Given that the league has otherwise adjusted the Week 10 assignments to keep the officials within driving distance of their hometowns, it's likely that the existing crews will be altered significantly. Which will introduce unfamiliarity and otherwise complicate the effort to get calls right on a consistent basis. Absent an advance announcement from the league as to the full extent of the changes, they won't be known until the NFL posts the official Game Books for the Sunday contests.
author: Mike Florio

title: For Week 9, Jalen Pitre was fined twice for illegal use of helmet
summary: Every Saturday, plenty of players get fined for illegal use of helmet fouls from the prior weekend's game.
full_text: Every Saturday, plenty of players get fined for illegal use of helmet fouls from the prior weekend's game. For Week 9, Texans safety Jalen Pitre got fined twice. Both instances occurred in the second quarter of the victory over the Chargers. Pitre was penalized for neither infraction. Each fine will cost $15,400, subject to appeal. They were Pitre's first fines of the season. For the season (including the preseason), 53 fines have been imposed for illegal use of the helmet. The NFL will impose larger fines on Pitre for future violations. Eventually, he'll be at risk for a suspension. Use of the helmet isn't one of the five safety rules that trigger a one-game suspension in the event of three violations.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jesse Minter: "Very, very impressed" with how Jacoby Brissett picked up offense
summary: It appears quarterback Jacoby Brissett earned a good grade in his crash course on the Ravens offense.
full_text: It appears quarterback Jacoby Brissett earned a good grade in his crash course on the Ravens offense. Brissett joined the team a little over a week ago in a trade with the Cardinals and is on track to start against the Chargers on Monday night. In comments to reporters on Saturday, head coach Jesse Minter didn't make it sound like Brissett will be limited to a small portion of the team's playbook when he takes the field. "The stuff you heard about was just like, 'Hey, he's a veteran presence and a real pro,'" Minter said, via the team's website. "Obviously, he's been around different systems and things like that. I would just say, I'm very, very impressed with how fast he's learned what we’re doing ." The Ravens head into Monday's game in last place in the AFC North, so they'll need Brissett to operate at a high level right out of the gate to stay in the thick of the playoff race heading into the back half of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Titans put Peter Skoronski, Tommy Townsend on IR
summary: The Titans ruled left guard Peter Skoronski out on Friday due to a hamstring injury and his absence is going to last beyond this Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
full_text: The Titans ruled left guard Peter Skoronski out on Friday due to a hamstring injury and his absence is going to last beyond this Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Skoronski was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Punter Tommy Townsend (knee, Achilles) also landed on the list and both players are going to miss at least four games as a result of the moves. The Titans also announced that they have waived running back Michael Carter. They signed guard Chandler Zavala, defensive back Isaiah Oliver, and punter Thomas Morestead to the active roster to fill the open spots. Wide receiver Xavier Restrepo and linebacker Dominique Hampton were elevated from the practice squad to round out the day's moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots place TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve
summary: Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson's absence from the lineup will stretch through at least Week 15.
full_text: ' Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson's absence from the lineup will stretch through at least Week 15. The Patriots placed Henderson on injured reserve Saturday as he continues to deal with a neurological issue that kept him out of the team's last two games. Henderson was ruled out for this Sunday ahead of the team's trip to Germany to face the Lions. Rhamondre Stevenson is listed as questionable for that matchup with a knee injury, which leaves Corey Kiner and Lan Larison as the healthy running backs on New England's roster. In addition to the Henderson move, the Patriots activated fullback Reggie Gilliam and guard Greg Van Roten from injured reserve. They also elevated guard Andrew Rupcich from injured reserve. Van Roten and Rupcich help fill out a position group that will be missing Ben Brown against the Lions. Walter Rouse is listed as questionable due to a concussion as well.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jakobe Thomas gave Kirk Cousins No. 8 for nothing (other than wins)
summary: The Raiders arguably could have driven a harder bargain over the trade that sent quarterback Kirk Cousins back to the Vikings.
full_text: The Raiders arguably could have driven a harder bargain over the trade that sent quarterback Kirk Cousins back to the Vikings. Vikings safety Jakobe Thomas could have driven a harder bargain over the return of Cousins's preferred number. Thomas told reporters that he gave Cousins No. 8 without payment. “No money needed,” Thomas said, via Ben Goessling of the Minneapolis Star Tribune . “I just need him to come here and win games . A lot of fans have his jersey anyway, so they could pull him out of the closet and put him back on. So that's all it is. Kirko's got a lot more memories and history in that number than I do, and it's rightfully his. So I just gave it back to his rightful owner.” Thomas moved to No. 6, the jersey number he wore at Middle Tennessee State. It makes sense. Thomas, a third-round pick out of Miami in April, has yet to be active for a regular-season game. Cousins is returning with the goal of winning a lot of games. Starting with Sunday at Lambeau Field, the site of the final game of his first stint with the Vikings.
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers activate RB Chris Brooks, WR Skyy Moore
summary: The Packers will have two offensive players back in the lineup for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings.
full_text: The Packers will have two offensive players back in the lineup for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings. Running back Chris Brooks and wide receiver Skyy Moore were both activated from injured reserve on Saturday. Brooks ran 15 times for 70 yards in the first four weeks of the season and has missed five games with an ankle injury. Moore has also been out with an ankle injury and had seven catches for 35 yards in five appearances. Brooks provides depth in the backfield with Josh Jacobs out this week. Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd, and Pierre Strong are also on hand. The Packers made space for Brooks and Moore by placing tight end Josh Whyle on injured reserve and waiving wide receiver Coleman Owen.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jared Goff takes 1-3 career record vs. Patriots into Germany game
summary: For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter.
full_text: ' For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter. That's a 59.7-percent win rate. Against the Patriots, Goff is 1-3. That's a 25-percent win rate. In those four games, Goff has two touchdown passes and five interceptions. Sunday's game in Germany will be the first one against the Patriots with a coach other than Bill Belichick. Goff has never faced current Patriots coach Mike Vrabel; during Goff's time as a starter with the Rams and Lions and Vrabel's tenure with the Titans, their two teams never crossed paths. Goff's first loss to New England came in 2016, in his third career start. The Patriots won, 26-10. Two years later, New England beat Goff and the Rams in the Super Bowl, 13-3. In 2020, Goff and the Rams beat the Patriots, 24-3. In 2022, the Patriots beat Goff and the Lions, 29-0. Sunday's game is consequential for both teams. The 6-2 Lions are caught in a cluster of four NFC North teams that all have six or more wins. The Patriots, at 5-4, are fading in the AFC East race and could be scrambling to secure a wild-card spot.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chargers list Ladd McConkey as questionable for Monday night
summary: Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is among the Chargers players listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the Ravens.
full_text: Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is among the Chargers players listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the Ravens. McConkey is dealing with a back injury that kept him off of the practice field this week. McConkey has dealt with a number of injuries this season and has 17 catches for 286 yards and a touchdown on the season. The Chargers also listed guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle), tight end David Njoku (fibula), linebacker Denzel Perryman (pectoral), and offensive lineman Trey Pipkins (personal, knee) as questionable. Njoku, Perryman, and Pipkins will need to be activated from injured reserve in order to play against Baltimore. Wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) is considered doubtful while guard Branson Taylor (ankle), cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), and safety Kendall Williamson (calf) have been ruled out.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys place RB Tyler Goodson on injured reserve
summary: The Cowboys said this week that running back Tyler Goodson will miss multiple weeks due to knee and ankle injuries and we learned on Saturday that he'll be out for at least the next four games.
full_text: The Cowboys said this week that running back Tyler Goodson will miss multiple weeks due to knee and ankle injuries and we learned on Saturday that he'll be out for at least the next four games. Goodson was placed on injured reserve as part of a series of roster moves the Cowboys made ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers. Those moves also included elevating running back Israel Abanikanda from the practice squad to join Javonte Williams in the backfield. Cornerback Derion Kendrick was also elevated for Sunday's game. Joey Porter Jr. and DaRon Bland are both listed as questionable. In addition to those moves, the Cowboys waived defensive end Tyrus Wheat while signing tight end James Mitchell off the practice squad and activating defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard from injured reserve.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Rodgers reunites with Jordan Rodgers
summary: Aaron Rodgers insists on keeping his personal life private.
full_text: '' Aaron Rodgers insists on keeping his personal life private. Except when he decides to take it public. Before retreating to the position that it's nobody's business. On Friday night, Rodgers reunited with his brother, Jordan. Via TMZ, Aaron Rodgers posted on social media a photo with Jordan on Friday . Jordan was in Pittsburgh for the game between Florida State and Pitt. "Great to see little bro @jrodgers11 in his element tonight @acrisurestadium," Aaron Rodgers said in the caption attached to the photo. "Really proud of how hard he’s worked to get to where he is now." When Rodgers and his family first renewed acquaintances earlier this year, Jordan was omitted . It was no surprise; the public rift between the brothers started when Jordan spoke about the situation during his time as a contestant on The Bachelorette . Here's a prediction. If a reporter asks Aaron about the photo with Jordan after Sunday night's game against the Bengals, Aaron will refuse to talk about private matters — despite the fact that he chose to make the matter anything but private with his social-media post.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL tells Senator that Jalen Hurts review will include "mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts"
summary: Five weeks since Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts played a game in London with a blood clot in his leg, the NFL and NFL Players Association have not yet begun an official investigation of the situation.
full_text: Five weeks since Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts played a game in London with a blood clot in his leg, the NFL and NFL Players Association have not yet begun an official investigation of the situation. As noted on Friday by Tim McManus of ESPN, the league and the union are still working " to hammer out [the] parameters " of the investigation. That has not stopped the NFL from providing some preliminary information to Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), who previously expressed concerns about the situation in a letter to the league. "As outlined by the league and NFLPA's Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties," NFL executive vice president of communications, public affairs and health policy Jeff Miller said in a statement that was released by Blunt Rochester's office on Friday. It's still unclear how the investigation will proceed or what it will entail. The NFLPA has not yet invoked its absolute right to launch an investigation under Article 39 of the Collective Bargaining Agreement as the communications with the league continue. The ensuing delay is approaching the status of "head scratching." With games being played every Thursday, Sunday, and Monday, there's a constant risk of a similar situation arising. The sooner the Hurts situation is properly explored and any lessons learned from it are put into action, the sooner all players will benefit from any enhanced protections. The Eagles and the league created widespread skepticism regarding whether a coverup is happening. (The NFL may not appreciate that being said, but that doesn't make the perception inaccurate.) The NFLPA can't afford to be viewed as being complicit in an effort to sweep the incident under the rug. Through it all, the most effective investigative process comes from litigation, an adversarial process aimed at getting to the truth. However it happens as to Hurts, the only goal should be getting to the truth about why it all happened — and how it can be prevented from happening again.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers activate WR Xavier Legette from IR
summary: The Panthers got wide receiver Xavier Legette back at practice this week and he will be available for Sunday's game against the Saints.
full_text: The Panthers got wide receiver Xavier Legette back at practice this week and he will be available for Sunday's game against the Saints. Legette was activated from injured reserve on Saturday. He has been out since suffering a knee injury in Week 2. Legette had two catches for 64 yards before his injury. The Panthers also designated cornerback Mike Jackson, and running back Jonathon Brooks for return from injured reserve this week, but neither one of them will be joining Legette in the lineup. The Panthers elevated cornerbacks Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton from the practice squad. They provide extra depth with Jackson and Jaycee Horn still on injured reserve and Will Lee (hamstring) listed as questionable to play.
author: Josh Alper

title: Colts activate Arden Key, place Mo Alie-Cox and Akeem Davis-Gaither on IR
summary: The Colts have not won a game since defensive end Arden Key went on injured reserve and he'll be back as they try to snap their five-game losing streak against the Dolphins on Sunday.
full_text: The Colts have not won a game since defensive end Arden Key went on injured reserve and he'll be back as they try to snap their five-game losing streak against the Dolphins on Sunday. Key missed all five of those games with a hamstring injury. He started the first four games of the season and had five tackles, a forced fumble and a half-sack in those appearances. While Key will be back, the Colts will be without tight end Mo Alie-Cox (groin) and linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) for at least the next four games. Both players were placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Key takes one of those roster spots and the other has been filled by signing linebacker West Weeks off of the practice squad. Long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer and wide receiver Quez Watkins were elevated from the practice squad in other moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Texans rule David Montgomery out for Sunday
summary: Texans running back David Montgomery will not make his return to the lineup in Sunday's game against the Browns.
full_text: Texans running back David Montgomery will not make his return to the lineup in Sunday's game against the Browns. Montgomery was listed as questionable to play on Friday's injury report, but the Texans announced on Saturday that he will not travel with the team and has been ruled out. This will be the fourth straight game that he has missed with a groin injury. The Texans also announced that cornerback Jaylin Smith (hamstring) will not be activated from injured reserve. Linebacker Jake Hummel has been activated from injured reserve. He's been out since Week 1 with a groin injury. title: Packers, Broncos explored possible Tony Pollard trade
summary: One week before the trade deadline, teams had interest in Titans running back Tony Pollard.
full_text: One week before the trade deadline, teams had interest in Titans running back Tony Pollard. But Tennessee was not yet talking. The Titans eventually engaged, but no one met their price. Via ESPNFL, the Packers and Broncos " checked in " on Pollard. The Titans wouldn't move Pollard for less than a third-round pick. Both teams had been linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. The Colts, after creating the impression that Taylor would be traded, opted to take the best offer they could get. The fact that Green Bay and Denver explored acquiring two different tailbacks isn't much of a vote of confidence in their current depth charts. As to the Packers, it underscores the potentially tenuous status of Josh Jacobs. Pollard, a fourth-round pick of the Cowboys in 2019, started his career as the backup/understudy to Ezekiel Elliott. Pollard had a breakthrough season in 2022, rushing for 1,007 yards and making it to the Pro Bowl despite Elliott still being the starter. (Elliott gained 876 yards that season.) Pollard became the full-time starter in 2023, a franchise-tag season. He signed with the Titans in 2024. He has four straight 1,000-yard seasons. Through eight games in 2026, he has 595 yards. Which puts him on pace for what would be a career-high 1,190 yards. Pollard is in the final year of a three-year, $21.75 million contract. He's due to be a free agent in March.

title: Bengals vs. Steelers prediction: AFC North rivals to battle for first place in the division on 'SNF'

full_text:
The 10th Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will conclude with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals battling for first place in the AFC North division.
Pittsburgh (6-2) currently leads the North by virtue of its Week 5 win over Cincinnati (6-2). The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. The second of those two losses occurred the last time these two teams played in Cincinnati. Last October, Cincinnati won a 33-31 shootout. The Steelers won the rematch a month later in Pittsburgh.
Here's how you can follow the action in real time. We've also included a breakdown and a prediction for Sunday night's showdown.
The Steelers sealed a 30-27 win when Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow on the Bengals' final series. Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred.
Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception.
Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns.
Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-27 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain.
It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury.
Pittsburgh's success has been powered by Warren (and, to a lesser degree, fellow running back Rico Dowdle , who has played well in a complementary role since returning from his injury in Week 6) and a defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters. Pittsburgh is once again getting high-level play from T.J. Watt , who has already eclipsed his 2025 sack tally.
Cincinnati's current winning streak has largely been the byproduct of Burrow (who leads the NFL in completion percentage and touchdown passes) and his success throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The Bengals have also received solid play from a defense that is getting big contributions from offseason acquisitions Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe .
This game will come down to two things: Pittsburgh's ability to throw the ball (which would in turn help open things up for the running game) and Cincinnati's ability to keep Burrow clean, which has at times been an issue against the Steelers.
The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline. While Pittsburgh's plan can in theory work, its lack of depth at the receiver position might come back to haunt them on Sunday night.
In close matchups like this, special teams can often make the difference. If that ends up being the case in this game, the Bengals have the advantage in Evan McPherson , who has not missed a field goal or an extra point this season. Conversely, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell has already missed field goals this season. Pick: Bengals 23, Steelers 20

title: FAA ground stop forces NFL to reshuffle officiating crews for Week 10
summary: The changes include one referee pulling double-duty on Sunday
full_text:
The NFL has made several officiating changes for Week 10 in response to Friday's FAA ground stop. Officials have been reassigned to games that are within driving distance of their hometowns.
Among the biggest changes for Sunday will be two referees working games as umpires, three backup referees assigned to work games, four officials working multiple games, and one game without on-site replay officials and assistants.
Alex Kemp, who is ordinarily a referee, is going to be an umpire under Clete Blakeman for the Packers ' home game against the Vikings . Carl Cheffers, who is also ordinarily a referee, is going to be an umpire under Bill Vinovich for the Raiders ' home game against Seattle.
Backup referees Barry Anderson (umpire), Duane Heydt (umpire) and Don Willard (side judge) will each work as referees on Sunday. Anderson will work the Titans ' home game against the Jaguars . Willard, who has never worked as a referee for a regular season game, will work the Colts ' home game against the Dolphins before making the nearly two-hour drive to Cincinnati to work the night game between the Bengals and Steelers .
Along with Williard, umpire Terry Killens, field judge Jabir Walker and side judge Justin Larrew will also make the road trip from Indianapolis to Pittsburgh to work Sunday night's game in Cincinnati after working the Colts-Dolphins game. This might get interesting if the Colts-Dolphins game goes into overtime, delaying their arrival in Cincinnati. Regardless, it's safe to assume that there will be no shortage of caffeine consumption for this group of officials on Sunday.
Don Willard isn’t the only #NFL official doing two games tomorrow as of the current assignments. Willard, the side judge who will serve as referee for @NFLonCBS ’ #Dolphins - #Colts game before driving to Cincy to ref @SNFonNBC ’s Steelers- #Bengals game, is slated to be joined by…
As noted above, the league's replay officials and assistants were also impacted by the ground stop. The result is that the Panthers ' home game against the Saints ' will not have on-site replay officials and assistants.
The #NFL ’s replay officials and assistants were all in Detroit for a clinic Friday. I’m told by the league office that ALL are able to get to their originally assigned games, with the exception of #Panthers - #Saints . The replay official’s duties for that game will be handled from…
Below is a rundown of each officiating crew and their assigned games, courtesy of CBS Sports NFL sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala. The bold names indicate the backup referees who will be working tomorrow's games.
How will all this impact the games? Kinkhabwala asked a longtime, now-retired NFL official whether these changes will create any specific challenges. According to his response, the first few series may go a long way toward determining how smoothly the rest of the game goes.
"He said familiarity and a general crew tempo are real, so we should watch how the officials adjust to each other the first couple series," Kinkhabwala wrote on X. "And while most officials watch film of the teams they have to be aware of tendencies (and won't have time to do so now), he did downplay any impact there, saying it's ultimately all about watching your keys."
With tomorrow’s #NFL games featuring thrown-together officiating crews on new assignments, I asked a longtime (now-retired) NFL official if that presented any specific challenges. He said familiarity and a general crew tempo are real, so we should watch how the officials adjust…
The FAA ground stop -- the second since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks -- resulted in more than 2,000 canceled flights. The stop was later attributed to the addition of new technology to the nation's air traffic control system, which caused "intermittent" communications and radar gaps.

There's arguably no offense hotter right now than the Bengals . Over their four-game winning streak, they've averaged over 35 points per game, and Joe Burrow has been playing at an MVP level. The Cincinnati QB has 18 total touchdowns over this stretch and a 132.0 passer rating. Simply put, they've been a bulldozer. However, I do think it's worth pointing out who they've played over the course of the winning streak: at Dolphins , at Ravens (no Lamar Jackson ), vs. Titans and vs. Falcons . While they'll be at home in Week 10, Cincinnati is coming off an international game in Madrid last week. As for the Steelers, they're fresh off their bye week, creating a sizable rest discrepancy. That may only put them further behind the eight ball against a Chiefs team that cruised to a 35-12 win over the Jets last week. Patrick Mahomes did give us all a scare in the midst of that game after injuring his elbow, but it's not serious enough to keep him out of this matchup.
Mahomes has thrown five touchdowns and no interceptions over his past two games, but his lack of a downfield threat has been noticeable. He's averaging an NFL-low 5.6 air yards per attempt this season as the Chiefs have really looked for pass catches to put up yards after the catch. The wideout has a knack for creating separation and now has a capable quarterback to deliver the football to him, so Kansas City could see quick dividends from this addition. That's a lot of talent being drained from the defense, which doesn't bode well against Trevor Lawrence , who is making a sneaky MVP push. Injuries are popping up all around the league as we enter the second half of the 2026 season, and that includes at running back. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III, whose 872 rushing yards rank as the second most in the NFL this season, popped up on the injury report on Friday after tweaking his groin, causing him to not practice on the final day of the week. Walker was ruled out by the Chiefs on Saturday.
"We're feeling it out just to see. We're not going to put him at risk," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Friday, via ESPN . "If he can go, he'll go. If he can't, he can't."
Some believe new Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr.'s absence in Week 9 at the Indianapolis Colts with an ankle injury is somehow connected to his lack of a new contract in the final year of his rookie deal. However, Porter Jr. (ankle) made it clear that isn't the case on Thursday. He called his entire foot, heel and ankle "jacked up." He also said the determination on whether he will play against the San Francisco 49ers will be made after practice on Friday and based on how he feels on Sunday. Porter Jr. didn't practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but he was a limited participant on Friday. That's why the Cowboys listed him as questionable for Week 10.
"That has no, I don't even know where that narrative comes from. I get it, it's the internet. I don't really pay attention to that. I don't really care for that," Porter Jr. said after practice on Thursday. "My goal is to win games and play football. That's what I want to do. If there's any chance I can get on the field, I'm going to get on the field and do what I do best."

title: NFL week 10 anytime TD best bets: Look for Chris Olave, Jonathan Taylor to find the end zone

full_text:
Welcome to our 10th NFL Sunday of the year! Can you believe it? This week, Kirk Cousins leads the Minnesota Vikings against Jordan Love and the red-hot Green Bay Packers , the Carolina Panthers and New Orleans Saints play an important divisional game in the Superdome, and the lead in the AFC North is up for grabs when the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals take the field on "Sunday Night Football."
Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a running back.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
Bhayshul Tuten is the lead back for the Jacksonville Jaguars , but he missed two practices this week with ankle and foot injuries. Chris Rodriguez Jr . is the goal-line back, and he's scored touchdowns in two consecutive games despite receiving just 16 rushing attempts.
With the Jaguars facing the lowly Tennessee Titans this week, Rodriguez should get another chance at a goal-line touchdown -- which could come much easier since Jeffery Simmons is no longer on that defensive line. Or, maybe Rodriguez gets more touches if this is a blowout.
Chris Olave has registered under 100 yards receiving in four straight games after beginning the season with 100 yards in three of his first four games. He's recorded just two receptions of 20+ air yards over the last four games, which is surprising. We predict Olave gets back on track this week against the Panthers secondary, which allowed Bo Nix to have one of his best outings of the season last week, and got diced up by Christian Watson and Matthew Golden the week prior. Olave has scored touchdowns in each of his last two games against Carolina.
I don't love suggesting a -120 touchdown scorer, but I like this situation for Jonathan Taylor . He can finally exhale now that the trade deadline has officially passed, and this week, his Indianapolis Colts host one of the worst teams in the NFL that is starting a quarterback who has never taken a snap in an NFL game before. Taylor scores on Sunday.
Here's an interesting flier. Keenan Allen played the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday when he was still with the Colts. After he was traded to the San Francisco 49ers on Tuesday, Allen will play the Cowboys again this Sunday!
Mike Evans won't play again this week, but Deebo Samuel is back. Allen just got to town, but I can see Kyle Shanahan utilizing him like he did Evans earlier in the year in the red zone. This is my long shot of the week.
One of my favorite bets I made this year was for Tee Higgins to score a touchdown against the Steelers in Week 3. He was already off to a hot start at that point, and had actually caught touchdowns in each of his last two games vs. Pittsburgh. Sure enough, he cashed at +175 with six catches for 90 yards and a touchdown. Higgins has caught six touchdowns in eight games this season! He and Ja'Marr Chase are virtually unguardable, as this dynamic duo has caught 47 passes for 693 yards and eight touchdowns over the last three games. You can take Chase to find the end zone at -120, but I'll opt for the plus money. This Bengals team is on an absolute roll, having scored at least 34 points in three straight games. I'll keep riding this passing attack.

full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images Cardinals safety Kitan Crawford’s wallet is a little lighter after he was hit with a $5,775 fine for a blindside block in Week 9 during the Cardinals’ 17-3 loss to the reigning Super Bowl champs, the Seattle Seahawks. Crawford was not flagged for the blindside block during the game. It’s his only fine so far in the 2026 season. The Cardinals selected Crawford in the seventh round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Over his first season and a half, he’s landed 30 tackles, a pass breakup, and a blocked kick for Arizona. Crawford was the only Cardinal fined in Week 9’s losing effort. On the Seahawks side, linebacker Ernest Jones was fined $23,882 for unnecessary roughness in the first quarter for a hit on Cardinals QB Gardner Minshew. Jones was flagged for the play in real time. Cornerback Devon Witherspoon was also fined $17,911 for taunting Trey McBride after a Seahawks’ defensive stand in the fourth quarter. It’s Witherspoon’s second taunting fine of the season — he was fined $11,941 earlier this season for taunting receiver Mack Hollins when the Seahawks beat the Patriots in the season opener, which is why this fine is so steep. The NFL splits the funds it collects from player discipline and splits it between the NFLPA’s services to support retired players, the NFL Foundation, and other nonprofit organizations supporting sports leagues, community health initiatives, and player health and safety initiatives at all levels of sports.

title: Falcons’ new starting C Corey Levin is ready to go vs. Chiefs
summary: The best offensive lines function as one. Chemistry is so important to the success of this position group, and it’s most important for the center who’s calling the protections. This is why I was mildly surprised the Falcons shipped Ryan Neuzil off to the Ravens just before the trade deadline on Tuesday. The NFC South […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - SEPTEMBER 24: Corey Levin #62 of the Atlanta Falcons stands in the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The best offensive lines function as one. Chemistry is so important to the success of this position group, and it’s most important for the center who’s calling the protections. This is why I was mildly surprised the Falcons shipped Ryan Neuzil off to the Ravens just before the trade deadline on Tuesday. The NFC South is a mess, every team is currently sitting with three wins, and winning the division is still very possible. Michael Penix Jr.’s early career and development have been disrupted by injury and Kirk Cousins, and switching out centers in the middle of the season doesn’t seem like the smoothest path to his success. You know who isn’t worried about the chemistry with his teammates? New starting center Corey Levin. For Levin, it’s all about building trust with his teammates. “First and foremost, just proving to them that they can trust me with everything that they trusted Neuzil with,” Levin said Wednesday. “And then, obviously, I’m a different player than Neuzil. We play our own style and things like that. So them getting comfortable with how I may do a certain thing or communicate a certain way — just building that as quick as possible, and we get plenty of reps of practice to do it. So we really have no excuse.” While Neuzil would have gotten the first-team practice reps to prepare for each opponent up to this week, the backup center does take some early reps with the starter in each practice and in warmups before each game. In the immortal words of legendary Falcons safety William Moore , “How am I supposed to get ready when I stay ready?” That’s the goal for the backup center — to stay ready in case the next man up is needed. And now Levin is. When asked about the differences between his play and Neuzil’s, Levin noted the difference in their builds and athleticism. “Like, he’s extremely athletic, and I’m not saying I’m not athletic. But I might weigh a little bit more than him, so different ways to play center. And I try to emulate him when he’s here, for the offense that we’re running, and now that he’s not here, just kind of doing… not entirely my way, but still within my way.” And now that Levin is the Falcons’ starter, he got about 60 practice snaps per day with the starting offense in this week’s practices to prepare for the Chiefs this week. His teammates describe Levin as a high-energy, happy guy. His experience as an NFL journeyman certainly impacted that attitude. “[I’m] just kind of always a positive, upbeat guy,” he said. “I’m happy to come to work with a smile on my face. Just because I’m grateful. Like you said, I bounced around. I know what it looks like to not have exactly the situation you want to be in. So when you’re in the building every day, it’s a blessing. Sunday’s game against the Chiefs will be Levin’s eighth NFL start. He’s played 14 offensive snaps and 36 special teams snaps so far this season.

title: Falcons vs. Chiefs series history: Win-loss record, matchup results
summary: The Falcons keep the train rolling in AFC play with a date against the Kansas City Chiefs before the bye week. These teams have not met each other often due to the difference in conferences, but in the games where they have faced off, KC has often come out on top with an 8-3 advantage […]
full_text: ATLANTA - SEPTEMBER 21: Running back Larry Johnson #27 of the Kansas City Chiefs is tripped up by cornerback Brent Grimes #20 of the Atlanta Falcons at Georgia Dome on September 21, 2008 in Atlanta, Georgia. The Falcons defeated the Chiefs 38-14. (Photo by Doug Benc/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons keep the train rolling in AFC play with a date against the Kansas City Chiefs before the bye week. These teams have not met each other often due to the difference in conferences, but in the games where they have faced off, KC has often come out on top with an 8-3 advantage in the head to head record. The matchups have been more balanced in recent years, but in the early days KC always came out on top, winning the first four matchups, the latter three of those by double digits. These teams only met those four times over a 28 year period between 1972 and 1999. In 2000, the Falcons finally registered their first victory against the Chiefs, doing it behind Chris Chandler in a quarterback matchup against Elvis Grbac, whose one passing touchdown in the game went to a young Tony Gonzalez. The Chiefs got revenge and then some in the next meeting, in 2004, securing a 56-10 victory in a game where Priest Holmes and Derrick Blaylock each had four rushing touchdowns. Atlanta finally started settling some scores behind Matt Ryan, who led the Birds to blowout wins in 2008 and 2012, but recent history has things looking a lot more like pre-2000 with three consecutive wins for a Chiefs team that has built a dynasty since their last defeat to Atlanta. When these teams met last The Kansas City Chiefs were the best team in the league, coming off of back to back Super Bowl titles and on the hunt for a three peat when they went to Atlanta for a date on Sunday Night Football. The upstart Falcons were in the midst of Raheem Morris’ first season at the helm and had new quarterback Kirk Cousins leading them. Things got off to a perfect start for the Falcons when Cousins connected with Drake London for an opening drive touchdown. Patrick Mahomes led the Chiefs on a methodical 17-play drive which ate up over eight minutes, but he was then intercepted by Justin Simmons (who made a habit of picking off Mahomes in his career) in the red zone. The Chiefs and Falcons traded touchdowns to begin the second quarter before Atlanta’s offense went quiet. Atlanta’s next three drives were a 3 and out, interception and another 3 and out as KC kicked three field goals and found the end zone via a Juju Smith-Schuster touchdown before the Falcons finally got something going and put up a field goal of their own to make it a one score game again, at 22-17. From there the defense tightened up, forcing two 3 and outs against the prolific Mahomes, while the offense put together two very long drives that reached the Chief red zone, but they came away with no points turning it over on downs both times. Controversy ensued when it looked like Kyle Pitts was interfered with in the end zone on a 3rd and goal on the first of those drives with no call made. The comeback attempt fell short.

McConkey, 25, was a last-minute scratch for last Sunday’s game against the Houston Texans due to back spasms that began during pregame warmups. His lack of progress this week suggests he is unlikely to suit up, depriving Justin Herbert – who is dealing with an injury to his non-throwing hand – of his best receiver. That is good news for a Baltimore secondary that has struggled to stop opposing passing games this year, making even the league’s lowest-scoring offense a potential threat. That secondary, though, will be without Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) for another week. The former Patriot occupied a 81% snap share but seemed to struggle as the Ravens’ third safety before fore going down in Week 6. He returned to practice in a limited capacity this week but will still miss his fourth straight contest. The Ravens also listed running back Adam Randall (foot) as questionable pending his activation from injured reserve. The sixth-round rookie was a full participant in practice all week, and the Ravens have open spots on their 53-man roster. The stage could be set for owner Steve Bisciotti’s personal draft pick to make his NFL debut. The winless Chargers listed nine additional players on their final Week 10 injury report alongside McConkey, including tight end David Njoku and defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe. title: Jaguars DT Arik Armstead fined for hip drop tackle on Ravens RB Derrick Henry
summary: The NFL is still struggling to officiate hip drop tackles in games, but the league has been vigilant in enforcing penalties after the fact via fines. No Ravens had their wallets lightened this week, but Jaguars defensive lineman Arik Armstead will have to cough up $17,911 after a hip drop tackle on Derrick Henry. Henry […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - NOVEMBER 05: Arik Armstead #91 of the Jacksonville Jaguars rushes the passer during an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on November 5, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL is still struggling to officiate hip drop tackles in games, but the league has been vigilant in enforcing penalties after the fact via fines. No Ravens had their wallets lightened this week, but Jaguars defensive lineman Arik Armstead will have to cough up $17,911 after a hip drop tackle on Derrick Henry. Jaguars DL Arik Armstead was fined $17,911 for this hip-drop tackle early in the third quarter last week on Derrick Henry. No Ravens fines from Week 9. pic.twitter.com/hSezxvFhAn — Jonas Shaffer (@jonas_shaffer) November 14, 2026 Henry is no stranger to shouldering a heavy burden, but he was asked to do even more than usual against Jacksonville. Joe Fagnano’s ankle injury limited his dropback abilities and set Henry up for plenty of action out of wildcat formations. The 11-year veteran doubled his previous high of five snaps at ‘quarterback’ last Thursday. The Ravens have struggled with penalties in all three phases this season, but their offense have rarely been egregious enough to qualify for a fine. Baltimore’s players have been fined just six times this year, tied with three other teams for the fifth-fewest penalties. The roster has collectively be fined $101,496, the eighth-lowest sum in the league. Linebacker Roquan Smith is responsible for three fines worth $47,763, roughly 47% of the team’s total. On a per-fine basis, however, the Ravens rank second with an average of $16,916.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens update QB Lamar Jackson’s status after successful thumb surgery
summary: November 14: Jackson underwent surgery on his thumb last week, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Minter declined to confirm on Saturday, only saying “the surgery happened and the timeline is the timeline.” November 13: The Baltimore Ravens released a statement from head coach Jesse Minter on Friday morning that delivered the team’s first rough timeline on […]
full_text: Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images | Getty Images November 14: Jackson underwent surgery on his thumb last week, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter . Minter declined to confirm on Saturday, only saying “the surgery happened and the timeline is the timeline.” November 13: The Baltimore Ravens released a statement from head coach Jesse Minter on Friday morning that delivered the team’s first rough timeline on Lamar Jackson’s return from a thumb injury suffered 0n November 1. Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8. Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return. We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season. The statement is the most concrete update on Jackson’s status since he went down two weeks ago in Buffalo. However, it lacks the following information: Has Jackson undergone surgery on his thumb? If so, when? If not, when will he get surgery on his thumb? Is the given timeline based on when he suffered the injury, when the statement was released, or when he undergoes surgery? The first three questions were subsequently answered by ESPN’s Jamison Hensley and The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec, who both reported that Jackson has undergone surgery and is currently in the rehab process. It is somewhat baffling why the Ravens would not include that information in their statement. Presumably, the beat reporters who confirmed the surgery received their information from a team source. Why, then, couldn’t the team just say that Jackson had undergone successful surgery? Giving a precise date is not even necessary – the type of thing fans and media would love to know, but do not really need to.

title: Buffalo Bills game-day food: Pancakes with Bourbon-Pepper Syrup
summary: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a […]
full_text: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a themed recipe based on the Bills and their opponent. I don’t usually write dissertations before recipes, but I’m gonna make you read a short story this time around as I explain the lore behind these pancakes. Dawkins Pancakes w/ Bourbon-Pepper Syrup Thank you to my incredible sister for taking me to the home opener this season, which marked the first meaningful game in the Buffalo Bills’ new home. What a day of memories it was, starting well before we even approached the stadium. These pancakes have a story, and I hope I do it justice. If you’re the type of person who gets aggravated with recipes starting with really long narratives, this might not be your week… My sister is the more social one of us and before we head in for the game we do the rounds at her favorite tailgate stops. And that’s how I ended up meeting Dion Dawkins’ mother aka “Mama Dawk.” Before I go any further you’ve hopefully come to trust my analysis over the years and you’ll believe me when I saw she’s an absolute gem. That applies to the whole family as far as I can tell, as there was another family member at that game I had the pleasure to talk to (more on that in a second) and yet more of the family at the Ravens game. Now, shameless self-promoter that I am at times, I mentioned this series and asked what Dion Dawkins’ favorite food was so I could do a recipe. To my surprise, not only did Mama Dawk take the time to indulge me and thoroughly contemplate the question; she called over the other family member so we could really nail down the details. Now for an aside… I try to take things seriously despite my (lousy) attempts at humor. I know who I spoke with and made sure to get their name. After meeting them, I wanted to make sure I treated things respectfully because; truth be told, while Dion and Mama Dawk have become deeply intertwined with the community I knew far less about the rest of the family. The last thing I would want is to toss someone into a spotlight who may not want it. So this will have to be a “trust me bro” type of source. I didn’t find public mentions of this person so I won’t be the one to blow up any potential spot. If I get confirmation it’s OK to reveal the source, I’ll change that stance. But for now what I’ll stick to is that if you’re reading this; It was great to meet you, I can’t thank both you and your mother enough for taking the time to brainstorm this one. Finally, I made a promise to send positive thoughts your way the following day as you had a bit of a big deal going on. I’m thinking you likely nailed it with or without my positive vibes, but I kept my promise as a small way to thank you. Now for the rest of you reading this you’re here for pancakes, which I assume by now you figured out is what I was told is Dion’s favorite. I could have left it with that, but I wasn’t about to let the chance to dig deeper into things slip away. Now I want to clarify a bit. While pancakes were noted to be Dion’s favorite, he was busy attending to the matter of playing against the Detroit Lions. I was enjoying the conversation with my unnamed source and well, I wasn’t about to walk away without some information on what they liked so I could steer the recipe. After all, there’s a ton of ways to make pancakes. My big takeaways were that both sweet and savory flavors were good choices. I was told very directly that crispy edges were a preference. The bourbon-and-pepper infused syrup I made for these adds some savory/umami direction to the dish, but doesn’t hold back on the sweet. And you can bet these edges are crispy. The last decision I needed to make was what game to make these for. Sorry for the wait on these, but I wasn’t about to forget the New Jersey connection. I appreciate everyone who took the time to read this and indulging the story. We’re all here for food, but once in a while the wall of words is necessary. Dawkins Pancakes with Bourbon-Pepper Syrup Makes: Enough for 4-5 people Active time: 30 min Total time: 2-3 hours Ingredients Bourbon-Pepper Syrup 2 serrano peppers 2 shots of bourbon 1 cup maple syrup Pancakes 2 cups all-purpose flour 1 tsp salt 1 Tbsp baking powder 2 large eggs 2 cups heavy cream 1/2 cup maple syrup 1 cup water, divided as noted below 3 Tbsp unsalted butter, melted Extra butter for frying Essentials: Shot glass, sauce pan, mixing bowls (one large, one medium), measuring cups and spoons, egg beater or whisk, rubber spatula, fry pan, ladle or large spoon, spatula Wash peppers and cut into small pieces (I made rings); removing seeds is optional. Immerse peppers in bourbon; cover and let them soak 1-2 hours. Strain pepper-infused bourbon into sauce pan; add 1 cup maple syrup. Bring to light simmer on LOW heat; cook off alcohol and reduce mixture back to syrup consistency, about 10 min. Preheat pan on stovetop to MED heat (on my stove I used between 5 and 6.5 out of 10, see below). Combine flour, salt, and baking powder in large mixing bowl. Beat (or whisk) together eggs, heavy cream, 1/2 cup maple syrup, melted butter and start with 1/2 cup water (see tips below on changing liquid amount and how that impacts cooking temp and time) in medium mixing bowl. Pour liquid mixture slowly into dry mixture while beating or whisking together; scrape sides of bowl and beat/whisk again. Place a small pat of butter in center of frying pan; allow to melt. Ladle pancake batter into center of pan (see below on tips for testing before committing to this step). When bubbles start to form through pancakes (about 3 min), flip and cook another 1-2 min. Repeat until you’re either out of batter or tired of making pancakes; whichever comes first. Enjoy! Wingin’ It tips I’ve learned this year through researching this and another recipe that capsaicin is alcohol soluble. What does that mean? It means soaking peppers in bourbon is a very fast way to get spicy bourbon. The first picture shows how big the peppers I used were so you have an idea of what I did. You could also do a hotter variant than serrano, but uh… maybe don’t. On the second picture I show the leading edge of a pancake with bubbles around it. That’s the butter. If you drop the butter in the center then follow suit with the batter, the batter will naturally displace the butter to the edges and that’s how you get crispy edges. Incidentally, do you see that there’s a couple little lumps of dry ingredients in there still? Totally fine. They cook in without any issue. The last two pictures are just fun. I promised “see below” several times and I can wrap all of them up in short order. One of the great things with pancakes is how easy it is to modify them to your liking. I started off this recipe with 1/2 cup of water and the batter was very thick. Now, that’s how I like them. These fluff right up and it’s like a cloud. That said, you need to cook them longer and at lower temperature that way. That was 5 on the stove for temperature and each pancake can take 7 or 8 minutes. In the picture with the butter above, that’s with about a full cup of water added in. These spread out in the pan much easier. They cook faster, about 4 or 5 minutes per pancake. You can push the crispiness a bit further by turning the heat up. I was about 6.5 on the temperature doing that. Speaking of temperature, going too high will burn your butter and that’s no good. You can use other fats (like vegetable oil) that take higher heat before scorching and should still get crispy edges if you want to cut down on cooking time. For my two cents though, butter is where it’s at. Give me money. Money me. Money now. Me a money needing a lot now ! Skarekrow likes certain products. Skarekrow likes money. Skarekrow recommends the following…
