title: Cowboys vs 49ers: 2 players to buy, 2 to sell against San Francisco
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are coming off a narrow win over the Indianapolis Colts, and now the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers are coming to town, bringing one of the league’s most complete rosters and a defense that has consistently given Dallas problems in their recent matchups. There are some opportunities for the Cowboys, particularly with CeeDee […]
full_text: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are coming off a narrow win over the Indianapolis Colts, and now the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers are coming to town, bringing one of the league’s most complete rosters and a defense that has consistently given Dallas problems in their recent matchups. There are some opportunities for the Cowboys, particularly with CeeDee Lamb playing at a high level, but there are also some difficult matchups that could expose weaknesses on Dallas’ roster. Here are two players to buy and two to sell ahead of Sunday’s game. Buy: CeeDee Lamb I mean, who else would this list start with? Lamb has been the best player for the Cowboys all season, and there’s no reason to think that Dallas will stop feeding him the ball. Lamb is coming off a monster performance against Indianapolis, hauling in 10 catches for 195 yards and a touchdown on 16 targets. It was his second-highest receiving total in a game during his career. Through nine games, Lamb has 70 receptions for 904 yards and seven touchdowns. He’s already surpassed the 900-yard mark, and his 108 targets lead the Cowboys by a wide margin. The matchup against San Francisco is difficult, but Lamb is the kind of receiver who can change a game regardless of the opponent. With George Pickens possibly missing another week and Dallas dealing with inconsistencies elsewhere the offense, Dak Prescott should continue looking Lamb’s way early and often. The 49ers will undoubtedly have a plan for him, but Lamb’s recent production makes him difficult to leave out of the buyers market. He’s been the Cowboys’ most reliable playmaker overall, and Dallas needs to find ways to get him involved. DAK TD TO CEEDEE FOR 44 YARDS DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uIIXrKbg2y — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Sell: Dak Prescott At some point, the Cowboys have to figure out how to beat San Francisco, and Dak Prescott has to be a big part of that solution. Unfortunately, his history against the 49ers doesn’t inspire much confidence. Prescott is 2-4 against San Francisco in his career, including an 0-2 record in the playoffs. In those two postseason games, he has thrown for 460 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. His most recent regular-season meetings haven’t been much better. He threw three interceptions in the 2023 blowout loss and two more in the 2024 matchup. Across his four regular-season games against San Francisco, Prescott has completed 65.5% of his passes for 875 yards, eight touchdowns and five interceptions. That’s not necessarily disastrous production, but the turnovers have been costly, particularly against a team that knows how to capitalize on mistakes. The 49ers have won four straight meetings against Dallas, and Prescott will have to overcome both that team history and his own struggles against this opponent. San Francisco’s defense is disciplined, physical and capable of making quarterbacks pay for forcing throws. With Fred Warner leading the unit, Prescott will have to be sharp with his reads and decision-making, especially against the blitz, where he has looked terrible this year. Dallas needs a big performance from its quarterback to pull off the upset. Given the history, though, this is a matchup where I’m selling Prescott until he proves otherwise. Another zero blitz look where everyone is running deep routes and no one is in the middle of the field. Dak let's it fly early and takes a big-hit, almost looks like a go ball, but Lamb is running a post. Miscommunication? Bad ball? Still begging someone to ask someone why they… pic.twitter.com/sPycW7qg9y — Connor Livesay (@ConnorNFLDraft) November 9, 2026 Buy: Brevyn Spann-Ford With Jake Ferguson ruled out due to a knee injury, Brevyn Spann-Ford has an opportunity to take on an even bigger role in the Cowboys’ offense. It might not be the most obvious matchup to exploit, but he could be a sneaky contributor against San Francisco. Spann-Ford has caught 15 passes for 130 yards this season, and his role has been growing. Against Indianapolis, he played 55 offensive snaps compared to Ferguson’s 27, catching two of three targets for 20 yards. That workload suggests the Cowboys are already comfortable giving him significant playing time. The 49ers have plenty of defensive talent to account for, and their attention will naturally gravitate toward Lamb and the Cowboys’ other primary playmakers. That could leave opportunities for Spann-Ford underneath or in the middle of the field, particularly if Dallas uses him to help with protection before releasing him into a route. This isn’t a prediction that Spann-Ford is suddenly going to become the focal point of the passing game. Rather, it’s a bet that his increased playing time and the attention paid to Dallas’ other weapons could create a few favorable opportunities. With Ferguson unavailable, the Cowboys need someone else to contribute from the tight end position. Spann-Ford is in a good position to do that. Sell: Jaishawn Barham The Cowboys have indicated that Jaishawn Barham could see an increased workload as injuries continue to pile up on the defensive side of the ball. That’s understandable from a personnel standpoint, but it also creates a potential problem against an offense as versatile as San Francisco’s. Barham had some encouraging moments early in the season, but his limitations have become more apparent as the competition has increased. His playing time has also been limited recently, which makes the prospect of a larger role against the 49ers particularly concerning. San Francisco is exactly the type of opponent that can put a young linebacker in difficult situations. Kyle Shanahan’s offense uses motion, misdirection and mismatches to create space, and open up running lanes. If Dallas gives him more responsibility, San Francisco will have plenty of opportunities to test him. The Cowboys need all the help they can get defensively, but this is a tough week to ask an inconsistent young player to take on a bigger role.

title: Cowboys key matchup: Dallas WRs vs San Francisco 49ers CBs
summary: Ahead of the 2026 season, all Dallas Cowboys fans had Week 10 circled. The Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers rivalry dates back to the 70’s, but recently the Cowboys have come up short more often than not. Heading into Week 10, the two teams are not playing on the same level. Sitting at 7-1 the […]
full_text: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images | Getty Images Ahead of the 2026 season, all Dallas Cowboys fans had Week 10 circled. The Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers rivalry dates back to the 70’s, but recently the Cowboys have come up short more often than not. Heading into Week 10, the two teams are not playing on the same level. Sitting at 7-1 the 49ers are staring the NFC number one seed in the face, while the Cowboys are currently fighting for their lives to make the postseason. With both teams banged up and final injury reports issued , we can finally get an idea of what the key matchup for this contest will be, and the Cowboys best path to victory is pretty clear. The 49ers defense is currently seventh in the NFL in EPA/play and 14th in success rate, but their number one rush defense in the NFL helps weight those rankings. If the Cowboys are able to pull of a massive upset, the Cowboys will need to win through the air, early and often. Through nine weeks, the 49ers have the 12th-ranked defense in the league in terms of dropback EPA allowed and the 10th-ranked defense in the league in terms of success rate allowed. Despite ranking 20th in rushing success rate allowed, the 49ers rank first in rush EPA. With no clear path to running the football successfully, this game falls into the hands of CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, and even KaVontae Turpin. With Pickens cleared to go, the Cowboys will be at full strength on offense for the first time in a few weeks, minus Jake Ferguson. On the other side of the field, the 49ers secondary is quite banged up. Starting cornerbacks Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green are questionable for the game, after both logging limited practices on Friday, after both being DNP’s on Wednesday and Thursday. Starting nickel Upton Stout is also questionable for the game after practicing in limited fashion all week. The 49ers are pretty thin from a depth perspective in the secondary if even one of their starting corners are unable to go, but if they end up missing multiple players, the Cowboys wide receivers should be able to dominate this matchup. Even if all three guys suit up, the Cowboys wide receivers can find plenty of wins against this unit. After sitting out last week, Pickens holds no injury destination heading into the game and seems to be near full strength for the first time in over a month. With Pickens back in the lineup and Turpin expected to return, the Cowboys should have their full complement of weapons to attack a banged up secondary of the 49ers. If the Cowboys want to upset the NFC favorites in Week 10, they will need all four of their starting receivers to impact the game in a big way, making this the key matchup to watch on Sunday.

title: College football draft targets for the Cowboys: Week 11
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are still chasing their playoff dream this season, although it is going to be tough to get there. While that is going on, there is no reason not to take a quick peek ahead to the 2027 draft. Here are some players that might be of interest. USC vs. Indiana Indiana returns […]
full_text: Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are still chasing their playoff dream this season, although it is going to be tough to get there. While that is going on, there is no reason not to take a quick peek ahead to the 2027 draft. Here are some players that might be of interest. USC vs. Indiana Indiana returns from its bye needing a win to remain in the playoff race, while USC arrives with one of the most talented passing attacks in the Big Ten. The Trojans have two receivers capable of stretching the field and a quarterback whose draft stock continues to rise. That puts Indiana cornerback Jamari Sharpe under the spotlight. On the other side, USC defensive end Kameryn Crawford must create pressure against a Hoosiers line that has protected its quarterback well for much of the season. Indiana: Jamari Sharpe, cornerback Sharpe is a clean outside cornerback who has become one of the leaders of Indiana’s defense. He enters the game with 25 tackles, seven passes defended and an interception this season. He’s consistent and has the talent to keep up on a defense that asks its secondary to understand route combinations and keep the ball in front of it. His best work comes in zone coverage. Sharpe reads the quarterback and recognizes routes developing around him. He also understands when to pass one receiver to a teammate before closing on another. His length helps him challenge the throwing window, while his closing speed allows him to break on the ball without giving every short completion room to become a larger gain. Why The Cowboys Care We live in a world where cornerback is a top draft priority. DaRon Bland has yet to regain the form that made him a valuable starter. Shavon Revel is still trying to build his career. The Cowboys cannot enter another season relying on everything to break correctly for a thin group, and that includes the addition of Joey Porter Jr. Sharpe would give Dallas size, experience and ball awareness on the outside. His comfort in zone coverage would help him contribute early while the coaching staff develops his man technique. He also plays with the physical mindset required to support the run and attack the football, which creates value beyond simply staying close to a receiver. USC: Kameryn Crawford, defensive end Crawford brings the frame teams search for at defensive end. The 6-foot-5, 255-pound junior has long arms and an explosive first step. He can rush from a two-point stance or place his hand on the ground. He has recorded 29 tackles, two sacks and seven quarterback hits this season after producing 5.5 sacks and 10.5 tackles for loss in 2025. His burst creates the initial problem. Crawford can gain ground quickly and threaten the tackle’s outside shoulder. Once the tackle opens the corner, Crawford has the length to keep himself clean and enough flexibility to flatten toward the quarterback. He can also convert speed into power when he builds momentum, driving through a blocker who sets too softly. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas still needs young pass rushers who can grow into larger roles. The defense has produced better pressure in recent weeks, but its long-term edge rotation remains uncertain. Malachi Lawrence has offered useful snaps and Donovan Ezeiruaku is still trying to break through; neither removes the need to keep adding talent at a premium position. Texas vs. LSU Texas heads to Death Valley with major questions along its offensive line. Starting left tackle Trevor Goosby is out for the season, increasing the importance of right tackle Melvin Siani. LSU counters with Princewill Umanmielen, who ranks among the most disruptive edge defenders in the country. LSU can move Umanmielen around the formation, but his opportunities against Siani should provide some of the most useful draft tape for his evaluation. Texas: Melvin Siani, right tackle Siani is a very tall and well built senior who has started all nine games for Texas, including seven at right tackle. He previously started at left tackle for Wake Forest and played on both sides at Temple, giving him more positional experience than most tackles in this class. His movement ability stands out for a player of his size. Siani gains depth quickly in his pass set and mirrors changes of direction. He has enough range to reach defenders in space. In the running game, he is at his best when Texas allows him to move. Why The Cowboys Care Terence Steele’s contract and uneven play make his future at Dallas very sketchy next year, while Tyler Guyton gives fans and coaches optimism that the left tackle position could be resolved. The Cowboys need a player capable of competing on the right side and covering both positions when injuries strike. Siani’s experience at left and right tackle gives him a clear route onto the roster. He could begin as the swing tackle and provide competition for Steele’s position to help coaches evaluate whether it’s time to move on. His ability to move in the running game would also suit the offense. LSU: Princewill Umanmielen, defensive end Umanmielen has become one of the breakout defenders of the 2026 season. He’s recorded 35 tackles, 12 tackles for loss and 8.5 sacks, adding 13 quarterback hits. He has produced at least half a sack in six games and entered November among the national leaders in both sacks and tackles for loss. His athleticism drives the pass rush. Umanmielen accelerates quickly from a wide alignment and has the change of direction to finish when the quarterback steps away from the original pressure. He also uses his hands well enough to avoid being carried beyond the pocket. Why The Cowboys Care Umanmielen fits the Cowboys’ need for a pass rusher who can contribute quickly without requiring a first-round selection. His burst would give Parker a threat from wide alignments, and his experience standing up or playing with a hand down would allow Dallas to move him through different fronts. He would not need to become a full-time run defender immediately. The Cowboys could use him in the rotation and let him attack on third down while he adds strength. That role would give the defense more speed off the edge and reduce its dependence on manufactured pressure.

title: What the numbers say about a winner in Cowboys vs 49ers
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys take on the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. Cowboys key stats from last week […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys take on the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards, two touchdowns and finished with a passer rating of 114.2 . He finished the game with a four-play, 65-yard game winning touchdown drive in just 29 seconds. CeeDee Lamb led the team with another massive performance through the air. He racked up an astonishing 195 receiving yards and one touchdown, also fumbling once on an odd play. Javonte Williams and Tyler Goodson finished with a combined 32 carries and 178 yards on the ground. Despite these incredible numbers, the Cowboys offense failed to convert yards into points throughout the day. Held back by turnovers and penalties, it took a fantastic one-handed catch from Ryan Flournoy in the waning moments of the game to sneak out of Indianapolis with a win. DAK PRESCOTT LET IT FLY RYAN FLOURNOY ONE-HANDED CATCH (via: @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/FnxrSX3qbx — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) November 8, 2026 49ers key stats from last week Brock Purdy and the 49ers finished last week with 232 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, and one interception. Purdy also rushed for 40 yards and converted a touchdown with his legs. Kaelon Black outrushed Christian McCaffrey on seven less rushing attempts, finishing with 70 yards. McCaffrey remains this biggest threat, however, finishing with 87 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. The 49ers defense limited Las Vegas to just 24 rushing yards on their way to a 38-17 rout of the Silver and Black. They forced three interceptions, including one pick-six. The formula for San Francisco remains the same after all these years – play efficient offense and let the physical defense swing the game. Call an aggressively smart game The Cowboys are going to have to put up points. San Francisco just has too many weapons offensively, especially in the backfield, for this defense to shut them down for 60 minutes. It’s extremely unlikely this turns into a defensive fist fight. With that in mind, this should be the proper week to bust out the gutsy calls. 4th and inches at your own 40? Sounds like a QB sneak to me. Dallas can choose to kick a 57-yard field goal or they can go for it on 4th and 2. This is one time where it’s ok to skip leg day. Send out the offense and attack. Brian Schottenheimer needs to understand what’s at stake here. Nobody expects the Cowboys to win, but a win has the potential to turn this entire season into something meaningful. Call this game like your back is against the wall and your football life is on the line. It’s going to take a gutsy performance from every player and every coach this week if the Cowboys are to stand a chance. What do the numbers mean? The Cowboys are one of the worst rushing defenses in the NFL. The 49ers possess one of the best rushing attacks, utilizing two backs and a scheme where you never know where the ball is going to go. Dallas is also one of the league’s worst third-down defenses while the 49ers convert at a higher rate than almost every team. The 49ers are clearly the better team, especially when looking at their offense against the Cowboys defense. Yet the FanDuel line is only a 4.5 point spread . This tells me that the line setters understand that Dallas has the talent in the building to keep up and win a game against the 49ers. It just takes one week for everything to come together and see an explosion from this Cowboys team. We’ve yet to see it in 2026, however. If Dallas is to stand a chance this week, they’ll need to finally put together a complete performance for the first time this season. They’ll need to play mistake-free football while making the plays on both sides of the ball that they just haven’t done often enough in 2026. And don’t sleep on the special teams performance playing an important role in the field position battle. If the Cowboys put out their best performance on 2026 by playing mistake free football, scoring touchdowns instead of field goals, and winning the turnover differential, I give them a 40-50% chance at winning this game. But from everything we’ve seen, the Cowboys do not play mistake free football. They are unable to consistently get stops on defense, especially against good teams with good rushing attacks. This team has also played several games where the offense has struggled to put points on the board. To top it off, the head coach has made far too many questionable decisions that have directly impacted the results of these games. The Cowboys are the ultimate wild card this week. Put it all together and have a chance to steal a tough win. Play the same brand of football we’ve seen far too often this season, and this could be a multiple score loss. This is the game that determines the team they’ll be the rest of the season.
author: Dyllan Rivers

Cowboys WR George Pickens confident he should play vs. 49ers: ‘You gonna see me’ -Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News George Pickens has been dealing with injuries that kept him out last week. He feels that this Sunday he’ll be back on the field against the 49ers. FRISCO — Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens was playful with reporters after Friday’s practice. Pickens, who missed last week’s game against the Colts with a hamstring injury, was coy when asked about his playing status for Sunday against the 49ers. “You gonna see me out there, you got to turn the TV screen on,” Pickens said. That will have to be utilized quite a bit versus the 49ers. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer referred to some of San Francisco’s offensive pieces like TE George Kittle, RB Christian McCaffrey and FB Kyle Juszczyk less by their positions, but more as “weapons” for the offense, and they’re all threats when going downfield, especially Kittle and McCaffrey. With injuries at safety, rookie DB Caleb Downs will likely play some on top of the defense, but his role in the nickel against players like Kittle and McCaffrey may be even more important in this game as they look to work the middle of the field. title: Broncos have mastered the art of winning close games
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! The Denver Broncos know how to win games. No matter the situation this team is in, the Broncos never lose belief that they’re still in the game. That’s one of the main reasons Denver has set the NFL record for 16 straight wins in one-score games. It’s also why the bye […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos gestures during the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! The Denver Broncos know how to win games. No matter the situation this team is in, the Broncos never lose belief that they’re still in the game. That’s one of the main reasons Denver has set the NFL record for 16 straight wins in one-score games. It’s also why the bye week comes at a great time. The Broncos are eager to use it for the stretch run, but also to give everyone a breather from these heart-racing finishes. As Denver head coach Sean Payton said to the media after the win over the Carolina Panthers in one-score games: “Well, part of it pisses me off because there’s been a few of them that you would say shouldn’t have been one-score games, and then obviously there’s some that are, but they’ve been great. We knew coming in Thursday, we just knew the type of team we were playing. They’ve been doing some really explosive things on offense. They were banged up, certainly, on defense, as we were. “But we’ll take this break, but we still have to be — and it’s not that you’re never satisfied, but we still have some work to do. To your question, I don’t think I have a great answer. I think we had a decent start. We ended up settling for a field goal.” For the Broncos, that confidence you’re never out of a game is a powerful thing. It’s not so much easier for the team, but a belief. As a fan, it never gets easy. “I’ll be honest, it seems like it’s always the same feeling,” Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said to the media after the win over the Panthers. “There’s always a look in the huddle that, like, hey guys, we don’t have a choice right here. We got to go make something out of it. Today, those second-half touchdowns were really, really important. We were down by one there, 14-13, and we needed one and went and scored, missed the two-point, and got another opportunity. Then, (we) went down and got another touchdown. “I thought that was the best part of the game because it showed that we stacked two drives together, two critical moments, and gave our defense some rest on the sideline with those longer drives. Also, a good cushion, and they did just a good job responding and scoring.” Since it keeps happening, is it lucky or good? “Well, when it keeps happening, I think our league is what it is,” Payton said to the media after the win over Carolina. “When those things keep falling your way, that’s not by accident.” At least we get a reprieve for the week. title: Predicting the Denver Broncos record down the stretch
summary: The Denver Broncos reached their bye week with a 7-2 record, which if you had asked most of us before the season we’d would have been overjoyed that they made it through the early season gauntlet with that record. Now comes the ‘easy’ part of their schedule — as easy as easy gets in the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrates a touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams during the fourth quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos reached their bye week with a 7-2 record, which if you had asked most of us before the season we’d would have been overjoyed that they made it through the early season gauntlet with that record. Now comes the ‘easy’ part of their schedule — as easy as easy gets in the NFL anyway. Their remaining schedule is against mostly non-playoff teams with three very important matchups in the final eight games against actual playoff contenders: Week 11: vs. Las Vegas Raiders Week 12: at Pittsburgh Steelers (Black Friday) Week 13: vs. Miami Dolphins Week 14: at New York Jets Week 15: at Las Vegas Raiders Week 16: vs. Buffalo Bills (Christmas Day) Week 17: at New England Patriots Week 18: vs. Los Angeles Chargers Let’s predict every game and see where things land. For me, I think they have to beat the non-playoff teams. So beating the Raiders twice, Dolphins, Jets, and Chargers. That gets them 12 wins on the season. For the final three against playoff teams, I think it could go one of two ways. Either they beat the Steelers or they lose and then they split games against the Bills and Patriots. So either 2-1 or 1-2. I mean looking at it either way, that is yet another possible 14-win season. Hard to imagine given some of the struggles they’ve had early, but they also played some of the best defensive teams in the NFL to start the season. Bo Nix and the offense should have a much easier time on drives moving forward. That is all ‘what if’ subjective. Let me give my final and official prediction for each game: Week 11: vs. Las Vegas Raiders [8-2] Week 12: at Pittsburgh Steelers (Black Friday) [9-2] Week 13: vs. Miami Dolphins [10-2] Week 14: at New York Jets [11-2] Week 15: at Las Vegas Raiders [12-2] Week 16: vs. Buffalo Bills (Christmas Day) [12-3] Week 17: at New England Patriots [13-3] Week 18: vs. Los Angeles Chargers [14-3] Denver will have their 10-game win streak snapped by Josh Allen, but they’ll bounce back and finish strong. I’m not too worried about Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers. He is a statue back there and Denver’s defense is leading the NFL in pressure rate. What say you? Copy pasta the remaining schedule in the comments and let us know how you think the final eight games plays out.

title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 11 of NCAA Football Season
summary: Welcome back to another installment of Future Broncos. Last week, I focused on a trio of defenders for Broncos Country to keep their eye on as the rest of the collegiate football season transpires. This week, I’ll switch gears and offer three players on offense since that side of the ball has been Denver’s biggest […]
full_text: CHAPEL HILL, NC - OCTOBER 03: Anthonie Knapp (54) of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish comes to the sideline after suffering a bloody nose during the college football game against the North Carolina Tar Heels on October 03, 2026 at Kenan Memorial Stadium in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome back to another installment of Future Broncos . Last week , I focused on a trio of defenders for Broncos Country to keep their eye on as the rest of the collegiate football season transpires. This week, I’ll switch gears and offer three players on offense since that side of the ball has been Denver’s biggest issue in 2026. Earnest Green III — Offensive Tackle — Georgia So far this season, I’ve offered my thoughts on a handful of offensive line prospects. Mizzou’s Cayden Green, Indiana’s Carter Smith, Minnesota’s Greg Johnson, and USC’s Elijah Paige. Based on the comments section, identifying more big guys in the offensive trenches is something you are all interested in. Georgia fifth-year senior Earnest Green III has been on my radar for a while. Back in 2023, he was a fourteen-game starter for the Bulldogs at left tackle protecting future top pick Carson Beck. He continued to man down that position for nine games in 2024, but a lingering shoulder issue cost him a few games and slowed the promise he showed as a freshman. Last season, Greene (6’4″, 320 pounds) flipped to right tackle while Monroe Freeling was manning the blindside. However, he started just nine games due to lingering back issues. Though he didn’t give up a sack in the over 800 offensive snaps he played in 2005. Now healthy, Greene is back home where it all started on the left side of Georgia’s stalwart offensive line. The redshirt senior is poised to finish his collegiate career with over 40 starts and over 3,000 snaps between both tackle positions and having three different line coaches. That experience will pay off and mean a lot to NFL scouts and general managers who value experience and top-notch SEC pedigrees. I’m a big fan of the depth he gets in his pass sets. I also like his ability to anchor and hold his own against strong power rushers. Moreover, I am impressed with his ability to get up field and take on blockers at the second level. It’ll be interesting to see how he measures [arm length] during the pre-draft circuit. There are some who believe his best football is inside at guard, but I think he can stick at tackle. Last week’s performance versus Ole Miss earned him the Outland Trophy Player of the Week honors. To date, Greene has only given up four quarterback pressures on the season. The Broncos could use a tough and battle-tested player in their trenches next April, and I believe Greene (if medicals check out) has a shot at being a Day 2 selection. You can catch him in action this afternoon on ABC when the top-ranked Bulldogs host Mizzou. Anthonie Knapp — Offensive Lineman — Notre Dame For most of my Future Broncos installments, I’ve tried to focus on seniors whether it be fourth or fifth-year players. One particular reason is that NIL money has changed the NFL Draft landscape. Early declarations are basically half of what they used to be. In turn, that makes it a lot harder to find quality players to address needs. However, a potential early round pick that may wind up declaring early if he keeps playing well is Notre Dame offensive lineman Anthonie Knapp. He manned down the left tackle position for the Fighting Irish for the first 27 games of his collegiate career. For his third season, the junior has kicked inside to guard. That’s where many analysts have stated his best NFL potential might be. However, there are a handful of others who think a further kick inside to the pivot may be where he blossoms. Regardless, his versatility will be a big enhancer for his draft stock if he chooses to declare. We all know Head Coach Sean Payton values experience and versatility when it comes to offensive lineman. This Golden Domer certainly fits the bill. By the end of this season, Knapp (6’5”, 305 pounds) will have logged well over 2,000 snaps and have three full seasons of starting experience. While he could stand to put on some weight and muscle to handle the rigors of the pro game, his anchor is incredibly strong at this stage. In my opinion, he plays with NFL ready technique at the line of scrimmage. He has been an enforcer in the run game and a key reason for Notre Dame’s success on the ground this season. As a pass protector, Knapp has been credited with giving up just one sack in nearly three dozen starts. Whether or not Knapp chooses to declare remains to be seen but given Denver’s long-term needs at multiple positions on the offensive line, he would be a quality prospect for them to consider. I believe he has a legitimate shot to be a Top 50 player easily if he decides to take his talents to the NFL. You can watch him in action when the third-ranked Fighting Irish host Boston College this afternoon. DJ Vonnahme — Tight End — Iowa Thus far in our Future Broncos installments, we have highlighted just two tight ends in the 2027 NFL Draft. Underclassmen Oregon’s Jamari Johnson and Virginia Tech’s Luke Reynolds. I have a strong feeling both of them will declare and will merit early consideration by NFL teams looking to upgrade the position. This collegiate season, another underclassman from Iowa is making quite the statement this season—DJ Vonnahme. Over the years, the Hawkeyes have been a tight end producing factory under Kirk Ferentz. Players like George Kittle, Noah Fant, T.J. Hockensen, and Sam LaPorta all come to mind. Vonnahme (6’4”, 241 pounds) appears to be next to follow in their footsteps. Appearing in twelve games as a redshirt freshman in 2025, Vonnahme logged five starts and was the Hawkeyes’ leading receiver with 29 catches, 434 yards, and 3 touchdowns. He popped onto the map of scouts last season with a dominant seven catch, 146-yard performance against Vanderbilt in last year’s ReliaQuest Bowl . In eight games in 2026, Vonnahme sports 32 receptions for 314 yards and 3 touchdowns as well as one rushing touchdown. His yards per route ran (2.59) is amongst the highest in the nation. He has one of the best contested catch rates in the nation and can work multiple levels of the field. While there is no doubting his upside and talent as a receiving threat at the next level, Vonnahme’s work as a blocker leaves a lot to be desired. It’s important to note he is only 20 years old and is a former quarterback that is still learning the nuances of the position. Getting better at blocking is something he can certainly get better at with more time. Vonnahme is just a redshirt sophomore. With that in mind, a return back to Iowa seems quite likely. Though with this year’s class not having a clear-cut number one just yet, perhaps he goes pro if he gets good enough feedback in the pre-draft process. You can catch him in tonight when the sixteenth ranked Hawkeyes host Purdue tomorrow evening on NBC.

title: Best player prop bets for New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions, Week 10
summary: Whether it’s morning, afternoon, or evening, there’s always time to watch your Detroit Lions! This week, they head to Munich, Germany, to play the New England Patriots in a rare above-.500 battle across the pond. Since it’s an early kickoff, it’s best to get your bets in sooner rather than later, because if you don’t […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions in action against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Whether it’s morning, afternoon, or evening, there’s always time to watch your Detroit Lions! This week, they head to Munich, Germany, to play the New England Patriots in a rare above-.500 battle across the pond. Since it’s an early kickoff, it’s best to get your bets in sooner rather than later, because if you don’t have your morning coffee, you could end up placing the wrong bet! Last week was a losing week, as the Lions’ defense did their part, but the offense struggled more than I expected. Now two games below .500, we need a perfect 3/3 week to get back above, or at least two out of the three to get back to even. Here are three wagers to watch in this matchup. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook . 1. Jared Goff Over 268.5 passing yards (-112) Lions quarterback Jared Goff is having a solid season so far, and despite a quiet game against the Miami Dolphins last week, I think he will rebound well against New England. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love just threw for 372 yards against the Patriots, the most they’ve allowed this season. That was at home for New England too; now they are on the road and without their top cornerback, Carlton Davis III. Goff will want to rebound after being held without a passing touchdown for the first time this season last week. With his star wide receiver, Amon-Ra St. Brown, also having ties to Germany, he will do his best to get him a touchdown in front of his home crowd. Goff has thrown for over 268 yards in five games this season, and with New England allowing an average of 231.9 yards per game, going above that by only 37 seems doable with the weapons he has. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85 2. Jameson Williams Alt receiving yards 50+ (-158) Piggybacking off the first point with Goff, I think this secondary, without its No. 2 corner Davis, will have its hands full with wide receivers St. Brown and Jameson Williams. The Packers’ top two receivers got over 100 yards each in last week’s win, and each also had at least one catch over 40 yards. Williams is a big-play receiver; he can do that on one play, too. His speed will be tough to contain, and even on short to intermediate routes, he can turn a three-yard catch or a 10-yard snag into something more. St. Brown will probably receive the most attention, which gives Williams a chance to break out and take advantage of the lackluster secondary. Williams has only gotten this line in three games this season, and he could’ve had it last week if he didn’t drop a catch. Where Goff can find Williams is in play-action. Goff can have the offense believe it’s a run and suddenly, Williams is downfield wide open. When it comes to play action, New England is in for a world of trouble. Patriots are the 31st ranked defense vs under center (+0.11 EPA/P). Worst vs early down play action (+0.46 EPA/DB) They face Goff and the Lions in Germany — Football Insights 📊 (@fball_insights) November 12, 2026 Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $16.33 3. Amon-Ra St. Brown anytime touchdown (-130) As I mentioned earlier, St. Brown has German ties and will want to show out for the “home” crowd. When reporters asked him Friday if he already had a touchdown celebration in mind because of the circumstances, he said: “I don’t have it planned yet, I still have two days to figure that out. You know, I haven’t been in the endzone in some weeks so I feel like Germany would be a great time to touch the paint again.” St. Brown is in a bit of a rut when it comes to finding the end zone, as he hasn’t scored since Week 3. Five straight games without a touchdown is the longest he’s gone without one since the end of the 2022 season, when he didn’t score in the last five games. He also had seven straight games without a touchdown that season. This bet is strictly vibes-based and can sometimes be a bust, but I think the stars are aligning too much for you not to think the Lions and Goff won’t have plays drawn up for him to score. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $17.69 If you want to turn these three single bets into a same-game parlay, the odds are +286 and $10 -> $38.66 Record: 11-13 Brandon’s Bold Bet If you want to go bold and build a big parlay that could pay well, put these three bets together in a parlay: Jahmyr Gibbs 4+ receptions (-210) St. Brown over 7.5 receptions (+102) Jared Goff 3+ touchdowns (+225) For this week’s bold bets, I am including running back Jahmyr Gibbs, but not for his ground game. The Patriots are averaging at least three passes per game to their running backs, and with the running game possibly limited, Detroit could use Gibbs more as a receiver this week to find success. Gibbs is averaging four catches a game, and he was held to none against Miami and only two against the Minnesota Vikings. I think he gets back on track this week with at least four. Speaking of the receiving game, St. Brown won’t just find the end zone on Sunday; I think he will be a go-to option for Goff, which won’t be surprising. St. Brown is averaging 7.6 catches a game this season, so I think he can hit eight. St. Brown will want to put on as much of a show as he can in Germany, so he seems like the best guy to lean on this week. Finally, my boldest pick this week is Goff to throw for at least three passing touchdowns. Goff has done this in only two games this season, but I think it’ll be a high-scoring affair in Munich. Detroit may have to lean on the passing game and Goff, giving him a chance to score multiple times. New England is averaging 1.5 passing touchdowns a game and just allowed three passing touchdowns to Green Bay. Goff has a chance to rebound after last week’s dud and show the world he’s an MVP candidate. Whatever we did, it’s not indicative of our work ethic or complacency or our process. title: Lions vs. Patriots 5 Qs preview: Can Drake Maye clean up turnovers against Detroit in Germany?
summary: For their first game in 11 days, the Detroit Lions take their show on the road across the Atlantic for an international Week 10 showdown in Munich, Germany, facing off against the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots. We had the pleasure of connecting with Taylor Kyles, a staff writer for Pats Pulpit, to give […]
full_text: Nov 13, 2026; Munich, Germany; An advertisement for the 2026 NFL Munich Game with images of New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (0) and Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (14) at the Zaitoon Market. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For their first game in 11 days, the Detroit Lions take their show on the road across the Atlantic for an international Week 10 showdown in Munich, Germany, facing off against the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots. We had the pleasure of connecting with Taylor Kyles, a staff writer for Pats Pulpit, to give us some insight into this New England squad ahead of Sunday morning’s tilt. We learned about the growing concern surrounding Drake Maye’s turnover regression, how injuries have decimated New England’s offensive line, and the coverage busts plaguing an otherwise physical defense—plus how Detroit’s offensive weapons could exploit the Patriots’ secondary in Munich: 1. The Patriots have had a bit of a Jekyll and Hyde season through nine games. It looked like they were hitting their stride after beating the Bills, Raiders, and Jets, but since then, they’ve dropped two of their last three games. As the defending AFC Champions, what’s most concerning about this uneven start to 2026? What’s there to be encouraged by in their first half of 2026? The most discouraging thing has been their inconsistency against upper-echelon teams outside of their division. The defense looks great against mid-tier passing attacks, but some of their schematic quirks (not using as much press and man as expected for their personnel, heavy use of disguises, spinning the dial with coverages) have been exposed against the league’s best passers. Drake Maye also regressed to his turnover-prone ways last week after over a month of clean football and MVP-caliber play. On a positive note, Maye looked good outside of his interceptions last week while fighting for his life against the Packers’ pressure packages, so cutting back on poor decisions and throws should allow him to return to his more recent form. Defensively, they have the players to perform better than what we’ve seen, but I think the coaching staff needs to do a better job putting players in better positions to succeed and potentially simplifying things so players can do what they do best. 2. Drake Maye was six voting points away from being the league’s MVP a season ago, throwing 31 touchdowns to just 8 interceptions. 2026 has seen some pretty volatile play from Maye on a week-to-week basis, leading to him already surpassing his turnover total from a year ago through nine games. Do you see Maye regressing from a decision-making standpoint, or is his 2026 season a victim of circumstances beyond his control? A relatively lackluster supporting cast and a banged-up offensive line have made life difficult for Maye. A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs haven’t lived up to expectations when on the field, and blockers Mike Onwenu, Alijah Vera-Tucker, and Reggie Gilliam are all currently on injured reserve. That said, most of Maye’s turnovers resulted from avoidable mistakes, such as forced attempts and throwing the wrong kind of pass for the situation. Maye winning Offensive Player of the Month in October showed he can rise above these issues, but we have yet to see him do it for a truly extended stretch. 3. Injuries have plagued the Patriots all season long. Where do you feel the effects of injuries are hurting this team the most? Who are some players that have made the most out of their newfound opportunities? Injuries have most profoundly impacted the offensive line. The ground game has been limited due to the loss of both starting guards, forcing the Patriots into being a fairly straightforward downhill rushing attack. Josh McDaniel has tried incorporating different looks and wrinkles, but outside zone hasn’t really been an option with so little chemistry up front. Pass protection held up surprisingly well for a bit, but schemed pressures like blitzes and stunts have become increasingly problematic over the past three weeks, resulting in far too many unblocked pressures. There is hope things will settle down if veteran Greg Van Roten returns from IR, but he’s missed significant time and is one of the oldest players on the team, so how he performs down the stretch is anyone’s guess. Matt Pryor has emerged as a relative bright spot beside Morgan Moses, who’s been dealing with a foot injury for weeks, but the big-bodied guard can be exposed if forced to quickly redirect. 4. New England’s defense is a super interesting read from a statistical perspective. They have one of the most effective pass rushes in the NFL, and their run defense is a top-10 unit at minimum, yet they’re average as a whole unit by DVOA (15th) and below average in EPA/play (23rd). When the Patriots defense is at its best, what are they doing successfully? Where are New England’s weaknesses on this side of the ball? Are there certain positional matchups, or player archetypes they struggle in defending? Physicality and discipline stand out most when the Patriots are playing at their best. It’s a veteran group that plays with a lot of pride and attitude, and that translates into players swarming to the football and laying the wood when given the opportunity. Unfortunately, communication lapses and issues against tempo have led to coverage busts and big plays for opposing offenses. The defense has also struggled to take the ball away this season, which has made life tougher for both sides of the ball. This week, I’m worried about their ability to defend Jahmyr Gibbs out of the backfield. New England has yet to face an opponent that truly fed a talented receiving back through the air, but I’m not sure the defense has the linebacker or safety depth to keep Gibbs quiet if Detroit presses the issue. Jameson Williams could also have himself a day if the secondary doesn’t actively disrupt his releases and route stems. 5. The Patriots opened as 2.5-point home underdogs at FanDuel Sportsbook heading into this international matchup against the Lions. What’s one thing you want to see, what’s one thing you need to see, and one thing you’re sure you’ll see happen in this matchup between the Lions and Patriots on Sunday morning our time? I’d like to see Drake Maye play a clean game and go toe-to-toe with Jared Goff. He had the talent to do so and elevate his supporting cast, but it will ultimately come down to picking his spots and avoiding bad decisions. I need to see a more competitive effort from the defense, particularly in the red area. This feels like a bend-but-don’t-break kind of game, so holding the Lions to field goals will be crucial. Finally, I’m sure I’ll see the Lions move the ball effectively. There are simply too many weapons for the Patriots to defend consistently, particularly without Carlton Davis. Goff will take what the defense gives him and hit a handful of shots, but again, the Patriots must be competitive once the Lions reach the red area.

title: New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions preview: 6 key stats
summary: Holy scheiße! The Detroit Lions’ first overseas game in over a decade, dating back to the early Jim Caldwell era, is finally here, and the Motor City militia is ready to make some noise in Munich, Germany. While it’s still one of the more compelling European games this season, the buildup is different than expected. […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - OCTOBER 09: Detroit Lions running back Jamaal Williams (30) blocks New England Patriots safety Adrian Phillips (21) as Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) prepares to throw a pass during a NFL game between Detroit Lions and New England Patriots on October 9, 2022, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, MA. (Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Holy scheiße! The Detroit Lions’ first overseas game in over a decade, dating back to the early Jim Caldwell era, is finally here, and the Motor City militia is ready to make some noise in Munich, Germany. While it’s still one of the more compelling European games this season, the buildup is different than expected. The Lions are coming off an emotional week that ended in a low-scoring affair in Miami, while the Patriots were bombarded by Green Bay at home. New England’s season has had its ups and downs, highlighted by a road win in Buffalo, but the team hasn’t found its mojo since the Super Bowl, aside from its head coach this offseason. Interestingly, the game pits two tough-minded, former-player, CEO-type head coaches against each other. The Lions are looking to extend their four-game winning streak, thanks in large part to their defensive improvements, with their sights set on containing reigning MVP runner-up Drake Maye. They’ll also hope for a much better offensive performance than last time they faced the Patriots, when Bailey Zappe was the quarterback on the other side of the ball, and they got skunked. So tap the keg and crack a few eggs, as this week’s preview will examine six key stats and matchups Detroit needs to handle to keep the winning streak train on the tracks and let you enjoy your Sunday morning kickoff. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus. Pop Goes The Weasel The Patriots’ offense heads to Germany with a bit of a MASH unit, as they’ll be down to backup offensive guards Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor. Sending my best regards to those two as they face Alim McNeill and Tyleik Williams. They’ll also be without skill-position players Romeo Doubs and TreVeyon Henderson, while A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson (161 rushing yards vs. the Lions in 2021) are questionable. Lions fans know not to take a team lightly, even one ravaged by injuries; they only need to look back at Carolina scoring 32 points against them while missing numerous key offensive pieces. Detroit’s defense will still need to shut down the areas opposing offenses plan to attack. Following Maye’s early-season struggles, which included a 58.6 passer rating, six interceptions, and nine sacks in the first three weeks, he has leaned into fourth-year slot receiver DeMario “Pop” Douglas, despite injuries to Brown and Doubs. Since Week 5, Douglas has recorded 22 receptions for 352 receiving yards and four receiving touchdowns. His receiving yards rank 11th among all players, just two yards fewer than Amon-Ra St. Brown in that span, while his four touchdowns are tied for third. Douglas is a career 11-yards-per-reception player, but he’s averaging 16 yards per reception over that stretch. Douglas has spent a league-leading 81.3% of his snaps in the slot during that span, with the next-closest player at just 72.5%. His 11 receiving first downs from the slot also lead the league over that stretch. Stopping Douglas will be no easy task for the Lions’ improving defense, as Detroit allows a league-worst +0.59 EPA/pass on targets to the slot. The Lions have faced 101 slot targets (2nd), allowing 8.7 yards/pass (24th), a 10.7-yard average depth of target (30th), seven passing touchdowns (t-28th), and a 60.2% passing success rate on throws to the slot. They’ve also allowed the second-fastest average time to throw on those passes at just 2.45 seconds, nullifying much of the disruption that Aidan Hutchinson, McNeill, and any blitzes can generate. Stopping Pop Douglas will require a dedicated effort in Kelvin Sheppard’s game plan, with Roger McCreary likely seeing plenty of time trying to burst his bubble, along with help from the linebackers and safeties. Perhaps Brian Branch will see some dedicated time against the small, shifty, but explosive Douglas. If the Lions can keep Pop bottled up in Munich, they’ll go a long way toward cutting off the Patriots’ offensive tap. The Munich Meat Grinder The last time the Patriots and Lions faced off, early in Dan Campbell’s second season and potentially a low point of his coaching tenure in Detroit before the team grabbed the rope and started climbing, Rhamondre Stevenson was a problem, particularly running up the middle. He recorded 11 carries for 86 rushing yards (7.8 yards per carry), including a startling 7.8 yards before contact per carry. However, things might be a little different this time around. Whether it’s Stevenson or the more diminutive Corey Kiner attempting to run up the middle against the Lions’ defense, with the aforementioned McNeill and Williams, especially without beefy guards Mike Onwenu and Alijah Vera-Tucker, they might get pounded into schnitzel. Since Week 5, the Detroit Lions’ defense has allowed a league-best 23.3% rushing success rate on runs up the middle. That also includes just three first downs and zero rushing touchdowns allowed on 30 rushing attempts up the middle. Much like airplanes in America, they’re grounding rushing attacks up the middle. The Patriots’ offense prefers to run up the gut, with the third-most such carries (96) this season. However, they rank outside the top 10 in yards per rushing attempt (4.1) and just 19th in both EPA/rush (-0.093) and rushing success rate (39.6%). While they rely heavily on running between the tackles, they haven’t been overly successful. If the Lions can close down the Autobahn up the middle, they’ll force Maye to take the scenic route on third down, where Detroit’s pass rush will be waiting. The Bavarian Bootleg Often, when the Patriots run up the middle, they operate from under center, and their 41.5% under-center rate ranks 12th in the league. However, they struggle when Maye is crouched behind second-year pivot Jared Wilson, ranking 27th in the NFL with -0.173 EPA/play from under center. It doesn’t get much better when they use play-action from under center, either. This season, the Patriots’ under-center play-action passing metrics have been a little startling, as they’re averaging -0.359 EPA/dropback (30th), a 12.7% turnover rate (32nd), a 61.2% completion percentage (22nd), and a 43.6% pressure rate (20th) — despite allowing only one sack. Longtime offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels hasn’t been able to help unlock Drake Maye and the under-center play-action passing attack, and that’s music to Lions fans’ ears as Detroit continues to adjust to a linebacker corps of Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez (possibly getting more Mike linebacker reps), and Trevor Nowaske, while also acclimating Brian Branch and newly acquired Andre Cisco into the equation. One of those Lions defenders coming up with a turnover, given that Maye has been handing out footballs like beer steins at Oktoberfest with seven turnovers on just 55 under-center play-action dropbacks, would be a welcome gift for Detroit’s overseas success. Maye-day Parade Where the Patriots’ offense has been buttering its bread, err, putting the bratwurst in its bun, has been from shotgun, particularly with 11-personnel. Whether it’s operating from the ‘gun and airing it out to the likes of DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism II, Mack Hollins, and Hunter Henry, or Eli Raridon, Maye has been in an aggressive zone. From shotgun in 11-personnel, the Patriots’ passing offense has averaged +0.176 EPA/dropback (4th), a 46.7% passing success rate (8th), 8.81 yards per attempt (2nd), an 11.66-yard average depth of target (1st), and a 12.5% explosive pass rate (4th). They’ve also managed to manufacture plenty of…

A former third-round pick of the Arizona Cardinals in […]
full_text: GLENDALE, AZ - SEPTEMBER 25: Owen Pappoe #44 of the Arizona Cardinals celebrates during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at State Farm Stadium on September 25, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions announced they have elevated practice squad linebacker Owen Pappoe for Week 10 against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Pappoe signed to the Lions’ practice squad just 10 days ago, after Jimmy Rolder (and eventually Jack Campbell) were placed on injured reserve. A former third-round pick of the Arizona Cardinals in 2023, Pappoe has made a career out of primarily playing special teams (49 games), but does have some experience on the defensive side of the ball as well. A highly athletic linebacker with 4.39-second speed, Pappoe can contribute in all five phases of special teams and act as an emergency option at WILL linebacker. It’s not unusual for the Lions to roster seven linebackers on game day, given how much they value special teams, and this elevation likely reflects his quick acclimation to the Lions system and ability to contribute this Sunday. That said, with running backs Sione Vaki (ankle, questionable) and Jacob Saylors (neck, not listed with a designation) dealing with injuries, and Vaki’s increased usage on offense, the Lions could certainly use a player like Pappoe to help fill gaps on special teams. We will have to wait until inactives are announced ahead of the game for more details. Of note, with the Lions vs. Patriots game starting at 9:30 a.m. ET, inactives will be announced at 8 a.m. ET.

full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers throws a pass during the first half of a game against the Minnesota Vikings of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re somehow already in Week 10 of the NFL season, and it kicked off with a surprisingly thrilling game between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants on Thursday night. But there are plenty more fireworks ahead in a pretty good slate of games this week. Of course, things kick off in Germany with a huge showdown between the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots . But don’t sleep on some big contests in each time window for Sunday. Lions fans will be particularly interested in the 1 p.m. ET showdown between the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers, but Kansas City Chiefs vs. Atlanta Falcons could be a low-key banger. The late afternoon window features all four NFC West teams—all relevant to the Lions’ playoff chase: Seahawks vs. Raiders, Rams vs. Cardinals, and 49ers vs. Cowboys. title: Packers make 5 roster moves, don’t place Josh Jacobs on IR
summary: The Green Bay Packers, as expected, had to make a couple of roster moves on Saturday to piece together a 48-man game-day roster for Sunday. Today, the Packers announced the activations of running back Chris Brooks and receiver Skyy Moore from the injured reserve. To make room for those additions on the 53-man active roster, […]
full_text: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers, as expected , had to make a couple of roster moves on Saturday to piece together a 48-man game-day roster for Sunday. Today, the Packers announced the activations of running back Chris Brooks and receiver Skyy Moore from the injured reserve. To make room for those additions on the 53-man active roster, Green Bay placed tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) on the injured reserve and released receiver Coleman Owen. On top of these moves, the Packers also elevated tight end Drake Dabney from the practice squad for a second consecutive week. Brooks gives Green Bay five running backs on their 53-man roster at the moment, as Josh Jacobs, who had surgery on his broken finger on Saturday, was not placed on the injured reserve. Jacobs will miss Sunday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings, meaning the Packers are likely to carry three of their four healthy running backs — Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson — into tomorrow’s action. Moore is a slot receiver and a returner, the latter being a role that Owen filled while Moore was on the IR. Moore took over as the Packers’ starting slot receiver once Jayden Reed had his season-ending neck injury. Moore was later replaced by Savion Williams. It will be interesting to see if Moore takes over in the slot this week or if Williams will continue in that spot. Below is the full breakdown of the Packers’ 54 roster options going into Week 10: QB – 2: Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor RB – 5: Josh Jacobs, Chris Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson WR – 6: Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Skyy Moore, Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant TE – 4: Tucker Kraft, Mark Redman, Jonnu Smith and Drake Dabney OL – 11: Jordan Morgan, Aaron Banks, Sean Rhyan, Laken Tomlinson, Anthony Belton, Kevin Zeitler, John Williams, Travis Glover, Mekhi Becton Sr., Jager Burton and Donovan Jennings DL – 5: Karl Brooks, Devonte Wyatt, Chris McClellan, Jordon Riley and Anthony Campbell EDGE – 4: Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr. and Dani-Dennis Sutton LB – 5: Zaire Franklin, Isaiah McDuffie, Ty’Ron Hopper, Nick Niemann and Kristian Welch CB – 5: Keisean Nixon, Brandon Cisse, Carrington Valentine, Benjamin St-Juste and Kamal Hadden S – 4: Xavier McKinney, Evan Williams, Javon Bullard and Kitan Oladapo K – 1: Trey Smack P – 1: Daniel Whelan LS – 1: Matt Orzech Green Bay has already ruled out the following players against Minnesota: RB Josh Jacobs (finger) C Sean Rhyan (ankle) On top of that, linebacker Zaire Franklin is doubtful to play (fractured shin — didn’t practice this week), and these players are questionable: RB Chris Brooks (ankle) S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee) OL Travis Glover (knee) S Xavier McKinney (foot) WR Skyy Moore (ankle) EDGE Lukas Van Ness (back) G Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps) Based on the roster math — post-Jacobs and Rhyan — the team has 52 options to make up their 48-man game-day roster. Two more offensive linemen will be ruled out, as Green Bay generally keeps eight up on the game-day roster. That gets us down to 50. Add Franklin to that, and it’s 49. Scratching whoever is the fourth running back in the pecking order gets us down to the game-day 48. That’s probably the scenario we’re looking at for Sunday. Assuming that the questionable players (outside of potentially the offensive linemen) are going to suit up against the Vikings. If that were not the case, the Packers probably would have used a second practice squad elevation this week.

title: Jalen Pitre hit with 2 fines after Texans beat Chargers in Week 9
summary: Jalen Pitre was hit with not one, but two big fines for his play against the Chargers in Week 9. Pitre owes the league $30,800 for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet on two separate plays. Both plays occurred in the second quarter of the Texans’ 44-22 win over the worst team in the NFL right […]
full_text: Photo by Karl Anderson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jalen Pitre was hit with not one, but two big fines for his play against the Chargers in Week 9. Pitre owes the league $30,800 for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet on two separate plays. Both plays occurred in the second quarter of the Texans’ 44-22 win over the worst team in the NFL right now. On the first, at 8:58, Pitre’s fine for use of the helmet came on a tackle of Chargers WR Tre Harris on third-and-goal for a 7-yard loss. The play forced the Chargers to settle for a field goal. The second play, with :25 left in the first half, was a tackle on Chargers TE Charlie Kolar for a 5-yard game. Pitre was not flagged for either play during the game. Pitre has been fined three previous times in his NFL career for a total of $43,351, and the two fines from Texans vs. Chargers are his first since Jan. 2024. On the Chargers side, cornerback Donte Jackson was fined $12,537 for unnecessary roughness/striking, kicking, or kneeing for a play in the fourth quarter of Texans vs. Chargers, a Woody Marks carry for no gain. Jackson was flagged for the infraction at the time. The NFL divides the money it collects from player discipline and splits it between the NFLPA’s efforts to support retired players, the NFL Foundation, and other nonprofits that support sports leagues, community wellness, and player health and safety initiatives at every level of sports.

title: Colts activate Arden Key from injured reserve, place two veterans on IR
summary: The Indianapolis Colts announced several roster moves Saturday ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, activating defensive end Arden Key from injured reserve, signing linebacker West Weeks to the 53-man roster and placing tight end Mo Alie-Cox and linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither on injured reserve. The return of Key provides some much-needed help […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 20: Arden Key #98 of the Indianapolis Colts before an NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and Kansas City Chiefs on Sep 20, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts announced several roster moves Saturday ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, activating defensive end Arden Key from injured reserve, signing linebacker West Weeks to the 53-man roster and placing tight end Mo Alie-Cox and linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither on injured reserve. Injury Report Update for #MIAvsIND DE Arden Key (Hamstring) has been activated from IR, and the Questionable designation has been lifted for Sunday’s game. TE Will Mallory (Hamstring) has been downgraded to Out. https://t.co/INNIsbj8dY — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 14, 2026 The return of Key provides some much-needed help along Indianapolis’ defensive line, particularly following the recent trade of DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. The 30-year-old defensive end has been sidelined since suffering a hamstring injury during the Colts’ Week 4 victory over the Washington Commanders in London, forcing him to miss the team’s past five games. Before the injury, Key had started all four contests, recording 8 tackles, half a sack and 1 forced fumble. Key returned to practice Wednesday and was a full participant throughout the week, although he was listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report. His activation makes him eligible to return Sunday, potentially strengthening a pass-rushing rotation that has relied heavily on Laiatu Latu, Jaylahn Tuimoloau and Caden Curry. Unfortunately, the Colts also received some disappointing injury news, with Alie-Cox and Davis-Gaither both landing on injured reserve. Alie-Cox has been dealing with a groin injury that prevented him from practicing throughout the week, leaving Indianapolis without one of its most experienced blocking tight ends. His absence should create additional opportunities for Tyler Warren and Drew Ogletree, while Will Mallory’s availability remains uncertain after he appeared on Friday’s injury report with a hamstring issue. Davis-Gaither, meanwhile, has been sidelined by a knee injury and also missed last Sunday’s game against the Dallas Cowboys. His placement on injured reserve further weakens an already thin linebacker group, particularly with Jaylon Carlies also ruled out for Sunday’s contest. Rookie CJ Allen and Bryce Boettcher are expected to handle significant responsibilities, while the promotion of West Weeks provides some additional depth alongside Austin Ajiake. Weeks, an undrafted rookie out of LSU, joined Indianapolis during the offseason and has spent the season developing on the practice squad. His promotion gives the Colts another option at linebacker and on special teams as they attempt to navigate their growing injury concerns. With Indianapolis sitting at 2-7 and having lost five consecutive games, the organization is increasingly focused on evaluating younger talent over the remainder of the season. Key’s return is a welcome development for the defensive line, but the latest injuries create additional challenges for a roster that has already undergone substantial changes in recent weeks.

title: Jaguars Arik Armstead fined for unnecessary roughness vs. Ravens in Week 9
summary: Arik Armstead will be fined $17,911 for a hip-drop tackle in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Baltimore Ravens. The fine for unnecessary roughness stems from a tackle on Derrick Henry on the Ravens’ very first offensive play of the third quarter. The play was a direct snap to Henry, who was stopped after […]
full_text: Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images | Getty Images Arik Armstead will be fined $17,911 for a hip-drop tackle in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Baltimore Ravens. The fine for unnecessary roughness stems from a tackle on Derrick Henry on the Ravens’ very first offensive play of the third quarter. The play was a direct snap to Henry, who was stopped after just 1 yard by Armstead and Matt Dickerson. Armstead was not flagged for the play at the time. The fine is Armstead’s second of the season, after being fined 11,941 for a face mask penalty when the Jaguars played the Patriots back in Week 3 of the 2026 season. Armstead was the only Jaguars or Ravens player who was fined for their Week 9 play. Armstead, who signed with the Jaguars in 2024 after spending the first nine years of his career with the 49ers, has 14 tackles, 1.5 sacks and a pass breakup for the Jags this season. Armstead had two tackles in the Jaguars’ 33-10 victory, including the one he was fined for against the Joe Fagnano-led Ravens in Week 9. The funds the NFL collects through fines are donated to the NFLPA’s assistance to retired players, and the NFL Foundation and other nonprofit organizations that support kids’ sports leagues, community wellness initiatives, and the safety, health and well being of athletes at all levels of sports.

title: Chiefs elevate 2 players from practice squad for Week 10
summary: Before departing for Sunday’s road game against the Atlanta Falcons, the Kansas City Chiefs made a pair of practice squad elevations for the contest. Unsurprisingly, running back Nate Carter received a call up. With star rusher Kenneth Walker being downgraded to out on Saturday because of a late week groin issue, there was little doubt […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 21: Bam Martin-Scott #57 of the Carolina Panthers tackles Nate Carter #38 of the Atlanta Falcons during the third quarter at Bank of America Stadium on September 21, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before departing for Sunday’s road game against the Atlanta Falcons , the Kansas City Chiefs made a pair of practice squad elevations for the contest. We have activated Practice Squad players RB Nate Carter and WR Jacob De Jesus via Standard Elevation. pic.twitter.com/NZlhsB5X1k — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) November 14, 2026 Unsurprisingly, running back Nate Carter received a call up. With star rusher Kenneth Walker being downgraded to out on Saturday because of a late week groin issue, there was little doubt Carter would be made available. Third string running back Jadyn Ott also carries a questionable designation with a hamstring injury. Fittingly, Carter signed with the Falcons in 2025 as an undrafted free agent out of Michigan State. He appeared in seven games with Atlanta last year, recording nine rushes for 60 yards. After being waived in Atlanta’s final roster cuts, Carter signed with Kansas City’s practice squad on September 2. The Chiefs also elevated wide receiver and return man Jacob De Jesus — who was with the team in the preseason as an undrafted free agent out of Cal. After waiving incumbent return man Nikko Remigio on Wednesday, De Jesus may be getting an audition to take over the role. With newly acquired wideout Josh Downs expected to see his first action with the Chiefs on Sunday, having De Jesus as a return man will probably send one of Kansas City’s reserve receivers to the inactive list. Don’t be surprised if one of Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals or Andrew Armstrong is a healthy scratch in Atlanta. As elevated players, Carter and De Jesus will automatically return to the team’s practice squad after the game.

title: Chiefs downgrade Kenneth Walker to out against the Falcons
summary: On Friday morning, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker woke up with a “tight groin,” head coach Andy Reid said at the podium later that day. He was held out of practice for the first time all week due to the sudden injury, and he will now miss the Week 10 game against the […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Friday morning, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker woke up with a “tight groin,” head coach Andy Reid said at the podium later that day. He was held out of practice for the first time all week due to the sudden injury, and he will now miss the Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons . Kenneth Walker (groin) has been downgraded to out for Sunday’s game against the Falcons. Chris Jones (NIR – Personal) will not travel with the team and will arrive on his own to Atlanta. He has no game designation. — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) November 14, 2026 The team downgraded Walker (groin) from questionable to out on Saturday morning. The Chiefs also said defensive tackle Chris Jones will travel to Atlanta on his own, a notable headline after the FAA grounded all U.S. flights Friday afternoon; air travel has since resumed. This will be the first week Walker will be sidelined in the 2026 season, and it was a cautious move on Kansas City’s part. “We’re kind of feeling it out just to see where we’re at with that thing,” Reid shared on Friday. “We’re not going to put him at risk or any of that. That’s how we roll. If he can go, he can go. If he can’t, he can’t. That would be one of those.” Reid also discussed the possibility of Walker in relation to the opportunity for rookie running back Emmett Johnson. “If Emmett has to do it, then we all have confidence,” Reid said. “He’s going to play anyway, so whether Ken’s there or not there, he’s going to play. So, everybody has confidence in him.” Johnson is in line for his first career start against the Falcons, projected to take the lion’s share of the workload as rookie running back Jaydn Ott (hamstring) was also listed on the injury report as questionable.
