title: What placing TreVeyon Henderson on IR, activating Greg Van Roten and Reggie Gilliam means for the Patriots
summary: At around 10 p.m. local time in Germany on Saturday, the New England Patriots announced that they have made some changes to their roster. Running back TreVeyon Henderson was headed to injured reserve due to the illness that has kept him out since late October, while fullback Reggie Gilliam and offensive lineman Greg Van Roten […]
full_text: At around 10 p.m. local time in Germany on Saturday, the New England Patriots announced that they have made some changes to their roster . Running back TreVeyon Henderson was headed to injured reserve due to the illness that has kept him out since late October, while fullback Reggie Gilliam and offensive lineman Greg Van Roten were both activated from IR. With the Patriots having entered the weekend at 52 players on their roster, Saturday’s transactions meant that they now have a full complement of players available again. What else do the moves mean, though? Let’s find out. RB TreVeyon Henderson: Placed on IR TreVeyon Henderson taking to social media last Friday already was an ominous sign. In a statement addressing the illness that had kept him out for more than a week at that point, he mentioned that “my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions” were affected by the “unexpected and unusual medical emergency” he had been dealing with. While there might still have been hope at that point that he would be able to return in a relatively short period of time, Saturday’s move means that that will not be the case. Henderson will be out for at least the next four games, starting with the upcoming contest against the Detroit Lions. Other games he is now slated to miss include matchups with the Chargers, Bills and Vikings. He is eligible to return to practice and off injured reserve ahead of the Patriots’ Week 15 game in Kansas City, even though an obvious question mark hangs over that comeback given the most recent information we have available — information, head coach Mike Vrabel also did not add to this week. “I talk to TreVeyon every day and just like everybody else that’s not available, he’s working hard to get back,” he said on Thursday at the FC Bayern Munich training facility. “When that is I don’t know. I don’t have a timetable, but I love my interactions with him. I love talking with him and seeing how he’s doing.” From a football perspective, Henderson going to IR officially removes the No. 2 running back from the Patriots’ active roster. This leaves the group looking as follows: 53-man roster (3): Rhamondre Stevenson (38), Corey Kiner (9 | KR), Lan Larison (34) Practice squad (1): Terrell Jennings (26) IR (2): Myles Montgomery (39 | season-ending), TreVeyon Henderson (32) Rhamondre Stevenson is the clear top option, something that would not change with Henderson available. He is the Patriots’ most reliable back in all aspects of playing the position, and by far their best pass protector at the position. Still, Henderson as a rotational second option would bring a more dynamic element to the table than the likes of Corey Kiner and Lan Larison. That element is now missing, even though Kiner in particular has had some promising moments as of late and given Stevenson’s unclear outlook — he is questionable with a knee injury — might see increased reps versus Detroit. In addition to the roster perspective, Henderson going to IR also adds to the numbers crunch regarding the return spots. As a reminder, the Patriots had eight of those available at the start of the year but already used five on the likes of wide receivers A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins, offensive tackle Marcus Bryant and the aforementioned Reggie Gilliam and Greg Van Roten. Two of the remaining three are expected to go to a pair of starters, wide receiver Romeo Doubs and left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker. This, in turn, would potentially leave one such spot open for Henderson. Of course, if they were to qualify for the postseason, the Patriots would get two extra IR-return opportunities. FB Reggie Gilliam: Activated to 53-man roster Gilliam went to injured reserve after the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills. He had been dealing with a knee injury entering that contest, and additionally suffered an ankle ailment in that particular game. New England did not have a traditional fullback on the 53-man roster or practice squad at that point, and never added one either since initially losing Gilliam. This also meant that the fullback packages that were used earlier in the season were not further expanded upon, which in turn might have also played its part in the Patriots struggling to consistently move the football on the ground. Gilliam returning will not instantly fix those issues, but he should be an immediate upgrade over the player the team primarily used to replace him, since-released rookie tight end Tanner Arkin. At the very least, the Patriots can begin incorporating those packages on a more regular and purposeful basis again. In addition to the offensive element, Gilliam’s return also might have a positive impact on the Patriots’ special teams operation. His leadership has been praised repeatedly by coordinator Jeremy Springer, while he also might resume the three-unit role he played prior to his stint on IR: he was used on kickoff coverage, kickoff return and punt coverage, playing 41% of kicking game snaps over the first four weeks of the season. The kickoff coverage element in particular will be worth watching after the Patriots have had multiple breakdowns over the last few weeks. Adding as experienced a special teamer as Gilliam to the mix might help fix those issues. OL Greg Van Roten: Activated to 53-man roster We know that the Patriots offensive line is going to look different compared to the one that started last Sunday’s game against the Packers. The only question is how different. Obviously, three spots are set in stone as they very much have been for the entire season: Will Campbell and Morgan Moses will be the starting tackles, with Jared Wilson at center. The guard positions, meanwhile, remain a revolving door. Before looking into the options for Sunday and further into the future, let’s set the scene by looking at which interior O-linemen are, and are not, available right now: 53-man roster (5): Ben Brown (77 | LG), Jared Wilson (55 | C), Matt Pryor (65 | RG), Greg Van Roten (70), Walter Rouse (72) Practice squad (2): Xavier Newman-Johnson (64), Andrew Rupcich (67) IR (2): Mike Onwenu (71), Alijah Vera-Tucker (75) Ben Brown, who started last week at left guard, will not be available on Sunday against the Lions because of the knee injury he suffered in Week 9. This creates an opening Van Roten might be asked to fill, despite the fact that he played just one non-preseason snap at the position over the last seven years; the last time he played left guard extensively, Tom Brady was still the quarterback in New England. The problem is that the alternatives are not overly attractive either, especially looking at the Lions game. Matt Pryor has limited LG experience as well, while moving him would introduce change at two spots within a unit whose success depends largely on the chemistry between its individual members. Walter Rouse, meanwhile, is questionable to play in the game after showing concussion symptoms coming out of last week’s game versus the Packers. And so, Van Roten might still be the best option after all. Long-term, however, the goal is to bring Alijah Vera-Tucker back into the mix; who will then start at right guard between Pryor, Van Roten or Brown is a question for another time.

title: Patriots place TreVeyon Henderson on IR, activate 2 on eve of Lions game
summary: The New England Patriots made a series of transactions on the eve of their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions, including placing running back TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve. In addition, interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten and fullback Reggie Gilliam were both activated from IR. Furthermore, the Patriots decided to elevate interior offensive […]
full_text: The New England Patriots made a series of transactions on the eve of their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions, including placing running back TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve. In addition, interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten and fullback Reggie Gilliam were both activated from IR. Furthermore, the Patriots decided to elevate interior offensive lineman Andrew Rupcich from the practice squad to the game day roster for Sunday. Henderson, 24, has been sidelined since Oct. 29 due to an illness. Earlier this month, he shared an update on his status on social media and explained that he had recently “experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days.” A second-round draft pick by the Patriots in 2025, the Ohio State product finished his rookie campaign with 1,132 scrimmage yards and 10 touchdowns. His sophomore season, however, was a challenging one even before his recent illness: serving as the Patriots’ No. 2 behind Rhamondre Stevenson, Henderson missed time due to two separate ankle injuries sustained in August and October, respectively, and as a consequence was limited to six games as well as 57 touches for 248 scrimmage yards and one touchdown. With his move to IR freeing up a roster spot, the Patriots were able to activate two players. Van Roten, 36, arrived in New England during preseason after an then-top backup interior offensive lineman Ben Brown suffered an injury. On his ninth different team since entering the NFL in 2012, he remained on the roster even after Brown’s return and was the first man up when right guard Mike Onwenu fractured his ankle in Week 2. Unfortunately for the veteran backup, he himself sustained a thigh injury in his first start the following week and subsequently had to be placed on injured reserve as well. Gilliam, 29, signed a three-year, $10.8 million free agency contract with the Patriots in March. Taking over the fullback position upon his arrival, he played 58 offensive snaps and 32 on special teams over the first four weeks of the season; he caught one 4-yard pass along the way. Gilliam also sustained a knee injury at one point and in Week 4 against his former team, the Bills, added an ankle issue. That second injury prompted the Patriots to send him to IR a few days later. Both Van Roten and Gilliam had previously returned to practice to open their 21-day return windows. Van Roten returned last week alongside Mack Hollins, but unlike the wide receiver was not activated ahead of last Sunday’s game against the Packers. Van Roten made his return to the practice fields before the Patriots boarded their flight to Germany on Wednesday. The Patriots furthermore elevated the aforementioned Andrew Rupcich from the practice squad. With Van Roten only now returning, Ben Brown being ruled out of the game with a knee injury, and Walter Rouse questionable after entering concussion protocol this week, he provides experienced emergency depth up front. The Patriots will take on the Lions at Munich’s Allianz Arena at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday.

title: Patriots fans’ confidence in team nears season low
summary: Everything seemingly went right for the New England Patriots in 2025. In Mike Vrabel’s first season as head coach, Drake Maye emerged as an MVP candidate with a significant Year 2 leap, while nearly every major offseason addition, such as Milton Williams and Stefon Diggs, played a key role in the Patriots’ run to Super […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - November 8: New England Patriots fans react to a call in the second quarter. The New England Patriots played the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium on November 8, 2026. (Photo by Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images Everything seemingly went right for the New England Patriots in 2025. In Mike Vrabel’s first season as head coach, Drake Maye emerged as an MVP candidate with a significant Year 2 leap, while nearly every major offseason addition, such as Milton Williams and Stefon Diggs, played a key role in the Patriots’ run to Super Bowl LX. This season, however, has been a different story. With plenty of new faces on both sides of the ball and a league-high number of injuries, the 2026 Patriots season has felt more like a grind. The season has been defined by plenty of ups and downs, from Maye’s slow start highlighted by a blowout loss in Jacksonville to an upset win in Buffalo that kickstarted a winning streak. That win streak was followed by the Patriots dropping two games against NFC North opponents, including a troubling 45-27 loss at home to the Green Bay Packers. Those peaks and valleys have been reflected in Patriots fans’ confidence in the team, which nearly hit a season low this week following the loss to Green Bay, which marked the worst defeat of the Vrabel era. Despite fan confidence taking a major dip this past week, the 5-4 Patriots still find themselves in the AFC playoff picture and as contenders. “We’re 5-4. I think there’s going to be a lot of contending teams that are 5-4. I think that’s the nature of the National Football League,” Vrabel said. “We’ve got to draw a line here. We’ve got to think that we’re 0-0, and we’ve got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January.” According to Patriots fans, the team’s ceiling is viewed best just as a playoff contender. In the latest SB Nation Reacts survey, 54% of participants said that is how they see the team compared to just 3% who still view them as Super Bowl contenders. The remaining 43% of voters don’t view New England as a contender at all. Much of the comment section sees it similarly: MaineMan After getting blown out by the 5-3 Packers, if they lose to DET on Sunday, probably not. That will drop them to 5-5 and needing to win five, perhaps even six of their last seven games. Facing BUF (7-1), MIN (6-2), KCY (6-2) & DEN (7-2) in four of those games, even a 5-2 stretch run seems very unlikely. sanfranpatsfan so much negativity around here with 43% voting that we are not even playoff contenders despite stilling holding the 7 seed currently and no one below us looking good. one run to the SB and half the fan base is re-spoiled jeer9 They have 8 wins if they beat the 3 stinkers left on their schedule. That means they need to go 2 out of 5 against Detroit, Minnesota, KC, Buffalo, and Denver to make the playoffs – which is doable. Anything can happen once you’re in; though based on their erratic effort, I don’t see them making it very far. PatsHowYouDoIt I have full faith they will remain competitive and make it to the playoffs. luckyfukikentucky I think they sneak into the playoffs. Then it depends on how healthy and cohesive we are as a team. It’s a knockout competition from that point if you get hot you can go all the way. fdcpuffy6 This team feels like it might, might, sneak into the playoffs but be one and done. They can change the narrative by playing better football the rest of the season and beating the quality teams left on the schedule. All in all, this week’s survey results look as follows: While fans are down on the Patriots making a run back to the Super Bowl, the team currently holds the 13th best odds of hosting the Lombardi Trophy this season on FanDuel Sportsbook . That is sixth best in the AFC trailing just the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Kansas City Chiefs, Cincinnati Bengals and Denver Broncos.

title: 3-Point Stance: Defense could be a roadblock in Patriots’ playoff pursuit
summary: Last week, I wrote that the New England Patriots shouldn’t preemptively deal an impact player at the NFL trade deadline amid defensive players Christian Barmore and Carlton Davis reportedly being available for trade. Ultimately, the Patriots didn’t make any transactions on Tuesday. Although I cited the offseason as a better time to move either defender, […]
full_text: Last week, I wrote that the New England Patriots shouldn’t preemptively deal an impact player at the NFL trade deadline amid defensive players Christian Barmore and Carlton Davis reportedly being available for trade . Ultimately, the Patriots didn’t make any transactions on Tuesday. Although I cited the offseason as a better time to move either defender, I noted the defense’s encouraging Week Eight performance against the now 1-7 Miami Dolphins as a potential turning point for what has largely been an underwhelming and injured unit through the first half of the season. That didn’t stick. It’s hard not to be concerned about New England’s defense after last Sunday’s deflating performance against the Green Bay Packers. Those reservations are especially warranted when the Patriots’ most expensive cornerback room in the league allows two receivers, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson, to combine for 335 yards and two touchdowns, with each logging career highs. All-Pro Christian Gonzalez, entering 2026 on a four-year, $135 million contract extension, allowed 10 receptions for 187 yards, per NextGen Stats. “I’m a Christian Gonzalez fan,” NFL Hall of Famer Ty Law said on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show . “I just expect more out of him … I have never been a part of a situation in my 15-year career where a secondary played that bad … That’s unacceptable … You got the bag. You have to play better. “I’m seeing a lot of things that aren’t right when it comes to the New England Patriots’ secondary. Where is the leadership? Where is the communication? … Is it the players or the coaching?” After the game, Gonzalez took responsibility for his poor performance but also isn’t “too worried about it.” “I think Christian [Gonzalez] just did it to himself,” two-time Super Bowl champion Logan Ryan said on the Up & Adams Show . “I loved his comment … He said, ‘Hey, I’m allowed to have a bad day. I had a bad day.’ He doesn’t have a lot of them, and that’s going to happen. Watson and Golden are different [types of receivers] … He had to deal with them both. “Part of being a number one corner is that you have to guard whatever comes out there … Credit to what Green Bay did, but I think mentally he was in his head. He had a slow start, and [then] it continued … That’s the life of being a number one cornerback. You have to bounce back, and I think he will.” Head coach Mike Vrabel acknowledged that he expects more from Gonzalez while emphasizing that the rest of the defense must improve overall. Gonzalez’s struggles are surprising, but the organization paid him for a reason. Another performance like that would be an outlier. Still, his shortcomings highlight an underlying factor that has seen a steady decline in not only Gonzalez’s play but also the inconsistencies of the defense. A lack of execution Over the past week, Patriots defenders across multiple positional groups have cited execution as something to improve upon. Veteran safety Kevin Byard frequently alluded to that sentiment when discussing the Packers’ explosive plays. “We just didn’t execute enough,” Byard said on Sunday. “We knew that was going to be the key to the game, eliminating the big play, and we didn’t do good enough today at all. We all have to be better.” Linebacker and captain Robert Spillane emphasized a similar message Wednesday on The Greg Hill Show , stressing the importance of playing complementary football ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the Detroit Lions, whose offense shares similarities with Green Bay’s. “You put pressure on [Jared Goff] by stopping the run early, by forcing third-and-long passing situations, by being up on the scoreboard, by starting fast as a team, as a unit, and that’s all three phases. I think it’s really a collection of how we play as a team to get that done.” What does that execution come down to? It encompasses everything the team prepares for. Against the Packers, it was schematic and assignment breakdowns. Against the Chicago Bears in Week Seven, it was a lack of physicality. The defense allowed Chicago to notch 30 points on the evening and score on six of its nine offensive drives. Poor tackling plagued the unit throughout the game, giving up 161 yards after the catch. Vrabel’s defense appeared a step behind, exemplifying symptoms of a Super Bowl hangover. Following Sunday night’s loss, outside questions emerged about whether the lack of execution stems from a downward shift in team culture and energy nine months removed from the franchise’s championship appearance. When speaking with reporters in the locker room, wide receiver Mack Hollins said that players content with New England’s performance are “probably not meant for this team,” while DeMario Douglas called for more energy and support from each unit on the sideline. Vrabel echoed the need for better execution on Monday, specifically addressing Gonzalez’s lackluster performance, explaining that “you can’t take a nap in this league.” “You just can’t take a play off or think that they’re not going to challenge or throw the ball at you,” he said. “That’s it. You can’t think that you’re going to not draw attention.” Vrabel, however, views it as a preparation issue, seeing Hollins’ view and his comments about wanting players who want to be with the team as a reminder of the standards required to build the program he envisions. “Whatever reps we get, we have to make them count,” Vrabel said. ”We have to understand, if it’s a jog through, how we show the details of the play and make sure that we understand that.“ Regardless of the state of the team’s culture, poor execution and a lack of physicality are capping a defense that was slated to build on last season’s performance, ranking No. 4 in scoring defense. Healthier defense, underperforming results Statistically, the defense has played better while dealing with injuries compared to finally fielding a healthy starting group. Over the last three games, New England is giving up an average of 31.3 points per game, an increase from 18.8 through the first six contests. Squaring off with the Dolphins in Miami, things were trending upward as the divisional foes managed only five first downs in 10 offensive series. For reference, the game marked the first time the starting cornerback trio of Gonzalez, Carlton Davis and Marcus Jones all played together since Week Three. While Davis is ruled out for Sunday with a knee injury, the defense is still nearly whole. So far this season, the defense ranks 31st against under-center snaps and 32nd when facing early-down play-action. Their corrections against a Lions offense that frequently operates under center and has plenty of success running one of the highest play-action rates in the league. Offense hampered by injuries With so many injuries, the Patriots’ offense hasn’t established a rhythm all season. They simply haven’t had the pieces. Although A.J. Brown, Rhamondre Stevenson and Reggie Gilliam were limited in practice this week, New England only recently welcomed Mack Hollins back to the lineup. The Patriots also remain without Alijah Vera-Tucker, Romeo Doubs, TreVeyon Henderson and Mike Onwenu (potentially sidelined for the season), each potentially sidelined for the season, while Hunter Henry continues to play banged up. Even if a select few of those names return against Detroit, the defense needs to elevate its play to help New England get back in the win column consistently by keeping the offense in scoring range. The Patriots are still 5-4 and in the playoff picture, but with a tough rest-of-season schedule and the Houston Texans sneaking into the playoff bubble, things need to turn around swiftly.

title: College Players to Watch: Week 10
summary: The Saints seem to have found a running mate for Chase Young in Carl Granderson. Right now, those two are the best pass-rushing combination in the NFL. The priority for this team should be to address the defense at every level. With that in mind, here are some important players to watch. Will Echoles remains […]
full_text: OXFORD, MS - OCTOBER 17: Ole Miss Rebels defensive tackle Will Echoles (52) celebrates a defensive stand during the game between the Ole Miss Rebels and the Missouri Tigers on October 17, 2026 at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, MS. (Photo by Jason Homan/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Saints seem to have found a running mate for Chase Young in Carl Granderson. Right now, those two are the best pass-rushing combination in the NFL. The priority for this team should be to address the defense at every level. With that in mind, here are some important players to watch. Will Echoles remains my favorite player for this team right now. The interior defensive lineman is arguably the best player at his position in this draft class. Right now, Echoles has 22 tackles, five TFLs, and 2.5 sacks. With the surprising lack of availability from Christen Miller, DT remains a major position of need. Echoles and the Rebels will be on the road against Oklahoma at 3:15 p.m. on the SEC Network. It goes without saying that if the run defense is not living up to expectations, then the linebackers need to be better. Well, Georgia continues to be Linebacker U, and one of the best linebackers in this class is Chris Cole. Cole is a dynamic, do-it-all linebacker for the Bulldogs. So far this season, Cole has recorded 58 tackles, 11 TFLs, five sacks, three passes defended, three fumble recoveries, and two defensive TDs. Cole is a semifinalist for both the Butkus and Lombardi Awards. Cole and the Bulldogs will be hosting Missouri at 2:30 p.m. on ABC. When talking about the run game, being able to run the ball consistently is something that can always help a marginal defense by keeping it off the field. The Saints brought back Audric Estime, and he seems to be the missing piece of the rushing offense. However, adding another running back needs to be considered, especially one who has a higher floor and ceiling than what is currently in the running back room. A player to watch should be Florida running back Jaden Baugh. Baugh currently has 860 yards on 160 carries, averaging 5.4 yards per carry while playing in the SEC on an offense that cannot throw a forward pass with confidence. He has forced 48 missed tackles and has a breakaway percentage of 44.1%. He also has 14 TDs, which leads the SEC. Baugh will be in Lexington to take on Kentucky at 5:15 p.m. on ESPN. Finally, the Saints need better play at safety. There’s no other way to describe it. A name to watch is Amare Ferrell. Ferrell is a three-year starter at safety for Indiana, and he is a consistent ball hawk. He has 11 career interceptions, including three so far this season. He’s also a solid tackler. If the Saints are getting better pressure up front, the best complement would be a safety over the top who can force incompletions or come away with interceptions. Ferrell and the Hoosiers will be hosting the USC Trojans at 2:30 p.m. on CBS. Who are some players you are excited to watch this weekend? What are some names you think should be on Who Dat Nation’s radar? Share your thoughts in the comments section.

title: College football Week 11: Three draft prospects for the NY Giants
summary: Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 11 of the 2026 college football season! The college schedule is taking a bit of a breath after last week’s insane slate of games. So I want to take the time to focus on a few deep cut players who haven’t gotten much […]
full_text: Boise State running back Dylan Riley carries the ball against Colorado State. | Getty Images Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 11 of the 2026 college football season! The college schedule is taking a bit of a breath after last week’s insane slate of games. So I want to take the time to focus on a few deep cut players who haven’t gotten much national attention just yet, but could be real risers once the draft process gets underway. And, of course, they’ll be players at positions of (perceived) need for the Giants. We’ve spent quite a bit of time talking about defensive tackle and wide receiver, so this week I’m focusing on offensive line, defensive back, and running back. Iowa State vs. Cincinnati TNT – noon Player spotlight – Evan Tengesdahl (LG, Cincinnati) The Giants extended Jon Runyan Jr. just before the start of the 2026 season after a strong off-season and pre-season. However, he has had frustrating lapses in both pass protection and run blocking this year. The Giants might not be able to move on from Runyan easily in 2027, but it might be a good idea to have a successor in the pipeline. Tengesdahl is a big (6-foot-3, 320-pounds) mauler of a left guard who brings heavy hands and the ability to distort the line of scrimmage. He’s a solid pass protector as well as a powerful downhill run blocker, which should make him an intriguing fit in Greg Roman’s man-gap heavy run schemes. (5) Notre Dame vs. Boston College NBC – 3:30 p.m. Player spotlight – Luke Talich (S, Notre Dame) I wouldn’t ordinarily call attention to a game like this. Notre Dame should win handily against BC and this will probably be something of a snoozer. However, I wanted to take the opportunity to call attention to a player who could catch John Harbaugh’s eye in Notre Dame senior safety Luke Talich. Talich is a huge safety at 6-foot-4, 220 pounds, but also has rare versatility. His size obviously suggests a player who can thrive in the box as a pseudo-linebacker, however he has the ability to impact a game as a true “STAR” or defensive weapon. Talich currently has 43 tackles, 4.5 tackles for a loss, and a sack, which is expected for a safety of his size. What’s less expected is the fact that he leads a very good Notre Dame secondary with 3 interceptions. He also had 3 interceptions a year ago, as well as one as a sophomore. He moves surprisingly well for a player with his size and obviously has fantastic instincts for playing the ball in the air. It would be irresponsible to directly compare Talich to Kyle Hamilton, but rest assured that the “shades of…” comments will be coming once the Draft Process gets underway. And given that the Giants’ “Ravens Style” defense loves versatile defensive backs, Talich could be high on their board come draft time. (24) Boise State vs. Oregon State USA – 6pm Player Spotlight: Dylan Riley (RB, Boise State) This game has the potential to be a fun one. Boise State has been making noise lately, and they might even be a dark horse to get a College Football Playoff berth. Oregon State, meanwhile, has one of the most fun offenses in college football and freshman wideout Jesse Legree is quickly becoming a star. And since the Giants weren’t able to secure a running back to provide explosive runs at the trade deadline, I’m turning my attention to the draft. Junior running back Dylan Riley isn’t a rumbling power back at 5-foot-10, 205 pounds, but he is an absolute sparkplug with the ball in his hands. He’s currently averaging 6.7 yards per carry on 184 carries (1,241 rushing yards) with 11 rushing touchdowns — as well as 17 catches for 218 yards (12.8 per catch) and another 2 touchdowns. He has fantastic patience and vision behind the line of scrimmage, as well as a very good burst and long speed for breakaway runs. Riley also has more toughness and power than his frame would suggest, and doesn’t have a problem running between the tackles or finishing behind his pads. The Giants will be running back hunting this year, and Riley could be a much better value than a player like Jadan Baugh (Florida) or Keywan Lacey (Ole Miss) while offering similar upside.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Giants know why Dominic Zvada is missing kicks; now, can they fix it?
summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh has steadfastly stood by rookie placekicker Dominic Zvada through Zvada’s ups and downs this season, which have included too many costly misses. Harbaugh continued to do so after Zvada’s latest miss, an extra-point distance 33-yarder in what became a three-point loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday night. […]
full_text: Dominic Zvada after his 33-yard miss on Thursday. | Getty Images New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh has steadfastly stood by rookie placekicker Dominic Zvada through Zvada’s ups and downs this season, which have included too many costly misses. Harbaugh continued to do so after Zvada’s latest miss, an extra-point distance 33-yarder in what became a three-point loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday night. “You can’t, as soon as a guy doesn’t make a play, start firing people left and right. Especially your kicker who’s a rookie,” Harbaugh said. “So, I’m confident he’s going to become a good kicker. I mean, at some point in time, if it doesn’t happen, it doesn’t happen. But I’m not going to panic halfway through the season when a guy’s made a bunch of kicks, if that’s what you’re inferring we should be doing. We’re just not going to knee jerk it like that. He’s going to make kicks. He’s going to make a lot of kicks. I believe in him. I think he’s really good and really talented. We’re going to give him an opportunity to do it, and it’s up to him to do it.“ Turns out, all six of Zvada’s misses this season — three pushed wide right and three yanked wide left — have come from the right hash. All 6 of Dominic Zvada’s missed kicks this season have come from the right hash, including his 33-yard miss last night. The Giants have lined up on the left hash for every extra point, where Zvada is a perfect 16/16. https://t.co/D9YzxVSYyx pic.twitter.com/UHJa8av5EK — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) November 13, 2026 “There’s a technique issue there with his plant foot that we’re kind of looking at,” Harbaugh said on Friday. “And he needs to clean that up from a consistency standpoint. He knows that. Popped up again in that one kick there. There is an issue on the right hash, no question.” Zvada was tremendous all spring and summer, beating out Ben Sauls for the placekicking job. He started the season 9-for-9, but has made just 8 of 14 kicks since. It is fair to say that Zvada’s struggles were critical parts of why the Giants tied and lost games to the Commanders, rather than winning both games. He missed three kicks in the tie to Washington in Week 5, and his miss Thursday came in a 3-point loss. It is also fair to wonder if Zvada’s struggles have impacted some of Harbaugh’s decisions. The Giants punted three times inside Washington territory Thursday night — from the 37-, 41- and 46-yard lines. Two of those kicks would have come from inside 60 yards, where the Giants have already asked Zvada to kick nine times this season. Maybe the play-calling that led to the punts would have been different if the Giants truly had faith in Zvada. Or, maybe they would have allowed him to try those kicks. “Well, let’s look at the distances. Why don’t you go back and give me the distances. I don’t have it in front of me. What were those field goals have been? They were like high 50s, weren’t they? 55 plus,” Harbaugh said. “It’s kind of a risk-reward. I’m not saying that he can’t make those kicks, but it’s a windy night and it’s a field position game in some ways. It’s a big risk there, too. Sometimes it’s better to play a field position game. “So those were toss up kind of calls probably at least, probably leaning toward punting, but I’m not saying we shouldn’t have gone for them or couldn’t have kicked them either way. The one question is, “should you have gone for it?” The next question is, “should you have kicked the field goals?” That’s the follow-up question. I don’t know. The other question could have been if we’d have missed the field goal, maybe you should have punted it down in there and played the field position game. So they’re all kind of coin flip type of decisions.” Here is how the analytics saw each of the three situations in which the Giants chose to punt rather than try the field or go for the first down: Giants 0, Commanders 0 Fourth-and-7 at the Washington 37, Q1 11:28 Commanders 17, Giants 14 Fourth-and-3 at the Washington 46, Q4 14:15 Giants 21, Commanders 17 Fourth-and-5 at the Washington 41, Q4 1:54 The point here isn’t to debate which decisions Harbaugh made correctly, and which he didn’t. Though discussing that is certainly fair game. The point is that Zvada’s continued misses are complicating the decision-making and costing the Giants points that are probably costing them games. In an NFC East race that seems likely to go down to the wire, and where every decision, every made or missed kick, everything that happens in the margins of an NFL game, could end up making the difference how much rope can the Giants give Zvada to figure it out?
author: Ed Valentine

title: New York Giants mailbag: Kickoff rule, Rasul Douglas interception, more
summary: Lou Catalano asks: Could you please explain the rule concerning kickoffs going out of bounds? In the Giants/Washington game, the ball bounced in bounds, the returner stepped out of bounds, then caught the ball while his knee was touching the ground in bounds. What ever happpened to the old John Madden maxim that one knee […]
full_text: Lou Catalano asks: Could you please explain the rule concerning kickoffs going out of bounds? In the Giants/Washington game, the ball bounced in bounds, the returner stepped out of bounds, then caught the ball while his knee was touching the ground in bounds. What ever happpened to the old John Madden maxim that one knee equals two feet? Ed says: Lou, you weren’t the only confused by this. The rulebook says: “A ball that is in player possession is out of bounds when the runner is out of bounds.” On kickoffs, this is a bit of a loophole. Credit Luke McCaffrey of the Commanders for knowing the rule and making a great play. If you plant your feet out of bounds, then touch a ball that is inbounds, it makes the ball considered to be out of bounds. That creates a kickoff out of bounds and puts the ball at the 40-yard line. I have seen this happen a couple of times. I have also seen players mess this up by either catching the ball and stepping out of bounds, or by picking the ball up inbounds right near the sideline and trying to return it. David Silver asks: I’m trying to make sense out of the last throw JJ McCarthy made to Nabers that was intercepted. It looks like McCarthy hung the ball up based on the trajectory. It also gave Nabers plenty of time to get it sighted. Douglas comes from behind to high point Nabers, but it also looked like he hit Nabers early. But that is a 50/50 ball Nabers wants. My question is, bad throw, bad catch attempt, great defensive play, or pass interference? Ed says: David, sometimes you just have to give the other guy credit. I have watched this play a bunch of times, and I listened to Nabers and John Harbaugh talk about it on Friday. Washington sent a zero blitz, rushing more players than the Giants could block and forcing J.J. McCarthy to make a split-second decision. His decision was to give the Giants’ best receiver a chance to make a play. Right decision? Wrong decision? Harbaugh just said it was the decision that McCarthy made. Douglas didn’t interfere with Nabers. Nabers said he was focused on tracking the ball and knew there was a defender in the area, but didn’t know where. Douglas did not interfere with Nabers. He just ended up making a play. The Giants have won a couple of games like that this season. The other guys get paid, too. Raymond Dansereau asks: How much better are the Giants really than last year? Last year they had a tough schedule and close losses; this year, they’re playing a weak schedule and really not always looking great. Defense seems better, but is this a 10-7 playoffs team that gets beaten badly in the first round? Or, does this look like sustainable improvement? Or too soon to say? Ed says: Raymond, I can’t go position-by-position or player-by-player in a mailbag response. I think the real answer is that the Giants are better simply because they have John Harbaugh and they are coached better. It doesn’t hurt that this team has Arvell Reese, either. The Giants are winning close games, which they couldn’t do last year. A lot of that is coaching, whether it is in-game decisions or just preparing players well enough that they believe they are supposed to make plays and win close games. If it is a 9-7-1 playoff team that gets bounced in the first round, what’s wrong with that? The Giants won seven games combined the past two seasons — a playoff berth would be a fantastic accomplishment. Sustainable improvement? The NFL is such a week-to-week and year-to-year league that is impossible to say. As long as Harbaugh is the coach, though, the Giants have a chance to be relevant. That is a massive improvement. Matt Smith asks: We’ve had four failures in a row at the head coach position. They are bookended by two Hall of Fame coaches. My question is, seeing how far the gap is between Daboll and Harbaugh, do you find it surprising how long we waited to move on from him? It seems more and more apparent to me that we had talent that we could’ve done with if we had a professional head coach with standards. The red flags were always there. Ed says: Matt, I’m not at all surprised that the Giants waited as long as they did to move on from Brian Daboll. look at the Giants’ track record: Ben McAdoo lasted less than two full seasons. Pat Shurmur was fired after two seasons. Joe Judge was fired (well, he kinda fired himself) after two seasons. You cannot get ahead when you have to keep blowing things up and starting over every two years. That means an entire new coaching staff, gutting most of the roster, and starting over. You can never institute a real philosophy or build anything that way. John Mara knew it, and he said several times that he knew he needed to be more patient than he had been. Daboll had a shockingly good first season and won Coach of the Year. The Giants could have justified firing him and GM Joe Schoen after a 3-14 2024 season, but chose not to. Mike Vrabel got hired by New England that offseason. Zero chance he was picking the Giants over the Patriots, the team he played for an an organization he loves. Ben Johnson got hired by the Bears. No chance he was picking the Giants over the Bears, who already had Caleb Williams in place. Liam Coen got hired by the Jaguars, but nobody knew that would work out as well as it had. It was really the 2025 season when it became clear that the coaching staff wasn’t maximizing the talent of the players. Adam Singer asks: During the game against the Eagles, it looked like some of the players had a diagonal line through the word “GIANTS” on their helmets while others did not. What was going on there? Ed says: Adam, the word ‘GIANTS’ was underlined. I think what you saw was the chinstrip, which buckles on the side of the helmet, protruding over the lettering on some of the helmets. Ronald Lukoff asks: I usually do not disagree with a lot of your comments but I do take exception to your thoughts about the Giants making a blockbuster trade today (this is written Tuesday morning). I have been a Giant fan since 1956. I have seen a lot of success and a lot of failure. This team is made up of a lot of draft picks and I really do not want to give up future draft choices for a player that can give us a division title. This team has only played one team with a record above .500. Do you really think that one player is worth losing draft capital? If I thought one player could get us to the Super Bowl, I might feel differently. Do you think JJ is the answer at QB. He was great first 5 quarters, not so much last game. but a quarterback needy ream just traded him away, so I am hesitant to put all my faith in him and believe me, I hope I’m wrong. I feel like we are at least a year away from potentially going to the Super Bowl and while I would love to win the division, I just don’t think giving up draft choices is the best way to build a championship team. You’re feelings? Ed says: Ronald, it’s moot at this point since the trade deadline has come and gone. I want to clarify this, anyway. I wrote earlier in the week that the Giants should try to capitalize on the opportunity they have in the NFC East. You don’t know if or when that opportunity will come again. They did try to do that. They were very aggressive. They were also careful. I said earlier in the week there was a price they should not go to — meaning they should not go above the second-round pick they had offered the Colts for Jonathan Taylor. They — rightly — refused to do that. I said all along the end game is not winning the division this year and then going back to being a third- or fourth-place team for fove years after that. The end game is to be a championship contender on a consistent basis. You have to protect your future to do that.

title: NY Giants news: Reactions to Washington loss, J.J. McCarthy, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know this weekend. Giants embrace upcoming gauntlet: ‘We want all the smoke’ | NJ.com The Giants will be rooting hard for the 49ers this weekend. That’s because if the Cowboys somehow beat San Francisco, they’ll move closer to the Giants in the […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know this weekend. Giants embrace upcoming gauntlet: ‘We want all the smoke’ | NJ.com The Giants will be rooting hard for the 49ers this weekend. That’s because if the Cowboys somehow beat San Francisco, they’ll move closer to the Giants in the NFC East race. The Giants are 5-3-1 after Thursday night’s 24-21 gut-punch loss to the Commanders. Coach John Harbaugh’s team remains alone atop the division, ahead of the 4-5 Cowboys and 3-5-1 Commanders (who now have the head-to-head tiebreaker edge over the Giants). On to the next one J.J. McCarthy on moving forward after Thursday night pic.twitter.com/7Z2MNx8u4e — New York Giants (@Giants) November 13, 2026 Why J.J. McCarthy kept chucking ball downfield before game-sealing interception in Giants’ crushing loss | New York Post Quarterback J.J. McCarthy certainly shouldn’t shoulder all the blame, but an interception with 25 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter sealed the loss and gave the Commanders the tiebreaker over the Giants after the two teams tied in Week 5. Despite being at the Washington 48-yard line with 40 seconds remaining and needing only a field goal, McCarthy threw deep on his final two passes. The first fell to the turf for an incomplete pass, and the second was intended for Malik Nabers but instead landed in Rasul Douglas’ arms to end the Giants’ comeback attempt. “My thought process was pop it up to my playmakers, have them go make a play,” McCarthy said. What we saw as NY Giants fail to seal the deal against Commanders | The Record For the first time all season, the New York Giants failed to deliver with the lead in the fourth quarter and the game on the line. Jayden Daniels’ third touchdown pass, this one to Stefon Diggs, as two Giants defenders ran into each other with 57 seconds remaining allowed Washington to snap Big Blue’s two-game winning streak with a 24-21 victory at MetLife Stadium. Cam Skattebo scores twice after Giants’ quiet trade deadline, but wonders if he could’ve done more in loss to Commanders | New York Daily News But after the Giants’ offense stagnated down the stretch of a 24-21 loss — with Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy both getting stopped on third-down QB keepers — Skattebo was left wondering if he could have done more. “It sucks, and I think part of it is I put myself in a situation last time we played these guys that kind of killed the trust in Coach [John Harbaugh] maybe a little bit, of giving up the ball last time,” Skattebo said. “And maybe he didn’t want to give me the ball again. I don’t know. I’m not gonna say that was something that he was thinking, but I would think that as well.” Skattebo followed with runs of five and two yards, setting up a crucial 3rd and 3. But on a designed QB run, McCarthy was tackled by Sonny Styles behind the line of scrimmage, prompting another Giants punt. Asked if he felt he could have led the Giants into field-goal range had he gotten the ball, Skattebo replied, “I can’t say that. Do I think that? Yeah, but I can’t say that, because it could’ve been any situation at any time.” New York Giants slam ‘corny’ DPI penalty called on Deonte Banks | USAToday.com “This league is funny, bro,” said Safety Tyler Nubin. “This league is funny. There’s really nothing you can do about it, man. When you’re in trail position, nine times out of 10, they’re going to call that PI. That’s just how the league is. Just got to weather it.” “I’m going to be honest, and I ain’t going to say nothing that gets me fined,” Safety Jason Pinnock said. “But it’s getting to a point now where [offensive coordinators] are taking advantage of it. They’re not calling real plays. They’re going four wide, and they’re throwing that junk outside. And it looks like these receivers literally have techniques to get PIs. They’re grabbing the back of DBs’ necks. It’s almost like it’s becoming a technique.” The window that J.J. McCarthy put this in…. On 3rd & 7.. this should've been the defining pass play in a win pic.twitter.com/4xqG4zB3jr — Dan Schneier (@DanSchneierNFL) November 13, 2026 2026 NFL midseason award rankings: MVP picks, top rookies, OPOY, DPOY, coaches | ESPN.com Defensive Rookie of the Year. 1. Arvell Reese, LB/Edge, New York Giants. Picking between Bailey and Reese is unfair. I leaned Reese if only because he has been two impactful players in one this season. As an off-ball linebacker, Reese has been all over the place for a Giants team that has been better against the run this season, even after trading Dexter Lawrence II. Reese has made tackles on 15.3% of his snaps, the eighth-highest rate in the league. He has given up an 81.3 passer rating in coverage, a very credible number for a veteran linebacker, let alone a rookie just getting his feet wet at this level. And then there’s Reese’s side quest as a devastating force on blitzes. Despite rushing the quarterback only about 11 times per game, Reese already has 4.5 sacks and 14 pressures. His 10.2% quick pressure rate would be the second-best mark in the NFL if he qualified. And the average Reese pressure comes after 2.44 seconds, the fifth fastest among players with 10 pressures or more. NFL midseason superlatives and lessons: Josh Allen for MVP, all-in moves, dashed hopes | The Athletic Defensive rookie of the year – LB Arvell Reese, New York Giants. The No. 5 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has racked up 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss, 49 solo tackles (68 total), a forced fumble and an interception for the surprising Giants. Coach of the Year — John Harbaugh, New York Giants. Ben Johnson continues to lead an impressive Chicago Bears team, and Kyle Shanahan’s 49ers rank among the Super Bowl favorites. But with the Giants unexpectedly leading their division and contending for their first playoff berth since the 2022 season — with a backup quarterback, no less — Harbaugh gets the nod. 2026 NFL DROY Odds: Which New York Rookie Has The Edge? | FOX Sports Arvell Reese has jumped David Bailey on the odds board and sits at +100 after Week 9. The Giants rookie was drafted with the fifth pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, and so far, he’s exceeding those expectations. Through nine weeks, Reese is second in the entire NFL in solo tackles (49) and leads the Giants’ defense in total tackles as a rookie. Reese joined Nick Bosa (2019) as the only players in the last 25 seasons with at least four sacks, an interception, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in their first eight career games. It looks like the G-Men have finally found a guy they can build their defense around for the next decade. NFL midseason awards: The good, the bad and the Dallas Cowboys | Yahoo! Sports The ‘Chicken Salad from Chicken S**t’ Award: New York Giants. Boy, the Giants were feeling fine after their Week 1 win over Dallas. And just as quickly, hopes deflated when Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury in Week 2. But somehow, the Giants have cobbled together win after win, using quarterback after quarterback, and suddenly they’re dangerous. Granted, it’s a “is that stray dog going to beg for food or bite my face?” kind of dangerous, but it’s better than nothing. summary: The New York Jets are home in East Rutherford, New Jersey today. They will be taking on the Buffalo Bills. The game is scheduled to start shortly after 1:00 pm EST. full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: New York Jets fans cheer against the Tennessee Titans during the fourth quarter of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets are home in East Rutherford, New Jersey today. They will be taking on the Buffalo Bills. The game is scheduled to start shortly after 1:00 pm EST. The game will be played in typical chilly late autumn weather. Partly cloudy skies will prevail for the entirety of the game. Winds will be moderate and variable at around 10 to 15 mph with a few higher gusts up to 25 mph out of the north northwest to start the game, shifting to the northwest by game’s end. Temperatures will be steady in the high 40s to near 50 degrees throughout the game. Relative humidity will be moderate and steady in the mid 40s throughout the game. There will be a near zero chance of precipitation throughout the game. In short, this will be the first real football weather of the season in New Jersey. Conditions will be breezy and chilly, exactly how football in the northeast is supposed to be. For the players a few wind gusts could affect the passing game, and the wind could have a mild effect on field goals and extra points, but for the most part the weather shouldn’t be much of a factor. For the fans, it’s time to bundle up. Sitting and standing outside in this weather without some cold weather gear will be uncomfortable.Other than that, what a great day for football! Enjoy the game everyone.

title: Jets activate rookie defensive back, waive offensive lineman ahead of Bills game
summary: The New York Jets activated rookie safety VJ Payne off of the injured reserve list ahead of their game against the Buffalo Bills this Sunday. In a corresponding move the Jets waived backup offensive lineman Kohl Levao to make room for Payne. VJ Payne is a 22 year old, 6’ 3”, 205 pound safety drafted […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - FEBRUARY 27: VJ Payne #DB44 of Kansas State participates in a drill during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 27, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets activated rookie safety VJ Payne off of the injured reserve list ahead of their game against the Buffalo Bills this Sunday. In a corresponding move the Jets waived backup offensive lineman Kohl Levao to make room for Payne. VJ Payne is a 22 year old, 6’ 3”, 205 pound safety drafted by the Jets with the 228th selection in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL draft. Payne suffered a bone bruise during training camp and missed the entire preseason. He was placed on the injured reserve list prior to the start of the regular season with a designation to return. Payne returned to practice with the Jets on November 4. He is now eligible to make his NFL debut, possibly as early as Sunday against the Bills. VJ Payne played four years in college, all with the Kansas State Wildcats. He appeared in 52 games for the Wildcats, starting 42 of those games. In his final year in college in 2025, Payne had 59 tackles, three tackles for loss, one interception, four passes defended and two forced fumbles. He was named to the All-Big 12 team as an Honorable Mention. Kohl Levao is a 28 year old, 6’ 6”, 350 pound backup offensive lineman. He graduated from the University of Hawaii and spent time with the San Antonio Brahmas in the USFL prior to signing a futures contract with the Jets in 2025. Levao was signed to the Jets active roster on October 1, 2026 after spending time with the Jets practice squad. Levao made his NFL debut with the Jets this season, playing 15 snaps across four games, all on special teams.

full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images Jets tackle Armand Membou slammed his helmet down in frustration during the Week 9 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, and he was flagged for it in real time. Now the NFL has also assessed a $14,926 fine on Membou for unsportsmanlike conduct for the same action. The penalty occurred with about 7:20 remaining in the game. Membou got beat by Chiefs DT Chris Jones, who got to Geno Smith for a 6-yard sack. After the play, Membou was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct for slamming down his helmet in frustration. The sack and the unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on Membou led to a Jets punt. Bruh, I HAVE NEVER SEEN ARMAND MEMBOU GO OFF LIKE THIS! That is pure frustration with what is happening out there on the field. My goodness! I hope the #Jets can keep it together long enough to find the right head coach, with a good staff and get things on track! #JetUp pic.twitter.com/Z98d4rkuIO — The Long Beach Joe Show (@TheLongBeachJoe) November 10, 2026 The Jets went on to lose the matchup 35-12. This is Membou’s first fine of the season and of his young career. It’s Membou’s second season in the NFL after being drafted by the Jets in the first round of the 2025 NFL draft. No Kansas City Chiefs players were fined for any plays against the Jets. The NFL splits the money it collects from player discipline between the NFLPA’s efforts to support retired players, the NFL Foundation, and nonprofit organizations supporting kids sports leagues, community health initiatives, and player health and safety at every level of sports.

title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Buffalo Bills
summary: The last time the Jets faced the Buffalo Bills, they lost 35-8 despite the fact that the Bills were resting all of their starters. New York has a stronger team right now than they had at the end of last year, but there’s still a big gulf between them and the 7-1 Bills. On Sunday, […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 14: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills waits for the play call during the first quarter against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on September 14, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The last time the Jets faced the Buffalo Bills, they lost 35-8 despite the fact that the Bills were resting all of their starters. New York has a stronger team right now than they had at the end of last year, but there’s still a big gulf between them and the 7-1 Bills. On Sunday, the Jets will be heavy underdogs as the Bills seek to continue setting the pace in the race for the AFC’s number one seed. Let’s break down the Bills’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks With Josh Allen once again leading the way, the Bills have the league’s number one offense in terms of points and yardage. Allen has been solid, but his numbers are not as impressive as in some of his previous seasons. He hasn’t thrown for 300 yards since the opener and his quarterback rating is below 100. He’s also thrown six interceptions in the past six games, which is uncharacteristic for a player who had just 16 interceptions in his past 43 regular season and playoff games prior to this. He does have a career-best (and league-leading) yards per attempt average of 8.6 though. The backup is veteran Kyle Allen, who is 7-12 as a starter in his career. Offensive Line The only change on the offensive line this year for the Bills is that Alec Anderson has replaced David Edwards at left guard. The other four starters remain from a group that all started at least 15 regular or postseason games last year. The versatile Anderson had also played over 200 snaps off the bench. The other four starters include five-time pro bowler Dion Dawkins at left tackle and 2024 pro bowler Connor McGovern at center. On the right side, tackle Spencer Brown and guard O’Cyrus Torrence round out the starting group. The Bills have been banged up on the line, though. Dawkins and Anderson missed their last game against the Vikings on Monday night football, Brown missed practice on Thursday and McGovern was also limited in practice. Spencer has been listed as doubtful, but the other four starters are due to play. On the bench, the Bills have Tyler Grable, who has started a game at each tackle position this year and veteran Austin Corbett who started in place of Anderson on Sunday. The backup center is Lloyd Cushenberry and they also have two rookies – fourth rounder Jude Bowry and seventh rounder Ar’maj Reed-Adams. Running Backs The Bills have the number two running game in the NFL, led by James Cook, who is averaging over 100 rushing yards per game. Cook has also rushed for eight touchdowns, although that’s actually one less than Allen. Backup Ray Davis hasn’t featured much but should be confident having had a monster game against the Jets in January. The third down back is still ex-Jet Ty Johnson who has really found himself a home with the Bills. Johnson has 17 receptions off the bench. Pass catchers The Bills’ biggest star at wide receiver is DJ Moore, but he’s been slowed by injuries since posting a 100-yard game in the season opener. Instead, they’ve been led by Khalil Shakir, who has 31 catches. Keon Coleman has also contributed with 23 receptions and a team-high three touchdown catches. Tight end Dalton Kincaid leads the Bills in receiving yards with 429 as Dawson Knox, a 2022 pro bowler, continues to play second fiddle. The other backups at wide receiver – fourth round rookie Skyler Bell and ex-Jets return specialist Greg Dortch – have yet to register a catch. Reserve tight ends Jackson Hawes and Keleki Latu have just three catches between them, but Latu’s only reception was a 25-yard touchdown. Defensive Line New defensive coordinator and ex-Jets safety Jim Leonhard has switched the Bills’ defense to a 3-4 system this year and they’re in the middle of the pack overall but actually strong against the run and weak against the pass, statistically. The massive Deone Walker has arguably been the biggest beneficiary of the scheme change on the interior, continuing to emerge as a disruptive pass rusher in addition to the space he takes up against the run. He’s also batted down five passes at the line. The other two starters are Ed Oliver and TJ Sanders, although they’ve missed seven games between them so backups Greg Gaines, DeWayne Carter and Landon Jackson have all also seen extensive playing time. Oliver has been productive when he has played, with 10 quarterback hits in just five games. Linebackers Whether it was due to the scheme change or because he was just due to break out anyway, 2026 has been the year that Gregory Rousseau has taken his game to a new level coming off the edge. Rousseau, who led the team with seven sacks last year, already has eight sacks in eight games to tie his career high. In addition, he has eight passes defensed which more than doubles the most he has ever had in a season. Otherwise, Buffalo doesn’t have anyone with two sacks, although the other starting edge, Bradley Chubb, has 1.5 sacks and eight quarterback hits. The starters inside are Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard. Bernard plays a full-time role and leads the team with 57 tackles but Williams has two interceptions to lead the team. Fourth round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr has also seen action in coverage situations. Veteran Michael Hoecht and second round rookie TJ Parker are the main backups on the edge, with Javon Solomon and Mike Danna having not played much. Joe Andresseen has only played on special teams so far, but is the number four inside linebacker. Defensive Backs The Bills’ number one cornerback is Christian Benford but the other starter has been a surprise package. Second round rookie Davison Igbinosun currently leads the team with nine pass breakups. In the slot, the Bills let longtime slot cornerback Taron Johnson go during the offseason and replaced him with another experienced player in Dee Alford. Last year’s first round pick Maxwell Hairston has still received plenty of playing time on the outside but is behind the rookie right now. He may need to step up this week because Benford is listed as questionable with a wrist injury despite practicing full on Friday. The starting safeties are Damar Hamlin and Cole Bishop. CJ Gardner-Johnson had been starting but was released after getting suspended following a controversial spitting incident. Sam Franklin and fifth round rookie Jalon Kilgore are available as cover at safety, as is Amani Hooker, who was just acquired via trade. Te’Cory Couch is also on the roster as cornerback cover. Special Teams After missing the entire 2025 season due to injury, Tyler Bass is having a stellar 2026 season as he has made all 19 of his field goal attempts, including a game-winner against the Rams. He has missed two extra points though. Their punter is a rookie, seventh rounder Tommy Doman. So far, his numbers are underwhelming but he hasn’t allowed much in the way of return yardage. Davis, who was an all-pro kick returner a few years ago, splits kickoff return duties with Dortch, who is also the main punt returner. Davis had a 70-yarder and Dortch had a 58-yarder so far on kickoffs. Alford and Shakir are also options on punts and Johnson is the third-stringer on kickoffs. Andreessen, Franklin and Hoecht have been Buffalo’s most productive players in kick coverage. Andreessen was second in the league with 23 special teams tackles last season. Franklin is their primary punt gunner, although he has been listed as questionable with a shoulder issue.

title: Three Things I’m Looking At for the Jets vs Bills Game
summary: One of these days we’ll have a ‘Sunday fun day’ as Jets fans, but it probably won’t be this one. The 7-1 Bills have won four straight games and are coming to MetLife Stadium to face the 2-7 New York Jets, who have lost four straight. Jets coach Aaron Glenn claims the Jets are ‘on […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 14: Jowon Briggs #91 of the New York Jets attempts to tackle Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills during the second quarter at MetLife Stadium on September 14, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of these days we’ll have a ‘Sunday fun day’ as Jets fans, but it probably won’t be this one. The 7-1 Bills have won four straight games and are coming to MetLife Stadium to face the 2-7 New York Jets, who have lost four straight. Jets coach Aaron Glenn claims the Jets are ‘on the cusp’ of miraculously winning games despite leading for 0 seconds against a Dolphins team that hadn’t had a lead all season and hasn’t won a game since the Jets. All indications for this one are brutal. The Jets’ current losing streak has been by an average of 9.5 points per game, while the Bills’ winning streak has been by an average of 12.3 points per game. Specifically, this Jets/Bills matchup in the Aaron Glenn era is way worse: The Bills have won by an average of 23.5(!) points. The second matchup didn’t even include Josh Allen; he was a healthy scratch, and they still handed the Jets a 35-8 loss. Of course, it is any given Sunday, so if you’re looking for hopeful data, the Bills are winless against the AFC East this season. Yes, it was just one game, but so far, that one divisional game is the one blemish on the 2026 season. Also, before they faced Carson Wentz and the cluster of Vikings’ QBs this week, the Bills’ defense was allowing 28.5 points per game. The 2026 Jets showed they can compete in shootouts; is this the week they finally win a shootout? Probably not. But there is a chance! And for that, let’s discuss what to look for this game: Red Dead Redemption I very rarely recycle headings from the weekly previews I’ve been doing on various sites for the last 6 seasons, but this header is too good and too applicable to the current situation to leave it out. The Jets’ biggest current problem, by far, is scoring in the red zone. What makes this so frustrating is that they have no problem getting into the red zone. In these last few games, they’ve been a fantastic offense, but as soon as they cross that 20-yard line, the sacks and miscues are abundant. I mentioned heading into the Raiders game that the Jets were the only team to be in the red zone 20+ times and have fewer than 10 red zone touchdowns. At that time, that was the second-worst red zone TD percentage in the NFL. Since then, the Browns have finally reached the red zone 20+ times (23) and scored only 9 red zone touchdowns, making them the only team in the NFL with those metrics. The Jets are still second-worst, though, at a terrible 11/27 (40.7%). This also means that in the Chiefs and Raiders games specifically, the Jets were 2-7 (28.6%) in scoring touchdowns in the red zone. This does not include the two drives where the Jets got the ball in plus territory, moved it a combined -1 yard, and kicked two field goals (1/2). This is a serious problem for this talented unit. The revelation of the Average Separation Score from Fantasy Points Data has changed how I view this phenomenon. It’s easy to blame Frank Reich because his job title is Offensive Coordinator, and I’ve already shown my appreciation for Geno Smith , but when the top three receivers creating separation this season all belong to the Jets and the Jets offense is still struggling, something is clearly amiss. Michael Nania of Jets X-Factor had a great film breakdown of Omar Cooper Jr. getting open but not being targeted and gave Frank Reich credit without discrediting Geno. Allow me to be the first to seriously question Geno’s vision and ability to make the right read at the right time. This isn’t me saying he’s making bad reads; he’s clearly having a solid year with a 67.5% completion and only three picks, but could he be making better reads? Given the film breakdowns I’ve seen and how open the Jets’ receivers have been, it’s fair to blame Geno Smith. Reich has done his job of getting guys open; can Geno hit the right guy at the right time to put points on the board? Preferably 6s instead of 3s? I’ll come to his aid again in pointing out that Adonai Mitchell caught none of his seven targets and had some bad drops. Still, since this problem has been an issue all season and not just this past game, I have to go back to the one constant. Not only is he not throwing to the open receiver, but he’s taking so long to process the field that he’s taking sacks in the red zone. Can Geno speed up his process, make the ‘right read’ over a ‘good read,’ and score TDs against a team that allows TDs on 63.3% of its defensive red zone trips? Running Train Perhaps the safest week-to-week bet any of you bettors could make is the over on the opposing RB1’s rushing yards against the Jets. Last week, Kenneth Walker’s line was 93.5, and he dominated for 102 rushing yards and three(!) total touchdowns. This week, James Cook’s line is 91.5, and he’s coming off a 107-yard performance against the Vikings. Fun fact: Cook has rushed for 75+ yards and scored a touchdown in every game besides Week 1, so I’m ready to bet the farm on 100 yards and a touchdown this Sunday. I might sprinkle some dollars on 2+ TDs as well. When will the Jets’ run defense get better? I’ve seen zero indication that the play calling or personnel will change in any way to plug the clear holes on this team. It was still an issue with T’Vondre Sweat on the field; his absence certainly isn’t helping. Maybe they can finally bounce back next week against the struggling Chargers and the likes of Omarion Hampton? Probably not. Too Legit to Quit? I have no stats for this one. This is a pure eye test that should help continue writing the story of the Aaron Glenn Era. I’ve learned there are still plenty of fans who still think Glenn can be part of the solution for this franchise. It’s been reported that the Jets operated during the trade deadline as if this were indeed a possibility, and they’re giving him every chance to prove Woody right. The final nail in the coffin, in my opinion, would be losing the players in the locker room. Sure, last year you can blame players as “bad apples” and suggest addition by subtraction with the trades of Quinnen Williams, Sauce Gardner, Jermaine Johnson, etc. Now, these are Glenn’s guys; the visible sideline frustrations of Armand Membou, Geno Smith, and Garrett Wilson are all guys who were either brought in by Glenn or extended during the Glenn era. It is no longer about bad apples; now it’s time to blame the tree. Let’s see if the players Glenn has chosen remain committed to his vision, however shaky it is. We already saw a Glenn team have no fight – the entire months of December and January last year. November would be fairly early to give up, but given the sky-high percentage of fans who’ve already given up, I wouldn’t be surprised to see the players follow suit. I’m looking for body language, sideline interactions, and, of course, general play to see how this team’s morale looks. Let’s go Jets!

title: A scoop and score is long overdue for the Jets
summary: The Jets’ defense has had its issues in 2026, to say the least. However, there’s at least one area where they have improved. The defense as a whole has been a lot more opportunistic this year in terms of forcing fumbles. Led by David Bailey’s five, they have forced a total of 13 fumbles. That’s […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 18: David Bailey #31 of the New York Jets tackles Treveyon Henderson #32 of the New England Patriots during the third quarter at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jets’ defense has had its issues in 2026, to say the least. However, there’s at least one area where they have improved. The defense as a whole has been a lot more opportunistic this year in terms of forcing fumbles. Led by David Bailey’s five, they have forced a total of 13 fumbles. That’s already four more than the total for all of last season. New York’s fumble luck has been a lot better too, as they’ve recovered 50 percent of all fumbles. This is much higher than their 2025 percentage, which was the second-worst in the league at 35 percent (and was actually on target to break the all-time record until they had a few over the last few weeks of the season). Had they been closer to 50 percent last year, or 2023 when they were dead last in fumble recovery percentage, or 2022 when they were 30th, those seasons could arguably have played out very differently. 2023 in particular was particularly galling, as the Jets started 7-4 and then lost their last six as the turnovers dried up. They almost tied the all-time NFL record for the fewest defensive fumble recoveries until Carl Lawson ended a nine-game drought by recovering one with two games remaining. In the end, they only managed to recover 21 percent of fumbles by opposing offenses. It’s often been debated how much of fumble recovery percentages are dictated by talent and how much is based on luck, with most analytical studies concluding it’s mostly luck. However, if you have a team that is hungry and hustles to the ball, has players who are particularly adept at possessing loose balls or are creating the kinds of fumbles which are more likely to be recovered by the defense, this obviously has an effect on some level. Regardless, at least the Jets have seemingly started to regress to the mean in this area. So the next question becomes when will they start to do anything impactful with these recoveries? This Thursday marked the 14th anniversary of the last time a Jets defensive player recovered a ball off the turf and returned it for a touchdown. That was Muhammad Wilkerson, on a play where Mike DeVito had forced the ball loose on a sack of Russell Wilson. That’s a pretty remarkable statistic. Although there have only been six fumble returns for touchdowns in the first nine weeks of this NFL season, the Jets averaged over eight fumble returns per decade in the 80’s, 90’s and 2000’s. Doesn’t it feel like they’re long overdue? Wilkerson’s touchdown was not actually the last defensive fumble return for a touchdown by the Jets. Jamal Adams officially owns that distinction, on a memorable play where he ripped the ball out of Daniel Jones’ hands and ran it in. He therefore didn’t recover it off the ground, so it wasn’t a conventional scoop and score. Even this was a far-too-long seven years ago. Since 2012, the Jets have also scored three other touchdowns on fumbles but two (Matt Slauson and Charone Peake) were on offense, and the other was a muffed punt recovered in the end zone by Art Maulet. Again, none of these was in the past seven years. The Jets’ last defensive touchdown was a pick-six by Jermaine Johnson and that one dates back to 2023. It feels like a scoop and score is exactly the kind of momentum-shifting play that has been lacking ever since Aaron Glenn took over as head coach. It’s the kind of thing that could give them a chance to upset a favored opponent, which is something Glenn’s team probably needs to do a couple of times between now and the end of the season if he wants to mount a strong enough case to return for a third year. With Bailey in particular doing a good job of creating these opportunities, perhaps this could be something that happens sooner rather than later. Now we’ve written about this, perhaps this will manifest a Jets fumble return for a touchdown in an upcoming game. Otherwise, we’ll be writing about how long it was since Wilkerson’s touchdown again in a few seasons…
