full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Dallas Goedert #88 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs a route during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport shared an NFL trade deadline notebook on ESPN that featured several mentions of the Philadelphia Eagles. Let’s take a look at those here. 1) Dallas Goedert drew interest from the 49ers, among other teams. Here’s what was said: While the Eagles traded stars in Davis and center Cam Jurgens in the flurry leading up to the deadline, they held off trading another player who was wanted — Dallas Goedert. Sources said several teams inquired about the pass-catching tight end, including the 49ers. But Goedert, 31, never got close to being traded. He remains in Philadelphia and could even re-sign with the Eagles for 2027. Not exactly shocking to see that teams had interest in acquiring him. Goedert is a solid tight end who could make nice contributions to a contending team. At the same time, the Eagles didn’t need to give him away for meager compensation. Especially when accounting for his salary cap ramifications . It’s interesting to see mention of the Eagles potentially keeping Goedert beyond 2026. It felt like the Eagles were close to moving on from him after each of the past two seasons. And he turns 32 in January. Are the two sides really going to do another one-year bandaid contract? Maybe. The only Eagles tight end currently under contract beyond this season is … Eli Stowers. It wouldn’t be very wise for the team to put all of their eggs in the basket of him panning out since the 2026 second-round pick has yet to show promise thus far. 2) The Bills also had interest in Jordan Davis. Here’s what was said: The two teams that were most aggressive in trading for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis were the Bills and Jaguars, who wound up trading a first- and second-round pick to the Eagles. Interested to know exactly what the Bills were offering for Davis. Nevertheless, seems like there was a bidding war for the Eagles’ interior defender, which helps to explain why Howie Roseman was able to get such a big return from the jags. 3) The Eagles aren’t happy with the Bengals. Here’s what was said: The Eagles were not pleased that the Bengals reneged on their deal for Ebiketie after learning they would lose a third-round compensatory pick […] Understandably so. The Eagles thought they had a done deal with the Bengals to ship out Ebiketie for a 2027 sixth-round pick. Before it became official, however, Cincy realized (thanks to compensatory picks expert Nick Korte) that acquiring Ebiketie would cause him to forfeit the 2027 third-round pick comp pick they were set to earn for losing Trey Hendrickson. While one can understand why the Bengals wanted to back out after realizing their mistake, this failed trade is a pretty bad look for them. I feel like the Bengals owe the Eagles one. Not exactly sure what that looks like but it’s in Cincy’s own interests to maintain healthy working relationships with other NFL general managers.

title: Howie Roseman seen chatting up one of the top quarterback draft prospects
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are on their bye this weekend and Howie Roseman is spending part of the team’s time off by attending Saturday’s college football game between Duke and the University of Miami. This isn’t necessarily a formal scouting trip for Roseman; his son, Jake, attends Duke and contributes to the Blue Devils’ football program. […]
full_text: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 07: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes celebrates a touchdown against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish during the second half at Notre Dame Stadium on November 07, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are on their bye this weekend and Howie Roseman is spending part of the team’s time off by attending Saturday’s college football game between Duke and the University of Miami. This isn’t necessarily a formal scouting trip for Roseman; his son, Jake, attends Duke and contributes to the Blue Devils’ football program. The Eagles’ general manager could be there to primarily spend time with family. That being said, it is interesting to see that Roseman was chatting it up with one of the top prospects in the 2027 NFL Draft. Here’s a video of him meeting with Miami Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah during pregame warmups: "Bring him to Philly!" Philadelphia Eagles GM Howie Roseman a little pregame love for Canes QB Darian Mensah @WPLGLocal10 pic.twitter.com/QkhiiNuepN — Kacy Hintz (@KacyHintz) November 14, 2026 Mensah (+290) currently has the second-shortest Heisman Trophy Winner odds , only behind front-runner Jeremiah Smith (+170). ESPN’s Mel Kiper recently ranked him as the seventh overall prospect and third-best quarterback in this year’s draft class. This interaction definitely means the Eagles are drafting Mensah, right? Hardly. It’s not yet clear if the redshirt junior will declare for the draft or return for another year of college football. And even if he does declare, there’s no guarantee the Eagles will take a quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft. I suspect many fans will be against that idea. But it’s fair to wonder about Jalen Hurts’ future with the organization. It’s also probably important to remember the Eagles originally drafted Hurts at a time where virtually no one expected them to do so. The Eagles are currently projected to have the fifth overall selection in the upcoming draft. There’s potential for them to move even higher in the draft order as they continue to struggle and lose games. They also have plenty of draft pick ammunition to move up the draft board, if they so desire. Whether they actually draft a quarterback? We’ll see.

(Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Will be interesting to see what, if anything, comes of this investigation into the Jalen Hurts situation. Would be nice to see some transparency about the findings. Also would be really nice to hear from Jalen himself at some point, even if just to hear him say he’s doing well in his recovery. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … NFL outlines steps in Jalen Hurts investigation in letter to senator – ESPN Independent medical experts will examine the circumstances around Jalen Hurts’ blood clots and share their findings with the NFL and NFL Players Association as part of the forthcoming joint review, according to a league executive. The NFL provided some additional details about the review as well as its protocols for tracking blood clots in response to an inquiry from U.S. Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware. “As outlined by the league and NFLPA’s Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties,” executive vice president of communications, public affairs and health policy Jeff Miller said in a statement released by Blunt Rochester’s office Friday. Eagles reportedly releasing Fred Johnson – BGN The Philadelphia Eagles continue to make moves during their bye week, the latest of which is reportedly releasing Fred Johnson. The veteran offensive tackle provided some much needed depth at tackle, and occasionally at guard, over the years, but the team decided to move forward in another direction. Can Makai Lemon Develop Into Eagles’ WR2 In The Season’s Second Half? – PHLY Eagles Podcast Will Makai Lemon develop enough to keep the Eagles from needing another first-round receiver? Will Drew Kendall or Markel Bell show enough to earn a starting spot on the offensive line for 2027? Brandon Lee Gowton and Deniz Selman go through the things still left to learn about the Eagles coming off the bye week, including a temperature check on Nick Sirianni and some leftover thoughts from Howie Roseman’s trade deadline moves and non-moves. Bye Time – Iggles Blitz The goal is to develop young talent and figure out what you have moving forward. Jonathan Greenard played well last week. You want to see more of that from him over the final eight games so you feel good about his role in 2027. Makai Lemon had 6 catches last week. He also had a pair of costly drops. You want Lemon to learn from the mistakes so that he makes the catches next year, when hopefully wins and losses are more important. The biggest goal in the bye week should be fixing the OL and pass protection. It is impossible to fairly evaluate the QBs playing in a situation where they regularly have rushers coming free at them. Give the QBs better protection and you can get a better feel for what they can truly do. That will help you to get a better feel for the TEs and WRs as well. It would also help to figure out which of the OL should be looked at as future starters. There are times now when it is tough to discern mental mistakes vs physical ability. Don’t blame the Eagles if draft position is their priority. The NFL is incentivizing a race to the bottom – Inquirer Yet, the fact remains: it would greatly behoove the Eagles to draft as high as possible. To draft No. 1 overall could rewrite their destiny in the medium-to-long-term. The difference between a short-order return to the Super Bowl and five years of mediocrity could easily be the difference between drafting No. 1 and No. 5, or even between drafting No. 2 and No. 4. This is not an exaggeration. It is not a straw man. It is reality. Howie Roseman knows it. Bet your last dollar on that. Remember the uproar in January 2021 when the Eagles pulled Jalen Hurts in the fourth quarter of their season finale against the Commanders? Remember the questions about the play-calling? The Eagles incentive on that particular day was the prospect of moving from No. 9 to No. 6. Those three spots of draft position gained them an extra first-round pick. They traded down from No. 6 to No. 12, picking up a 2022 first-rounder from the Dolphins. That 2022 first-round pick became Jordan Davis, who helped the Eagles to a pair of Super Bowls and now has landed them 2027 first- and 2029 second-round picks from the Jaguars. In hindsight, the Eagles would have been committing organizational malpractice had they not done everything within the letter of the law to maximize their chances of drafting at No. 6 in 2021. This year, the potential reward is even greater. How did the Eagles become one of the NFL’s worst running teams? – NBCSP How did the Eagles become one of the NFL’s worst running teams? When the Eagles talk about finding their identity, it usually means, “We have to start running the ball because we can’t pass protect and our quarterbacks aren’t playing well, anyway.” And lately the Eagles have been talking about finding their identity, but this year they can’t run the ball either. Nine games into the season, the Eagles aren’t just one of the worst in the NFL throwing the ball – 29th in passing yards per game, last in passing yards per play – they’re one of the worst running it, too. Bad combination. The Eagles are rushing for only 88.6 yards per game and 3.7 yards per carry. Both are 28th in the league. Both are also their worst through nine games since 2005, when they were averaging 3.6 yards per carry and 72 rushing yards through nine games and 2nd-worst since 1991 (2.8, 76.4). Eagles legend Brandon Graham live tapes podcast, talks football at Rowan – Rowan University Former Philadelphia Eagles defensive end and two-time Super Bowl Champion Brandon Graham brought his PHLY weekly podcast, “Brandon Graham Unblocked,” to Rowan University for a live taping of its most recent episode. Organized by the Center for Sports Communication & Social Impact, this marked the first time the podcast taped outside of the studio and its first time in front of a collegiate audience. Graham and co-host Bo Wulf, an Eagles insider, discussed the team’s chances of making the playoffs, their picks for this week’s NFL games and leadership moments in Graham’s career. A focal point of the episode was the recent trade announcement of Eagles’ defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars. On that and several other team topics, Wulf gauged the crowd’s opinions by asking for cheers or boos—which the hundreds in attendance enthusiastically offered. Jaguars vs Titans: Injury Report Ahead of Week 10 – Big Cat Country Trade acquisitions Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis also sat out for rest and have already been declared out this week. Cam Skattebo reveals the junk food that made him barf during Giants-Commanders – SB Nation It’s flu season, and a lot of people are catching stuff going around right now — so the concern was understandable. The wild card was that Skattebo’s reaction to barfing wasn’t exactly normal. The running back was seemingly laughing about the fact he blew chunks on the bench, and appeared to wave off team doctors when they wanted to check him out. After the game he revealed that it wasn’t illness, or nerves that got the best of him — but a pretzel dog. New York Giants mailbag: Kickoff rule, Rasul Douglas interception, more – Big Blue View I wrote earlier in the week that the Giants should try to capitalize on the opportunity they have in the NFC East. You don’t know if or when that opportunity will come again. They did try to do that. They were very aggressive. They were also careful. I said earlier in the week there was a price they should not go to — meaning they should not go above…

While the receiver room has a bleak outlook right now, one of the Steelers’ highest paid receivers seems […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers made no trades ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, despite a clear need at wide receiver. Although the Steelers were interested in Tennessee’s Calvin Ridley and Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr., a trade never materialized. While the receiver room has a bleak outlook right now, one of the Steelers’ highest paid receivers seems close to making his return from injured reserve. Steelers veteran wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. has been out since Week 4 after suffering a plantar fasciitis injury. Still, it seems like his return could come sooner rather than later. “It feels good, and today was probably my best day yet,” Pittman told Brendan Howe of Steelers Now on Thursday. “Yesterday was good, today was even better, so definitely trending the right way.… I would love the opportunity to play this week, but that’s out of my control. I definitely let them know today that I thought it was good.” Pittman Jr. remains on injured reserve, with the Steelers yet to open his 21-day practice window. The receiver was seen working off to the side this week and even ran during warmups. Although Pittman Jr. will be out this week against Cincinnati, the receiver feels healthy enough to go. The Steelers acquired Pittman Jr. in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts this past March. The receiver has appeared in just three games so far this season, recording seven catches for 89 yards in those contests. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers activate DT Derrick Harmon off injured reserve
summary: One of Pittsburgh’s best run defenders is back to help bolster an already successful defensive line. The Steelers announced on Saturday afternoon that defensive tackle Derrick Harmon has been activated off injured reserve. Cornerback Terrell Smith was waived to create room on the 53-man roster. Harmon is still listed as questionable ahead of the Steelers’ […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images One of Pittsburgh’s best run defenders is back to help bolster an already successful defensive line. The Steelers announced on Saturday afternoon that defensive tackle Derrick Harmon has been activated off injured reserve. Cornerback Terrell Smith was waived to create room on the 53-man roster. Harmon is still listed as questionable ahead of the Steelers’ Week 10 matchup, but his activation is a good sign for his availability. Harmon suffered a foot injury in the first half of the Steelers’ loss at Cleveland on Thursday, Oct. 1. He was placed on IR and missed the next five weeks (four games). His last full game was against the Bengals on Sept. 27. In four games, Harmon logged 12 tackles, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one sack. The 2025 first-round pick is a significant component of Pittsburgh’s run defense, a unit that gave up an average of over 80 yards more on the ground last year (five games) when Harmon was out of the lineup. This season, regardless of whether Harmon has played, the Steelers are a top-five unit. Patrick Graham’s defense is allowing 83.9 rushing yards per game, third in the NFL. The Steelers only allowed 100 yards once in his absence. Harmon returns for arguably the biggest game in the AFC this season as the Steelers face the Bengals on Sunday Night Football. The winner will hold sole possession of first place in the AFC North and the Steelers would own a two-game lead in Cincinnati after sweeping the season series against their rival.

full_text: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are set to take on the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football for sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Whoever comes out of Paycor Stadium with a victory on primetime will have the inside track to win the division. With the stakes as high as they are, an underrated storyline in the contest is how the Friday mandatory ground stop on Friday will impact the referee crew for the Steelers vs. Bengals showdown. Longtime side judge Don Willard is working an unprecedented schedule due to travel problems. He will serve as the head referee for the Colts matchup against the Dolphins in Indianapolis on at 1 pm. After the conclusion of that game, Willard will make the drive to Cincinnati for Sunday Night Football, where he will also serve as the head referee. NFL referee Don Willard will officiate two games in one day because of travel delays from the FAA's ground stop. Ref Dolphins-Colts at 1 p.m. in Indianapolis Drive 110 miles to Cincinnati Ref Steelers-Bengals at 8:20 p.m. pic.twitter.com/yf3MV2QjaC — Front Office Sports (@FOS) November 14, 2026 The usual crew that Willard usually works with is not scheduled to work at all this weekend. The longtime side judge will step into a major role for two separate games on Sunday. While the league has had to make major changes to officiating crews for Sunday, it does not seem that the ground stoppage will have a major effect on any teams travels plans. Last night, Steelers director of communications Burt Lauten suggested that the team was considering bussing to Cincinnati. At the time of this writing, there is no update as to whether the Steelers will fly or drive to Cincinnati after the ground stoppage was lifted late last night. full_text: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the college football regular season winding down, some are beginning to turn their attention to the top NFL Draft prospects and beginning a long stretch of predictions and mock drafts. Dalton Wasserman of PFF released a post-trade deadline mock draft, where he has the Pittsburgh Steelers selecting Miami quarterback Darian Mensah. “Mensah has been college football’s most efficient quarterback this season, leading the FBS with a 76.8% completion rate while throwing 28 touchdown passes and just two interceptions,” Wassermann writes . “That level of efficiency should appeal to NFL franchises, though questions remain about his physical tools and whether he can maintain that level of play without star wide receiver Malachi Toney, who is sidelined by injury.” Mensah is completing roughly 77 percent of his passes, which leads the FBS. He’s thrown 28 touchdowns to just two interceptions this season. The Steelers drafted Drew Allar out of Penn State this past April in the third round, and kept both Allar and 2025 sixth-round pick Will Howard on the 53-man roster for the season. Should Pittsburgh select Mensah, or any other quarterback in the first round for that matter, it would all but certainly spell the end of the road for Allar and/or Howard. full_text: The Seattle Seahawks (5-4) have won three of their four games against AFC opposition, and their final one is against a longtime AFC West rival from yesteryear. Klint Kubiak left the Seattle Seahawks after winning the Super Bowl as offensive coordinator, and so far he’s got the Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) reasonably in the playoff hunt. Just a year ago under Pete Carroll and Geno Smith, the Raiders were 3-14, so this is already an upgrade in performance. Of course, the big story of the week is not just Kubiak facing his old team, but now it’s Kubiak facing his old team with his No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza, making his first career NFL start . The Raiders traded Kirk Cousins back to the Minnesota Vikings , which paved the way for the former Indiana star to get promoted to QB1 midseason. While Mendoza will have the awesome Brock Bowers to throw to, he won’t have the luxury of an effective run game or a top-flight defense to help him in his development this season. Seattle has opportunities to exploit the Raiders’ worst-ranked rushing offense and worst-ranked scoring defense, and it will have some of its key guys back. Drew Lock once again starts for the injured Sam Darnold, but he’ll have Rashid Shaheed back in the lineup. On defense, Uchenna Nwosu returns after missing two games with an ankle injury. The likes of Leonard Williams, Charles Cross, and Quenton Nelson won’t be seen until after the bye. It’s a must-win for Seattle to stay afloat in the playoff hunt. full_text: It’s been a hectic weekend for airline travel after apparent equipment issues resulted in a nationwide ground stop on Friday. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) did lift the order after four hours, but the resulting chaos was thousands of canceled and rescheduled flights, which continued into Saturday. Luckily, while college sports were significantly impacted by the sudden travel issues, the Seattle Seahawks were able to head to Las Vegas to take on the Raiders as originally scheduled. The Seahawks are en route to Las Vegas right now as planned, so no changes to their travel schedule. — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) November 14, 2026 It sure helps to have a charter flight in this scenario. For shorter trips like Seattle to Las Vegas, the Seahawks will typically travel on a Saturday, whereas cross-country trips like their Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders have involved Friday departures. The NFL is probably fortunate that not a single Week 10 Sunday matchup has a Pacific Time Zone team playing in the Eastern Time Zone (or vice versa). College football and basketball games were rescheduled throughout the country as a result of Friday’s outage, with the Washington Huskies men’s basketball matchup with Utah postponed outright to December due to additional travel problems . Huskies football did fly to Michigan on Friday night but still had their kickoff against Michigan State moved back by an hour. The NFL didn’t come away from the travel nightmare unscathed, as several games will have makeshift officiating crews. Side judge Don Willard will be the head referee for the Miami Dolphins and Indianapolis Colts at 10 am PT, then drive to Cincinnati to ref the Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football at 5:20 pm PT. Unfortunately, some fans hoping to go to Vegas for a weekend to catch some Seahawks football had their dreams dashed, as we documented on Friday .

title: Why Seahawks vs. Raiders is a Jarran Reed showcase game after trade interest
summary: Seattle Seahawks defensive lineman Jarran Reed has had an interesting week. He may not be the CEO of Nvidia, but he is a manager of violence. He got trade buzz at the trade deadline, but nothing happened. Reed was away from proactive this week, due to a “personal issue.” Was he mad about the trade […]
full_text: Seattle Seahawks defensive lineman Jarran Reed has had an interesting week. He may not be the CEO of Nvidia, but he is a manager of violence. What does it mean to be the "Manager of Violence"? Jarran Reed explains how the #Seahawks defense's motto ended up on t-shirts and why it is one of this favorites on with @TheMikeSalk . https://t.co/eif2mukIdc pic.twitter.com/6ipbTUEIdV — Seattle Sports (@SeattleSports) July 31, 2026 He got trade buzz at the trade deadline, but nothing happened. Reed was away from proactive this week, due to a “ personal issue .” Was he mad about the trade rumors? Was it the birth of a baby? Mike Macdonald said it was a “good” personal issue. We may never know! Either way, it is a lot of drama for a 3rd-string DT, who is standing in the way of more playing time for young player, Rylie Mills. What’s going on with Jarran Reed? Was in trade rumors for some bizarre reason and is now not practicing…. — Mike Macdonald’s Golf Swing (@CoachMike12s) November 13, 2026 Why was his name in the news? There may be some clues when we look at the patterns of the National Football League. Let’s go over all of the buzz that defensive tackles have been receiving 0ver the course of the 2026 NFL season. New Money Jalen Carter – Got $106M guaranteed Quinnen Williams – Got $101M guaranteed Leonard Williams – Got $30M per year average, among the top 5 highest paid DT’s Vita Vea – Got $30M one-year extension as a nose tackle Trades Jeffrey Simmons – Was traded for two 1st-Round picks + a 4th for a 5th, AND $100M guaranteed earlier in the season Davon Godchaux – Was traded for a conditional 6th-Round pick Jordan Davis – Was traded for a 1st and a 2nd-Round pick DeForest Buckner – Was traded for a 4th-Round pick To put this all into perspective, five of the top six highest-paid DT’s in the league were ones that got new money this year, the 2026 NFL season. Interior defensive linemen were, arguably, the number one position as trade targets this year. Three of the top four teams with the highest Super Bowl odds traded for an IDL this year. Derrick Brown of the Panthers would’ve likely joined this list if the NFC South didn’t feel absolutely wide open this year. This is not just a recent trend. View Link Jarran Reed is obviously not on the same level as Jeffrey Simmons, but, according to PFF, has 6 more pressures on 55 fewer snaps, when compared to Jordan Davis. Is it plausible that the Seattle Seahawks could have let their willingness to engage in negotiations leak, when they saw the DT craze taking hold across the league? Ultimately, it didn’t happen, as Seattle must’ve seen a potential move as not worth it. Reed is a veteran leader , who is VERY well respected in the Seattle Seahawks’ locker room. He is the lone remaining vestige of a former “Legion of Boom” roster that is still around, and he may have a chance to show why in the City of Sin. Leonard Williams is out for a second straight game. Reed should get plenty of work alongside Byron Muphy II. Mills and Brandon Pili should be on hand to relieve those two. I wouldn’t be shocked if this was Reed’s biggest game of the current campaign. Next year (’27) will be the first year in three years that Reed’s salary cap hit will exceed his dead cap charge (according to Spotrac ), making him an obvious cut candidate at 34 years of age (distressing as it is for all my fellow millennials, ancient, in NFL terms). Can he latch on as a contributor somewhere else next year, to keep his NFL career going? One more contract could be a helluva motivator for the veteran DT in Vegas this weekend. Assuming that the FAA allows it to happen.

The Canadian Football League’s 113th Grey Cup will be contested between the Edmonton Elks and Montreal Alouettes, with Edmonton seeking a first Grey Cup since 2015, while the Alouettes are vying for redemption after losing last year’s Grey Cup to the Saskatchewan Roughriders, in part because they fumbled a possible tying TD at the goal line. Are there notable former Seahawks players involved? Not anyone who’s ever played a regular season game in a Seattle uniform. But maybe a few of these names are familiar to anyone who’s deeply watched preseason and training camp from the Pete Carroll years. Joel Dublanko, LB, Edmonton Elks Dublanko is a native of Aberdeen, Washington, but he counts as a Canadian domestic player instead of an import due to his grandparents and father. He was with Seattle’s preseason roster in 2022, predominantly working on special teams but also competing for a spot as a reserve linebacker. Dublanko had some spring football stints before joining the CFL as the top Canadian draft pick in 2024, and he’s not looked back ever since. Dublanko recorded a couple of sacks, fumble recoveries, and an interception in 2026. Whether it’s the playoffs or regular season, I know the BC Lions are sick of seeing Dublanko this year. title: Seahawks elevate two practice squad veterans ahead of Raiders game
summary: Although the Seattle Seahawks are set to be without several key starters against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10, they’ll get some much needed depth from two experienced veterans. The Seahawks elevated cornerback Trevon Diggs and offensive tackle Bobby Hart from the practice squad for Sunday’s game against the Raiders, they announced on Saturday. […]
full_text: Although the Seattle Seahawks are set to be without several key starters against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10, they’ll get some much needed depth from two experienced veterans. The Seahawks elevated cornerback Trevon Diggs and offensive tackle Bobby Hart from the practice squad for Sunday’s game against the Raiders, they announced on Saturday . Both players already have suited up for Seattle this season. It marks the third (and final) consecutive elevation for Hart, who’s served as a depth piece behind swing tackle Josh Jones while OT Charles Cross continues to recover from a high ankle sprain he suffered in the team’s Week 7 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs. As for Diggs, he’s in line to make his fifth appearance of the year, with his last having come against the Kansas City Chiefs — where the longtime cornerback logged just six defensive snaps. With both Devon Witherspoon and Nehemiah Pritchett healthy, he’s once again unlikely to see a significant role, barring an injury. Despite both having made multiple appearances this season, neither has made a noticeable impact. The veteran lineman played his first three snaps of the season against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 and Diggs has recorded just one tackle across 27 defensive snaps. Given the Seahawks are also poised to be without QB Sam Darnold (quad, ribs), OG Quenton Nelson (knee) and DT Leonard Williams (stinger), it’s unclear why they opted to activate Diggs rather than add depth at a more significant position of need — especially considering there were several players waiting in the wings. While Seattle’s practice squad includes options at each position, none have spent an extended amount of the time with the team. The Seahawks signed OG Cordell Volson on Thursday, DT Cole Brevard two days prior and QB Adrian Martinez on Nov. 4, making it plausible the team didn’t feel any could make as much of an impact as a player like Diggs.

full_text: The Seattle Seahawks have one more game before their bye week, traveling to Nevada to play the Las Vegas Raiders. It’s the first time the Seahawks have played a regular season game in Las Vegas, and all eyes will be on No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza and how he fares against the vaunted Seattle defense. Klint Kubiak will also be tasked with solving his former team’s defense. Just like in the late 1990s through 2001, the Seahawks and Raiders will square off on CBS. There’s only one game being shown locally on CBS this weekend, with most of the country seeing the Kansas City Chiefs take on the Atlanta Falcons. It looks as if a good chunk of America will still be seeing Seahawks-Raiders, particularly markets like Minneapolis, Green Bay/Milwaukee, Cleveland, and other cities in which the hometown team is playing at 10 am PT on FOX and therefore don’t want a CBS game in the corresponding time slot. If you’re in the blue areas of this 506 Sports map, you’ll get Seahawks vs. Raiders at 1:05 pm PT. A note for folks in Alaska that Anchorage will be getting Chiefs-Falcons, whereas Fairbanks gets the Seahawks. Hawaiian Hawk fans, I have some bad news… Seahawks vs. Raiders broadcast map Ian Eagle and Ross Tucker, the B-team at CBS behind Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt, will be on the call from Las Vegas, with Evan Washburn as the sideline reporter. Tucker was promoted to B-team status after Watt replaced Tony Romo on lead broadcasts. title: NFL predictions: 4 game picks for intriguing Seahawks vs. Raiders matchup
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are hitting the road for the first time in a month to renew their former AFC West rivalry with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday for another must-win game. Seattle enters the game as 6.5-point favorites on the road, their second straight week being favored by FanDuel Sportsbook. While the Seahawks are […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are hitting the road for the first time in a month to renew their former AFC West rivalry with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday for another must-win game. Seattle enters the game as 6.5-point favorites on the road, their second straight week being favored by FanDuel Sportsbook . While the Seahawks are large favorites, they’ll depend on their dominant defense to get the job done yet again as their inconsistent offense is still quite injured. Seattle’s “Dark Side” defense will welcome the Raiders’ first overall pick, Fernando Mendoza, to the NFL and hope to slow Klint Kubiak’s offense, which is averaging 26.4 points per game. Here are four bets/game picks to consider ahead of Sunday’s game. 1. Jadarian Price anytime touchdown (+190) While Seattle’s rookie running back has battled injuries this season, it’s still hard to believe that he’s yet to find the end zone. Price has shown the most juice of any Seahawks running back and emerged as a receiving threat last week against the Cardinals. With Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock still hampered by injuries, Price is likely to get a lot of work in the passing and running game against a struggling Raiders defense. Las Vegas’ defense has allowed large receiving days to running backs this season, with the worst coming against the Buffalo Bills when back James Cook totaled 58 yards on three catches. While it might be hard to envision betting on the Seahawks offense after they only hung 17 on the Cardinals, a second week with Lock as the leading man should lead to a more complete game plan, allowing them to score and make a statement. 2. Maxx Crosby to record a sack (+144) With Charles Cross out and Abe Lucas struggling this season, there’s a near guarantee that the Raiders’ star pass rusher will be active in the Seahawks backfield on Sunday. Crosby leads the Raiders with four sacks, and while he hasn’t quite been in game-wrecking self this season, he shouldn’t need to be to get home against an injured Lock. 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 89.5 receiving yards (-114) Coming off his quietest outing of the year, there’s no question that Smith-Njigba should be more involved with the Seahawks offense this week. JSN has totaled over 100 yards in all, but two of his games this season and has padded his total against poor secondaries, which should include Las Vegas’ unit. While I already mentioned this in the Price prop, I’ll say it again: the Raiders’ defense is not good. Las Vegas secondary gives up an average of 234 passing yards per game, one of the worst marks in the league. Even though Lock is still dealing with an injury, JSN should be so open on Sunday he’ll only need half an arm to get it to him. 4. Seahawks -6.5 (-110) Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald is undefeated against quarterbacks making their first start, and there’s no reason this game should be different. Mendoza has limited reps as a starter and is getting thrown to the wolves against a Seahawks defense that is riding high after holding an NFC West rival to just three points last week. Lock and the Seahawks’ offense may struggle early, but there is simply too much star power for the Raiders defense to handle. Las Vegas’ defense has thrived on turnovers, so Seattle will need another turnover-free game from Lock and Price like they got last week. If the Seahawks’ offense can stay clean there’s no doubt the defense will handle Mendoza and allow the Seahawks to handle the Raiders with ease. full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Corliss Waitman #7 and Eddy Pineiro #18 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrate Pineiro's 59-yard field goal against the Las Vegas Raiders in the fourth quarter of their preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 18-12. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images After his father’s death, 49ers’ Corliss Waitman found purpose amid his pain (paywall) “In 2013, Waitman, a senior at Milton (Fla.) High School, was being recruited by Oregon and Auburn, two years after the Ducks and Tigers played in the national championship game. But he passed on the bluebloods. His heart was set on a startup: the University of South Alabama, which began playing football in 2009. Waitman’s dad, Jose, played basketball at South Alabama before embarking on a 15-season professional career in Europe. In 1987, he was named MVP of a Dutch league. Jose Waitman, 6-foot-9 and 220 pounds during his playing days, was a towering presence in Corliss’ life. He died at 48 on April 17, 2013, when Corliss was 17. Months later, Corliss sent an email to a coach at a fledgling program a year removed from a 2-11 season that didn’t know he was interested. He asked if the staff could recruit him. “I went to South Alabama,” Corliss said, “solely to honor my dad.” …In the months that followed, Corliss, alone, began climbing a fence to enter Milton’s locked stadium to practice punting. “His efforts and commitment to football changed dramatically,” Marsh said. “It just kind of lit a fire into him. He was dealing with a lot of grief, but I think he made a commitment to being the very best he could be.”.. …When his parents divorced, Corliss spent summers with his father. He eventually left the Netherlands to live with Jose full time. He and his mother, Adolfine Chaar, agreed that Corliss — a gifted, highly emotional athlete with an inconsistent work ethic — could benefit from Jose’s firm guidance and exacting standards. Asked about Jose’s tough-love approach when it came to athletics, Corliss smiled and offered an example. He used to run wildly around soccer fields to celebrate individually when he scored goals. Jose put a stop to that: Always celebrate with your teammates. Watch Waitman the next time he drops a punt inside the 10-yard line. The lesson stuck. “My mom thought it would be good to have my dad more in my life to kind of push me and get me mentally more ready for what might be ahead — to kind of get the engine going,” Waitman said. “It was great. He was really hard on me and helped shape me into the man I am today.” ….Looking back, Waitman says he struggled to process his emotions that followed his father’s death. At 17, however, it did provide the first sense that time was fleeting and his chances to realize his athletic potential weren’t limitless. Without his dad, he also felt a responsibility to finish the work that they’d started together. And then there was his fury at life’s unfairness. “It kind of made me angry and I used some of that to just start working harder in sports, which is not necessarily a healthy thing to do,” Waitman said. “But it did make me a better punter.” …Waitman, a regular in the 49ers’ postgame prayer huddles, credits his faith for his outlook. But he hasn’t found answers to the questions that followed his father’s death. Does everything happen for a reason? He’s not sure why he lost his dad at 17. “I feel that everything that’s happened helped get me to here,” Waitman said. “I wish some things were different, but I don’t feel like every single thing that happened has to be explained. I just have to deal with it, keep pushing and trying to inspire people.” Lack of 49ers roster moves hints at Week 10 status for top three CBs vs. Cowboys “The 49ers are expecting their three top cornerbacks to be available Sunday to face the Dallas Cowboys. The 49ers on Saturday did not make any roster moves to bolster their depth in the defensive backfield.” Report: 49ers rookie DT Gracen Halton undergoes surgery, expected back for OTAs “Despite the significant injury, Halton is expected to be back in time for the team’s organized team activities (OTAs), offering some encouraging news about his recovery timeline.” 49ers checked in on veteran Eagles tight end; Mac Jones asking price was too rich for the Vikings “The 49ers must feel pretty confident that Jones will sign a big enough contract this offseason to net the team at least a third-round compensatory pick. If you’re the 49ers, it’s wise to make a team you could face in the playoffs overpay for a quarterback. It might have been a different story if another team had inquired about Jones.”

full_text: San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle C.J. West (99) reacts after sacking Indianapolis Colts quarterback Philip Rivers (17) on Monday, Dec. 22, 2025, during a game at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The San Francisco 49ers were a bit quiet with their roster news for Saturday. They made no practice squad elevations ahead of their game against the Dallas Cowboys. That means Cornerback Nate Hobbs and Defensive lineman C.J. West have been downgraded to out. So it’s another week on injured reserve for the two of them. Hobbs staying on IR could be good for cornerbacks Renardo Green, Upton Stout, and Deommodore Lenoir’s status. Per Adam Schefter, he’s expected back for OTAs in 2027 .

title: 49ers checked in on veteran Eagles tight end; Mac Jones asking price was too rich for the Vikings
summary: Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport had a trade notebook, recapping everything related to the deadline. In the article, there’s a section dedicated to San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback Mac Jones: The San Francisco 49ers left no doubt how much they value quarterback Mac Jones. When the Vikings called San Francisco as part of due diligence […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport had a trade notebook , recapping everything related to the deadline. In the article, there’s a section dedicated to San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback Mac Jones: The San Francisco 49ers left no doubt how much they value quarterback Mac Jones . When the Vikings called San Francisco as part of due diligence in their search for a quarterback, sources told ESPN that Niners general manager John Lynch informed Minnesota brass that it would take a second-round pick and more for Jones. Perhaps a second-rounder and a middle-round pick might have gotten a trade done. Instead, because of the high cost associated with the veteran quarterback, the conversations ended there and Jones remains a valued member of the 49ers. This was not the first time the teams had spoken about Jones in a possible trade and not the first time San Francisco had set a price that high. Niners coach Kyle Shanahan views Jones as a franchise-caliber quarterback and would trade him only for a deal they had no choice but to accept. To add to that value, Jones won four of his first five starts in place of the injured Brock Purdy last year despite battling injuries of his own and ended up with a 5-3 record and a QB rating of 97.4 for the season. In the final year of his two-year, $8.41 million contract, Jones is a free agent after the season. The 49ers must feel pretty confident that Jones will sign a big enough contract this offseason to net the team at least a third-round compensatory pick. If you’re the 49ers, it’s wise to make a team you could face in the playoffs overpay for a quarterback. It might have been a different story if another team had inquired about Jones. Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert was on the 49ers’ radar: While the Eagles traded stars in Davis and center Cam Jurgens in the flurry leading up to the deadline, they held off trading another player who was wanted — Dallas Goedert . Sources said several teams inquired about the pass-catching tight end, including the 49ers. But Goedert, 31, never got close to being traded. He remains in Philadelphia and could even re-sign with the Eagles for 2027. Goedert has lined up as an inline tight end 48.7% of the time this year, compared to 38.1% in the slot. I think these moves tell us the 49ers were looking to get another big body to pair with George Kittle, who they can throw the ball to. He’s been a serviceable blocker, but Luke Farrell only has six targets this season. Goedert had six targets in Week 9.

title: 49ers Mailbag: Playoffs, parity, and Connor Colby
summary: Well, it’s always funnier when the 49ers beat the Cowboys. And it’s always better when we have a mailbag before a 49ers game. So I found out I have this nifty little tool that lets me link your comments to my Niners Nation Feed post directly. It’s pretty neat, so I’m using it for this. […]
full_text: Fans watch from the stands as the Arizona Cardinals play the San Francisco 49ers at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Nov. 16, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Well, it’s always funnier when the 49ers beat the Cowboys . And it’s always better when we have a mailbag before a 49ers game. So I found out I have this nifty little tool that lets me link your comments to my Niners Nation Feed post directly. It’s pretty neat, so I’m using it for this. Our mailbag requests come during the week in The Feed . I go through comments, good and/or bad, and pick a few to respond to. Those I don’t respond to are probably because I don’t have a witty-enough response or something I simply didn’t have time for (the final 53-man roster at season’s end is a great question, but I don’t even want to rack my brain on that one). Basically, it’s not you, it’s me. All you need to do is see my mailbag post on The Feed and then make a comment about what we should talk about! We had a lot of questions this week. I’ll try to answer some of them: I don’t mind parity; I do think it’s being taken a biiiiit too far, however. I’m against a top team having a first pick in the draft—that’s where you get all the NBA controversies with lotteries and such. That said NBA draft “lottery” was originally implemented to prevent all-out tanking, but somehow elite prospects get picked up by specific teams, defying the odds. Here’s what I WOULD like. I agree with your salary cap worries, but I don’t think it should be removed—instead, adjusted. Several companies that have remote workers adjust salaries based on cost of living. For example, I live in Seattle, Washington, so my salary for a position would be significantly higher than someone living in Jackpot, Nevada. I think income tax can be a key decision-maker for players, and teams that have to deal with income taxes should adjust accordingly. Washington has no income tax; California does. So adjust the salary cap accordingly based on the tax structure of that team’s state. How do you do this? I have no idea. I am the worst at numbers. My other suggestion for the salary cap is that for any player drafted by a team who accrues x years on that team and is up for an extension, a percentage of their new deal doesn’t count against the salary cap. This lets them get the deal they want without crippling the team. This also rewards teams for drafting well rather than penalizing them. It’s like a franchise tag you can use once a year on a newly signed contract. Oftentimes, players don’t want to leave their team, but the business side of things gets in the way, and the team can only offer so much. Having a rule like this in effect would create roster consistency and ensure the talent gets the salary they deserve. You can go even further, like any pick in the second round-on, while the first round has the fifth-year option. The whole idea is that teams are rewarded for investing their resources and time into a prospect rather than the player’s contract being up and priced out of whatever team wants to keep them. Probably the Minnesota Vikings now that Kirk Cousins is back. I’m still traumatized by his last game against the 49ers in the purple back in 2023. Cousins went 35-for-45 (77 percent completions), for 378 yards, two touchdowns, and a single interception. You know that game better for this stupid Steve Wilks call . This game was where the murmurs of Wilks’ incompetence pretty much spilled out into screaming rants. After this game, he left the booth and came to the sidelines to call games. You know how that season turned out. Yes, the 49ers went to the Super Bowl, but those defensive formations, man. So looking back, Kirk Cousins back on the Vikings scares me. If not for that trade this week, I’d probably lean towards the Chicago Bears, but the Vikings are my pick. I don’t get it at this point. He’s reinstated, and the 49ers have two weeks. I’ve been on the 49ers’ side for all of this until right now, when I’m wondering why they just don’t cut the cord. My guess is they don’t want to cut him and have him go to a team they may face in two weeks. I doubt he’s in football shape, but I also wonder what he could give the Seahawks and/or Vikings if he signed with them. Keeping him for two weeks makes any signing more of a crunch. But then he could go to the Rams? I just don’t know what the 49ers are doing right now. Get it over with already. Here’s a nice stat that will help you figure this out: Pressures allowed by the 49ers OL this season: Connor Colby: 23 (58.1 pass-block grade) Dominick Puni: 11 (84.7) Colton McKivitz: 9 (75.6) Trent Williams: 8 (87.6) Jake Brendel: 8 (80.3) We have a major problem at left guard pic.twitter.com/F3K1uxSVdy — Coach Yac 🗣 (@Coach_Yac) November 9, 2026 58.1…yet somehow the 49ers are still standing. I think Colby is surrounded by talent (hey there, Colton McKivitz), but he’s clearly the weak link of the offensive line at left guard. The rest of the line has been doing a fine job. Now that said, can he get better? I think so. This is only his second season, and it’s still an improvement over last year. If the 49ers look to add another guard in the draft (one can wish upon a star), I hope they lock up Dominick Puni so they have some consistency on that line. I don’t think Colby is horrible (remember Erik Pears? THAT was bad), but we need to see how he develops for the rest of the year. The last thing we need is Jeffery Simmons lined up against him in the playoffs. I’d say the 2023 team was maybe more balanced—once they figured their decorum out. The 2023 team had that losing streak to the Vikings and Bengals and looked awful. I don’t know what they did to turn it around, but whatever it was, it got them to the Super Bowl. The issue with the 2023 team was defensive coaching (Steve Wilks was defensive coordinator) and Brock Purdy’s inexperience (which he mitigated well). The 2026 team is balanced, but I need to see more from the defense. I don’t mind the pass rush having a hard time sacking the quarterback, so long as the secondary is making pass-catchers pay for catching the ball. Sure, the Raiders had dial-a-turnovers against the 49ers, but that’s an anomaly. A lot of those turnovers (like the end zone fumble) are simply not going to happen most of the time. The stats will tell me otherwise, as the 49ers defense is one of the better defenses in the league (especially against the run), but both the Falcons game and the Raiders game have me questioning the pass rush. Since we got Nick Bosa back and DeForest Buckner returned, I hope that changes as things gel. That sounds like something El Shorts would do. I wonder what ever happened to that guy? He was a good dude. Whichever one eliminates the team that is the worst matchup for the 49ers. The Minnesota Vikings did the 49ers fans a favor in 2019 by knocking the New Orleans Saints out, and that was the team I thought would give the 49ers the most headaches (though the Saleh defense showed itself against the Packers at the end). If I have to look at what’s there, I’d probably just enjoy Giants-Vikings and watching the Giants knock the Vikings out. Since the NFC East is not very good this year, that would provide some pretty good comedy. As far as a game, Bears-Packers would be great, since it removes one of the threats to the 49ers. Then again, Bears-Rams would be nice, but I don’t know who I’d want to win that one. So specifically wide receivers, I’m going to go with De’Zhaun Stribling, Mike Evans, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Deebo Samuel, and Keenan Allen. I think once Stribling is good to go and Evans returns to the field, Jacob Cowing could be the odd man out. I’d put Cooks on punt returns and Watkins/Samuel on Kickoff returns. I think we’ve seen what Cowing is capable of, and all I see is bad decisions, bad ball security, and quitting on plays (like Brock Purdy’s interception against the Falcons ). He’s been with the team long enough (drafted in 2024) and there…

title: 49ers News: Ground stop? Sounds like the 49ers run defense
summary: 49ers-Cowboys preview: Christian McCaffrey and the Niners should run wild“When you watch them, the issues stem from getting moved at the point of attack. Ball carriers aren’t getting touched until they cross the line of scrimmage. The eye test matches the stats: Dallas allows the second-most yards before contact per carry this season, at 1.78 […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - NOVEMBER 8: Nick Bosa #97 and Osa Odighizuwa #92 of the San Francisco 49ers on the sideline before the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 38-17. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images 49ers-Cowboys preview: Christian McCaffrey and the Niners should run wild “When you watch them, the issues stem from getting moved at the point of attack. Ball carriers aren’t getting touched until they cross the line of scrimmage. The eye test matches the stats: Dallas allows the second-most yards before contact per carry this season, at 1.78 yards. They get moved, easily, despite having played only two offenses in the top-15 in rushing success rate. The 49ers are running more and more inside the tackles. They’re running inside zone at a 19.1% clip, a slight increase from a year ago. This game sets up well for the Niners to keep attacking the Cowboys’ A and B gaps. Kyle Shanahan had to be grinning as he watched the 36-play reel of the Cowboys’ defense defending —a term used loosely—inside zone. They allowed 8.08 yards per carry. Seven of those 36 plays went for double digits. They allowed a 58.3% success rate. You could build the case that the 49ers aren’t running inside enough this season. Christian McCaffrey had two 11-yard runs on inside zone last week. McCaffrey has 24 inside zone carries this year and averages 5.04 yards per carry, with a 62.5% success rate….Rookie Caleb Downs is the player the Niners could find success against. He’s primarily played nickel. Against the Texans, Packers, and Cardinals, Downs allowed all 9 of his targets to be completed for 147 yards. Heading into Week 9, Downs had allowed a 90.5% completion percentage, which was the third-highest among slot cornerbacks this season. He has one pass breakup. Dallas tried to align him closer to the line of scrimmage, almost like a pseudo-linebacker in coverage against Arizona. He played linebacker 32.1% of the time against the Cardinals.…Downs is not a big player. He’s 5’11”, 206 pounds, but has a 10th percentile arm length. That shows up in contested situations when he can’t make plays on the ball.” 49ers Week 9 Trench Grades: Leveling up (paywall) “One of my main takeaways this week was the impact that DeForest Buckner had on everyone as a force multiplier. But he also drew attention away from Osa Odighizuwa….Also, Colton McKivitz had a pretty impressive day against Maxx Crosby. Now, I saw the stat that he didn’t allowed a pressure. Maybe you can argue this isn’t a pressure from Crosby. I think it is, regardless of the stunt from Tonka Hemingway getting home. McKivitz vs. Crosby is independent of that.” 49ers OT Williams, LB Greenlaw questionable, WR Evans out vs. Cowboys “Anytime you hurt your shoulder on a Thursday, it doesn’t make you totally at ease,” Shanahan said of Williams. “Sunday comes fast, but hopefully that’s enough time for him to be all right.” 49ers vs. Cowboys: The Standard’s 5 fast predictions (paywall) “ Kawakami: 49ers 31, Cowboys 24 . This one feels similar to last week against the Raiders, who were awful defensively but had Kirk Cousins throwing the ball all over the field. And Prescott has better receivers. But the 49ers are designed to methodically win these kinds of matchups. 49ers injury report: Deebo cleared, Trent Williams questionable against Cowboys “The 49ers fully cleared Samuel to return for the team’s Week 10 game against the Dallas Cowboys. He has not played since Oct. 11, when he sustained a hamstring injury in a Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks. The 49ers should get a further boost at wide receiver with the addition of veteran Keenan Allen, who will make his San Francisco debut after arriving in a midweek trade from the Indianapolis Colts.” Five important 49ers to watch in the ‘biggest game of the year’ against Cowboys The 49ers’ defensive backs will face a tall order on Sunday against Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott and a strong passing game. Stout will undoubtedly be matched up regularly against CeeDee Lamb, who has 70 catches for 904 yards and seven touchdowns in nine games. Lamb will line up in the slot throughout the game, and that is when Stout will get his chance to go up against one of the best receivers in the NFL.” Kawakami: Trent Williams on the 49ers’ North Stars, Kyle Shanahan’s un-politics, and more “It’s just confidence, and a lot of that is a team paying you [$53 million] a year, and you understand not only are they telling me that they love me and they got my back, they’ve shown me that they love me and they have my back. So now when I go out there, I don’t have to look over my shoulder. I’m not in the huddle on eggshells saying I got to show that I’m more than the last pick of the draft. … “So now I think that the confidence is there and it’s allowing him to keep everything football. ‘Yeah, I can throw this layered ball that a lot of quarterbacks are scared to throw. And guess what? If it gets picked, I’m gonna come out and do it again because they trust me.’ And that’s the only way we win is by throwing these balls on time, throwing to these spots, and trusting it.’ … “[It’s about] the ability to go back out just like last week [after an interception], the next play, he threw a ball, and as I’m blocking, I hear Maxx [Crosby] say, ‘Oh, that’s a pick,’ and the ball floats right over the head [of a defender], another layered ball the drive after he just threw a pick trying to throw a layered ball.”

full_text: Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images | Getty Images The Buccaneers lost a 27-24 heartbreaker to the Chicago Bears in Week 9, and cornerback Keionte Scott lost $6,540 to a NFL fine for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet in that loss. The fine was assessed for a second-quarter tackle of Bears WR Kalif Raymond. Williams hit Raymond for a short 6-yard gain, and Scott was not flagged for the tackle in real time, but the fine was assessed after the fact. This is Scott’s only fine so far this season, his first in the NFL after being drafted by the Buccaneers in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Miami University. On the other sideline, two Bears players were fined for their play against the Buccaneers. Defensive end Austin Booker was fined $6,457 for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet on an incomplete pass from Baker Mayfield that was intended for WR Emeka Egbuka with 30 seconds left to play in the first half. Bears WR Zavion Thomas was fined $6,901 for unnecessary roughness/striking, kicking, and/or kneeing. Thomas was flagged for this play, and the Bears took a 15-yard penalty for it, too. The NFL divides the money it collects from player discipline and splits it equally between the NFLPA’s efforts to support and assist retired players, and the NFL Foundation and other nonprofits that support youth sports, player health and safety at all levels of sports, and community health initiatives.

title: How Jayden Daniels, Washington Commanders can stay in NFC East race
summary: The Commanders emerged with a victory over the Giants on Thursday night in a positively-have-to-have-it moment that saved their season.  You’ve probably read that line in every recap/analysis of Washington’s 24-21 win at MetLife Stadium, including my past-midnight musings on this very site.  There’s an important clause missing from that first sentence. Let’s try again: […]
full_text: The Commanders emerged with a victory over the Giants on Thursday night in a positively-have-to-have-it moment that saved their season. You’ve probably read that line in every recap/analysis of Washington’s 24-21 win at MetLife Stadium, including my past-midnight musings on this very site. There’s an important clause missing from that first sentence. Let’s try again: The Commanders emerged with a victory over the Giants on Thursday night in a positively-have-to-have-it moment that saved their season. … For now. The Commanders are back in the NFC East race . Can they stay there? Is their improved play sustainable? That’s the real question moving forward. Only time will tell us the answer. We can’t create a prediction model for this odd duck of a team, which features real talent, intriguing, modern schemes and a bunch of humans who can’t seem to get out of their own way. “We’ve held ourselves back,” Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs said. “When we play complementary football, we execute at a high level on offense. We move the ball just fine. We have enough playmakers. We had to execute at a high level.” Diggs was referring to that decisive Thursday night drive , where he and Daniels generated a season-altering 32-yard touchdown. He could’ve been talking about the season overall. While the injury situation has delivered body blows and haymakers, 3-5-1 is a product of Washington’s own making. Improved outcomes can also be a Commanders creation. Getting enough of them is the hard part. It’s a possibility, though maybe not a high probability considering what we’ve experienced to this point. There are some gateways to success down the stretch, but are there enough? Let’s discuss a few. The schedule is chief among them. If Washington can upset Cincinnati in Week 11, a real run is possible. The Commanders play the Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons (in that order) after that. Those are all beatable teams with the right execution level. Then there’s this resurgent defense , which is figuring out how to execute Daronte Jones’ scheme. The play caller himself seems to be dialed in on what works and when to turn up the heat. The results aren’t perfect but they’re better, with point totals going down and pressure rates going northward. That scheme and the fact that Sonny Styles and Frankie Luvu have owned the midfield and Nick Cross and Trey Amos have fortified the secondary. And then there’s the Jayden Daniels of it all. The 2024 season wasn’t so long ago that we can’t recall how the quarterback played and dominated late-game situations . While he has played a role in this disappointment we call the season’s first half, he can be responsible for a resurgence that puts Washington atop this wide-open division. We could come up with a gnarly cons list as well, one that’s probably a bit longer. It would include inconsistent offensive line play and the fact Washington can’t seem to get the run game going with or without Bill Croskey-Merritt. The pre-snap penalties and mental mistakes decreased against the Giants but remain a drive-killing issue that isn’t fixed. And the offensive growing plans won’t suddenly stop under rookie offensive coordinator David Blough. We’ll also meet some teams down the stretch, most notably the Vikings and Jaguars where they’ll face a real talent disparity. Let’s not create illusions that Washington is a conference contender. But they are capable of making things interesting in a relatively lightweight NFC East. Do you think the Commanders can seriously contend for a division title? Or is this a positive moment in an otherwise frustrating campaign? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Tyler’s Take – Washington Commanders need a short-yardage package
summary: I was absolutely thrilled to watch the Commanders get the win on Thursday night against the rival Giants on the road in primetime. For as pleased as I was with the effort and fight the team showed, there were some things that still need IMMEDIATE attention! I brought up one of these issues in my […]
full_text: I was absolutely thrilled to watch the Commanders get the win on Thursday night against the rival Giants on the road in primetime. For as pleased as I was with the effort and fight the team showed, there were some things that still need IMMEDIATE attention! I brought up one of these issues in my Studs and Duds article. David Blough’s gameplan looked a LOT different than previous games – IN A GOOD WAY! It actually resembled more Kliff Kingsbury than Ben Johnson with all the shotgun, tempo and chipping to help Brandon Coleman, the weak link on Washington’s offensive line. We still DESPERATELY lack a running game, but Blough did call a few designed runs to Daniels during the game which I liked. The one gripe I have is the series right before the half, when Washington was at the half-yard line. I know Jayden should have scored on the quarterback lead, but RUN THE DAMN BALL WITH YOUR RUNNING BACK! AT THE HALF YARD LINE AND WE WERE IN THE DAMN ‘GUN!!!!! Short Yardage Package: It’s VERY evident, even to the most novice observer, that Washington needs a short-yardage/goal-line “Heavy” package. With Jayden Daniels’ current elbow injury, there is not a fan on this planet (although I believe we have some fans from another galaxy), who want to see our 210-pound signal caller getting RAMMED into a defensive front and pushed forward into a pile of 320-pound immovable objects by 250-plus pound men. Some would suggest using veteran backup Marcus Mariota in this situation, but the 33-year-old has dealt with some injuries of his own this season, and I’d rather not put him in a situation where we could potentially make any of those worse. My Idea: Here me out… A lot of teams have a QB sneak package. We do not. If I’m the coach, I put in McCaffrey or Yankoff as our “Tush Push” quarterback for short yardage/goal line and have both Sinnott and Bates behind him as the pushers Ridiculous we are in gun from the 1/2 yd line! — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 14, 2026 Luke McCaffrey: The 6-foot-2 200-pounder was a former 4-star quarterback recruit who committed to play at Nebraska for Scott Frost. He played two seasons in Lincoln before transferring to Rice . He started three games at quarterback in 2021 before being moved to wide receiver in 2022. Colson Yankoff: The 6-4, 225-pound tight end was a former 4-star quarterback recruit for the University of Washington. He ended up redshirting as a freshman, then transferred to UCLA . After sitting out the 2019 campaign per NCAA rules, he switched to wide receiver/running back for the Bruins. Both players have the ability to go under center and take a snap. Both guys are good with the ball in their hands and shouldn’t be viewed as a risk when it comes to ball security in heavy traffic. Each guy has the necessary size and, being former ball carriers themselves (McCaffrey was a very good rushing quarterback), each should possess the necessary ability to see a small crease in the defense and get the necessary yardage to either move the chains or push the ball into the end zone. How Washington should run this: Ideally, this would be implemented by using three tight ends (two of which line up in the backfield as up-backs), with an extra lineman reporting in as eligible and lining up as a tight end. Below you will see how this formation could look. QB: Luke McCaffrey/Colson Yankoff Left TE: Andrew Wylie Right TE: Chig Okonkwo Up-Back (Pusher): John Bates Up-Back (Pusher): Ben Sinnott Deep Back: Rachaad White OR Treylon Burks What to name it: The Eagles made this package famous calling it the “Tush Push” OR the “Brotherly Shove”. Washington needs their own verbiage… DC DIVE (yeah, I’m not very good at this) As long as they don’t use a stupid cadence. Then again, “Who let the Hogs out? Oink, oink, oink, oink!” Would be a great troll next time we play the Giants. — RobB407 (@RBenninghove) November 14, 2026 Cadence – Who let the Hogs Out? Oink, oink, oink, oink! Haha Here is where you come in. Design a name for this formation below in the comments section.

full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 12: J.J. McCarthy #18 of the New York Giants runs with the ball during the second quarter of the game against the Washington Commanders at MetLife Stadium on November 12, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Sports Illustrated Commanders could finish ahead of Giants with the same record after Thursday’s win The good news is the Commanders now own the tie-breaker advantage with New York, something that could factor into things down the stretch. By rule, the October tie counts as half a win and half a loss for each team. Head-to-head record is the NFL’s first tiebreaker between two clubs in the same division. If Washington goes 5-3 over its final eight games and New York goes 3-5, both would finish 8-8-1. In a two-team tie, the Commanders would finish ahead of the Giants because they went 1-0-1 against them. Thursday’s win gave Washington that edge, but it still has to erase the two-game gap. That example assumes a two-team tie; a three-team tie involving Dallas would follow the NFL’s separate tiebreaking procedure. Make no mistake: Washington still has to stack wins. After the mini-bye, New York hosts Jacksonville on Sunday, November 22, and the Commanders host Cincinnati the following night. A Giants loss and a Washington win would cut the gap to one game. The teams won’t meet again this season, so the head-to-head edge only matters if the Commanders make up the ground elsewhere. Stefon Diggs with the game winning touchdown for the Washington Commanders.. "That was an amazing play" ~ @OfficialAJHawk #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/1zl8frFEHS — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) November 13, 2026 To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Washington Post (paywall) The Commanders got burned and stayed aggressive; it may have saved their season [The Isaiah Likely touchdown] was a major breakdown, but it didn’t change how Jones operated. He maintained an attacking mindset. It proved instrumental in a 24-21 win over New York that may have saved Washington’s season. “The easy thing would be to be nervous in that spot and to back off,” Coach Dan Quinn said. “But he’s aggressive.” The previous time these teams met, Jones had a conservative approach on defense. Washington blew a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter and ultimately settled for a tie . New York ran on its first two plays, forcing Washington to burn a couple of timeouts and setting up a pivotal third and one. The Giants were in an empty formation, but the Commanders had eight players along the line of scrimmage prepared for another blitz. It wound up being a designed run for McCarthy, but a blitzing Styles blew up the play. “Starting with coach DJ, he has confidence in us,” Styles said. “Plays are going to happen. You clean them up. Hopefully, you don’t make the same mistakes, but plays are going to happen. The other team, they make money, too. “But for him to keep that confidence as the game goes on and not pull back, I think it just shows he sees the improvement. He’s getting more and more comfortable with the guys he’s got out there, in terms of us being able to execute on a consistent basis, especially later in the game.” “Defensively, they were not only keeping us in the game,” Quinn said. “I thought they won the game.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE AHHHHHHH @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/SMbY27tskN — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 13, 2026 Download the SB Nation app Commanders fans, take command of game day! Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Chat live during every game Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The Athletic (paywall) The biggest thing Jayden Daniels is doing this fall is to stay healthy and keep playing The calls for Quinn’s job won’t completely abate unless and until wins are stacked on top of each other, and this is a group that hasn’t posted back-to-back victories since the playoffs that followed the 2024 season. It’s been a minute. But what has been reestablished over Washington’s past five games — all Daniels starts — is that the quarterback gives them a chance any time they line up, and that it’s not impossible for him to stay healthy for long stretches, even entire seasons, at a time. Did you watch Thursday night and obsess over the brace that’s keeping Daniels’ left elbow in place? Me neither. When Daniels plays, he can build on his own performances. When he gets hurt — and he did miss two September games with that dislocated left elbow — he’s almost starting over, at least at this point in his still-nascent career. In the five games since his return, he has completed 67.3 percent of his throws for 248 yards per game with seven touchdowns and just the two picks. He owns the eighth-best passer rating in the league over that span. Thursday was enormous for the stability of the entire franchise. It’s important that Daniels was at the fulcrum. The winning play didn’t come completely from embattled first-year coordinator David Blough. It was third-and-4 from the Giants’ 32. “I gave a little signal to Stef,” Daniels said, “and he went on a slant — and the rest is history.” For all yall Daniels’ haters—-The Diggs Game Winner HE makes happen. @Commanders @PFTCommenter #nfllive Watch the SIGNAL at the end! pic.twitter.com/FnXRRqYRnV — Dan Orlovsky (@danorlovsky7) November 13, 2026 The little signal wasn’t by accident. The little signal was developed during the course of the week. Diggs will turn 33 later this month and is in his 12th NFL season. He has seen nearly everything. His impression of Daniels, in that moment, with the season in the balance? “Baby Kobe,” Diggs said, invoking the name of Daniels’ athletic hero. “He’s gonna be the same kind of player he is in the beginning of the game and at the end of games.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE From ESPN: Daniels has played five consecutive games since sitting out two because of a dislocated left elbow. It is the most games he has played in a row since starting all 20 contests in his rookie season. On Thursday, he completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards and three touchdowns. But playing that many games consecutively has helped him find a groove, he said. “I’m starting to get into that rhythm,” Daniels said. “It shows the more games you play consistently, the more reps you get, the more flow in the rhythm that you can [find]. And it was tough last year being in and out of the lineup and trying to catch a rhythm.” Being in a rhythm might have helped Daniels on his final throw. When New York showed a cover zero blitz, Daniels gave a signal to Diggs, who ran a slant against corner Dru Phillips and then broke his tackle attempt and sped to the end zone where he turned at the 1, paused and fell backward into the end zone. “He’ll be the same player he is in the beginning of the game as he is in the end of the game,” Diggs said. “Things will happen good and bad and he isn’t going to change.” To read more of this ESPN article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Washington was last in the NFL on 3rd down; what changed against the Giants? Against the Giants, the Commanders converted 7-of-14 third downs. Six came with one yard to go, including Sinnott’s third-and-goal touchdown. All three of Washington’s touchdowns came on third down. Washington ran the ball 33 times Thursday, gaining 105 yards. Daniels accounted for 11 attempts and 28 yards, and the offense still went 0-for-2 on fourth down. That’s a lot to clean up for a team that needed all three touchdowns to beat New York.…
