title: NFL Week 10 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
summary: Touchdown for Chuba Hubbard? Fantasy upside for Aaron Rodgers? Trick play from the Raiders? Let's predict 15 things for Week 10.
full_text:
Week 10 of the  2026 NFL season is underway after the Commanders beat the Giants on  Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Will the Steelers upset the Bengals? How many yards will  Trey McBride have against the Rams? Could  Jadarian Price score his first NFL touchdown? And will Raiders coach Klint Kubiak dial up a trick play in  Fernando Mendoza 's first start?

 Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Carolina Panthers +2.5 (+110 moneyline) at New Orleans Saints 

 Quarterback  Bryce Young is getting the ball out more quickly recently without sacrificing chances downfield, which could be helpful against New Orleans' pass rush. The Saints are allowing 7.8 yards per pass attempt, giving Tetairoa McMillan opportunities to make big plays.

 New Orleans hasn't gotten much from its running game, and it will be without starting center  Erik McCoy ( biceps injury ) on Sunday . That puts more stress on quarterback  Tyler Shough , enabling Carolina to keep this close and potentially win outright.

 
 

 

 Pittsburgh Steelers +3.5 (+150 moneyline) at Cincinnati Bengals 

 Running back  Jaylen Warren gives Pittsburgh a way to control this game. He already piled up 176 total yards in Pittsburgh's Week 3 win over Cincinnati , and the Bengals keep giving up long runs this season.

 Cincinnati also struggles to defend the middle of the field, where Steelers quarterback  Aaron Rodgers  has strong options in WR  Germie Bernard and TE  Darnell Washington . Bengals QB  Joe Burrow will get his points, but Pittsburgh can answer without asking Rodgers to force deep throws.

 

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 Malik Washington , WR, Miami Dolphins : 11 targets, 7 receptions, 78 receiving yards, 1 touchdown 

 Every year I look for the players who are excelling in ESPN's open score -- which measures a receiver's ability to get open on all routes , regardless of target -- but struggling in catch score. That's because open score is much more stable than catch score and correlates better with future production.

 Washington fits this profile exactly with an 82 open score (tied with Garrett Wilson for second best) but just a 38 catch score (below average). So there is a decent chance Washington's production will increase, and it could happen as early as this Sunday  -- even with backup quarterback   Kyle McCord  throwing him the ball. Washington should line up against Colts nickel cornerback  Justin Walley , who missed the past two games with a knee injury and is allowing 1.8 yards per coverage snap, per NFL Next Gen Stats. That's well above the 1.1 average.

 
 

 Trey McBride , TE, Arizona Cardinals : 13 targets, 9 receptions, 99 receiving yards 

 If I were quarterback  Carson Beck , I would make a point of throwing to McBride when in doubt during my NFL debut . But that would be especially true now that  Michael Wilson  is out for the season with a neck injury . And even further because 23% of targets against the Rams' defense have been to tight ends, the sixth-highest rate in the league.

 As long as cornerback  Trent McDuffie isn't on McBride, he ought to be the priority target on most plays. If the Cardinals fall behind, McBride should be in line for quite a bit of garbage-time production to come close to the 100-yard mark.

 
 

 Justin Eboigbe , DT, Los Angeles Chargers : 1.0 sacks, 4 pressures, 19% pass rush win rate 

 Eboigbe recorded 6.0 sacks a year ago but has just 0.5 this season. Plus, he has a well-below-average pass rush win rate. So why am I forecasting a big game for Eboigbe on Monday ? Because of who he'll line up against. Ravens right guard John Simpson has a sixth-percentile pass block win rate at the position, while center Cam Jurgens is literally last in pass block win rate at his position since he started playing for the Ravens in Week 7.

 

 

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Aaron Rodgers , QB, Pittsburgh Steelers (35.4% rostered in ESPN leagues) 

 Rodgers has averaged just 8.9 fantasy points over his past two games, with Pittsburgh leaning heavily on its running game. That could change Sunday night against a Bengals offense that ranks second in points per game, which could force the Steelers to throw more to keep pace.

 Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdown passes  against Cincinnati in Week 3 , finishing with 22.6 fantasy points. The Bengals have also allowed 17.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.

 
 

 Corey Kiner , RB, New England Patriots (31.9%) 

 Kiner could lead the Patriots' backfield against the Lions this week , with Rhamondre Stevenson listed as questionable ( knee tendon issue ) and TreVeyon Henderson  is  out . Kiner rushed for 55 yards and a touchdown on eight carries against the Packers last week ; he leads New England with 4.9 yards per carry this season.

 Detroit has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs, so it's a tough matchup. But Kiner could see 14-plus rushing attempts, while Lan Larison handles more of the work on passing downs.

 
 

 Tutu Atwell , WR, Los Angeles Rams (8.1%) 

 With  Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both sidelined, Atwell could see a lot more targets against the Cardinals . He has drawn nine targets over his past two games and played more snaps than any other healthy Rams receiver against the Commanders.

 Arizona has allowed 32.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers and the second-most passing touchdowns in the league. Atwell's production has been inconsistent, but his ability to make plays downfield and the opportunity for more targets make him worth considering in deeper leagues.

 

 
 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers 
 

 Jadarian Price , RB, Seattle Seahawks 

 Price had 78 total yards in the Week 9 win over the Cardinals , and he looked explosive in the pass game with four receptions for 54 yards. He will continue to split touches with Zach Charbonnet on Sunday versus the Raiders , but I see him scoring his first pro touchdown here -- off a screen pass.

 
 

 George Kittle , TE, San Francisco 49ers 

 Take the target volume with Kittle, plus the prime matchup versus the Dallas defense . Kittle has seen at least seven targets in three straight games, and coach Kyle Shanahan can scheme up his tight end to press the seams against the Cowboys' split-safety coverages.

 I'd expect multiple red zone targets for Kittle on Sunday. And the 49ers are the best in the league at turning those targets into touchdowns (84.6% red zone touchdown percentage this season).

 
 

 Chuba Hubbard , RB, Carolina Panthers 

 Hubbard has at least one rushing score in three of his past five games, and he is seeing consistent volume with 20 or more touches in four contests. Meanwhile, the Saints are giving up 133.9 rushing yards per game (fourth most) and have allowed 11 rushing touchdowns this season (tied for second most). With steady volume and red zone touches, Hubbard could easily find the end zone Sunday.

 

 

 

 Solak makes four more predictions 
 

 Rams WR  CJ Daniels will score a touchdown 

 The Rams' undrafted free agent receiver is in line for his first NFL action now that Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all on IR. Daniels critically has something that projected starting receivers Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell lack: size. At 6-foot-2, 205 pounds, don't be surprised if Daniels sees…

full_text:
The NFL regular season has officially passed the halfway point, meaning we are approaching the final chances to see threads on the field. Thankfully, the uniform heat isn't stopping any time soon as alternates continue to make headlines around the league. This week, it's the Tennessee Titans ' turn as they debut their Rivalries look.

 

 Tennessee will wear its "Music City"-inspired combination against the Jacksonville Jaguars . It includes a two-tone blue color palette with a Titans-blue lid and navy uniform. The numbers are reminiscent of a neon sign, a nod to those that run through Nashville. "Music City" runs across the chest, while six rhythmic stripes run down the side, similar to strings on a guitar. 

 It's a fresh look for the Baltimore Ravens , too, who will debut their all-black combination against the Los Angeles Chargers on "Monday Night Football." The headline for Baltimore's threads is a new matte black lid, nicknamed the "Darkness Helmet." It includes black talon stripes and a two-toned Ravens logo that features red eyes. The shield shoulder patch is black and midnight purple, while "darkness there and nothing more" runs on the inside collar -- a reference to a quote from Edgar Allen Poe's "The Raven."

 Monochromatic alternates are popular around the rest of the league. The Cincinnati Bengals will wear their "White Bengal" helmet with all-white uniforms, first introduced in 2022, against the Pittsburgh Steelers . Cincinnati has gone 5-1 in the white helmets since they debuted in 2022. The New York Jets are rocking the "Legacy Black" threads against the Buffalo Bills , while the New Orleans Saints will also go all-black against the Carolina Panthers . title: Falcons insist winning still the goal despite trading Jessie Bates III
summary: Atlanta wanted to ensure trading away Jessie Bates III didn't send the wrong message to the team.
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Overcommunication. That has been the order of business over the past several days for Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski.

 That has included one-on-one meetings with players, small-group conversations with the team's player leadership committee and full team meetings. Stefanski has wanted to make it absolutely certain that the Falcons, despite trading two starters before the NFL trade deadline earlier this week, are not in any way giving up on this season.

 "I would tell you we've got a great group of leadership on this team," Stefanski said. "I've talked to them a lot over the last few days -- like I do all the time, but in particular now. I'm very, very confident in their leadership."

 On Monday, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Bates, aside from being arguably the best safety in the league, was also a team captain and one of the most respected veterans in the building.

 A day later, Atlanta traded starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for reserve guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil was a Falcons success story, starting with the team as an undrafted free agent and working his way up to a starting role.

 The Falcons are 3-6. So, in that respect, it made perfect sense to get value back for two players who were set to become free agents in the offseason. With regards to Bates, a safety had not been acquired for a second-round pick since 2018. Few could blame Atlanta for making the move.

 

 "We believe the return gives us a meaningful opportunity to strengthen this roster over time," a team source said. "That does not mean Jessie stopped being an outstanding player. We are giving up something valuable and we understand that."

 On the other hand, the Falcons are in one of the most unique positions in the NFL. Their record is ugly, but they are a half-game out of first place in a weak NFC South. All four teams in the division are sitting at three wins apiece. Atlanta finishes its season playing its NFC South rivals back-to-back-to-back.

 So, there was also an argument for standing pat and making a good-faith run at the playoffs, where the Falcons have not been since 2017. Only the New York Jets have a longer drought.

 "We're still in it," quarterback Michael Penix Jr . said. "... We're so close in a lot of areas and I feel like in this organization we view that a lot. We use that a lot. We are so close.

 "I truly believe we have the team and the guys that's going to rally and flip the script because we got a lot of guys that care. Obviously, I feel like matchup wise, I feel like our team is one of the top teams in the league."

 The Falcons have shown glimpses of that, such as last month when they toppled the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers in an impressive performance. But since then, they have fallen to the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a full-on downpour and lost to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid.

 

 The schedule does not get any easier. The Kansas City Chiefs will come to town Sunday. After that, the Falcons have their bye week followed by a road game against the Minnesota Vikings , a home game against the Detroit Lions and then a trip to Cleveland. Those teams have a combined 23-10 record.

 It will be up to the team's leadership to keep the players focused on the task at hand. ESPN's FPI  is giving the Falcons only a 4.5% chance of making the playoffs, but the division remains wide open. The other three teams don't have easy schedules, either.

 Left tackle Jake Matthews , the longest-tenured Falcon and the only player left from the 2016 Super Bowl team, said Atlanta had a "really good practice" Wednesday "because everyone was kind of dialed in to 'Hey, this is our objective still and we fully expect to go out and play every weekend to win.'"

 "I think [Stefanski's] message and the point was kind of driven home that there's so much still ahead of us this season," Matthews said. "We need to double down."

title: Ranking the top 10 Super Bowl performances by a defender
summary: Not all Super Bowl MVPs were quarterbacks or offensive stars. We listed 10 standout individual defensive performances.
full_text:
Super Bowls are mostly remembered for offensive fireworks, miraculous fourth-quarter drives, gravity-defying catches and MVP quarterbacks who hoist the Vince Lombardi Trophy in victory.

 Yet, as the old adage in football reminds us, offense sells tickets while defense wins championships.

 While team defenses such as the 1985 Chicago Bears , 2000 Baltimore Ravens and 2013 Seattle Seahawks dominated as collective units, a select group of defenders delivered singular, dominant, game-altering performances on the NFL's biggest stage.

 Here are 10 of the best individual defensive performances in Super Bowl history, including four defenders who earned the game's Most Valuable Player award.

 COUNTDOWN TO SUPER BOWL LXI: ESPN will televise the Super Bowl for the first time in February. We are counting down to the big game with a Super Bowl Top 10 series , featuring rankings on everything from best catches and performances to biggest upsets, which will run every other Sunday leading up to Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, 2027. 

 

 

 1. Denver Broncos OLB Von Miller in  Super Bowl 50 
 When : Feb. 7, 2016

 Score : Broncos 24, Panthers 10

 Stats : 2.5 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, 1 pass defended

 Miller set the tone with a strip-sack of Cam Newton in the first quarter that was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown to give the Broncos a 10-0 lead. With Denver up 16-10 late in the fourth quarter, Miller once again jarred the ball loose from Newton when he sacked the quarterback deep in Carolina territory to put the Broncos in position to score the game-sealing touchdown four plays later.

 Miller's performance was so dominant he earned unanimous Super Bowl MVP honors, becoming the 10th defensive player and fourth linebacker in NFL history to win the award.

 
 

 2. Oakland Raiders LB Rod Martin in Super Bowl XV 
 When : Jan. 25, 1981

 Score : Raiders 27, Eagles 10

 Stats : 3 interceptions, 5 tackles

 Martin created the standard for ball-hawking dominance on the biggest stage when he set the Super Bowl record for interceptions -- a record that is shared but still stands -- by picking off Ron Jaworski three times.

 The linebacker staved off any chance of a Philadelphia comeback when he intercepted Jaworski in the first, third and fourth quarters of the Raiders' eventual 17-point win. He also added five tackles in Oakland's second Super Bowl victory.

 
 

 3. Chicago Bears DE Richard Dent in Super Bowl XX 
 When : Jan. 26, 1986

 Score : Bears 46, Patriots 10

 Stats : 1.5 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, 1 blocked pass, 3 tackles

 The "Sack Man" in Chicago's legendary "46 defense" led the NFL with 17.5 sacks during the 1985 season and gave a master class in pass rushing during Super Bowl XX. Dent wreaked havoc in the backfield with 1.5 sacks, three tackles two forced fumbles while constantly ripping through blocks to keep Patriots quarterback Tony Eason under pressure.

 Dent earned Super Bowl MVP honors and is the last true defensive end to win the award.

 
 

 4. Green Bay Packers DE Reggie White in Super Bowl XXXI 
 When : Jan. 26, 1997

 Score : Packers 35, Patriots 21

 Stats : 3 sacks, 4 QB hits, 1 tackle for a loss

 

 White established the Super Bowl record by sacking Drew Bledsoe three times.

 After a quiet first half, White lived up to his "Minister of Defense" nickname when it mattered most. With Bledsoe and the Patriots trying to mount a comeback after pulling within a touchdown in the third quarter, White took over and recorded three second-half sacks, which included back-to-back sacks that flipped the game's momentum.

 
 

 5. Tampa Bay Buccaneers CB Dwight Smith in Super Bowl XXXVII 
 When : Jan. 26, 2003

 Score : Buccaneers 48, Raiders 21

 Stats : Only player in Super Bowl history with 2 pick-sixes

 While his teammate Dexter Jackson captured MVP honors for setting the tone in a rout of the Raiders, Smith delivered the decisive knockout blows against league MVP Rich Gannon when he returned two interceptions for touchdowns.

 Smith picked off a third-quarter pass and took it 44 yards for a touchdown to extend Tampa Bay's lead to 34-3. He then punctuated the win with a 50-yard pick-six in the final seconds. Smith capped off a dominant five-interception defensive clinic by Monte Kiffin's "Tampa 2" unit and cemented his place in postseason lore.

 
 

 6. Los Angeles Rams DT Aaron Donald in Super Bowl LVI 
 When : Feb. 13, 2022

 Score : Rams 23, Bengals 20

 Stats : 2 sacks, 2 tackles for losses, 4 tackles, 3 QB hits

 Donald's second-half takeover came after fighting through constant double-teams and triple-teams. With Cincinnati trailing by three after just crossing into LA's territory with less than a minute to play, Donald blew up a run play on third-and-1 for no gain. He sealed the victory by pressuring quarterback Joe Burrow on fourth down and forcing an incomplete pass.

 The Rams took over in victory formation, and many believed Donald's effect should have earned him game MVP honors over Rams' wide receiver Cooper Kupp .

 
 

 7. Dallas Cowboys LB Chuck Howley in Super Bowl V 
 When : Jan. 17, 1971

 Score : Colts 16, Cowboys 13

 

 Stats : 10 tackles, 2 interceptions and a fumble recovery

 Howley made history as the first non-QB and player from the losing team to win Super Bowl MVP.

 The linebacker was a bright spot in a sloppy game that was nicknamed "The Blunder Bowl" due to 11 combined turnovers. He recorded two interceptions and recovered a fumble while single-handedly terrorizing Johnny Unitas and the Colts' passing game.

 
 

 8. Dallas Cowboys S James Washington in Super Bowl XXVIII 
 When : Jan. 30, 1994

 Score : Cowboys 30, Bills 13

 Stats : 1 interception, forced fumble and fumble recovery, which he returned for a TD

 Trailing 13-6 at halftime, the Cowboys desperately needed a spark, and Washington provided it 54 seconds into the third quarter when he recovered a fumble from Bills running back Thurman Thomas and returned it 46 yards for a game-tying touchdown.

 The safety anchored Dallas' secondary with a team-high 11 tackles and terrorized Buffalo's offense by adding a crucial interception and another forced fumble later in the second half. He played a direct role in three turnovers that fueled Dallas's second-half takeover.

 
 

 9. Carolina Panthers DE Kony Ealy in Super Bowl L 
 When : Feb. 7, 2016

 Score : Broncos 24, Panthers 10

 Stats : 3 sacks, 2 tackles for a loss, 3 QB hits, an interception, pass defended, fumble recovery and forced fumble

 Despite the Panthers' loss, Ealy delivered the most stat-sheet stuffing defensive performance in Super Bowl history. While logging only 23 defensive snaps (38%) as a rotational edge rusher, the second-year defender harassed Broncos quarterback Peyton Manning all night and matched the Super Bowl single-game sack record.

 Ealy's efforts kept the game close. He intercepted Manning in the second quarter and forced a fumble in the fourth to put the Panthers within a touchdown. He became the only player in Super Bowl history to record multiple sacks and an interception in the game.

 
 

 10. Seattle Seahawks LB Malcolm Smith in Super Bowl XLVIII 
 When : Feb. 2, 2014

 Score : Seahawks 43, Broncos 8

 Stats : An interception, touchdown, fumble recovery and 10 tackles.

 Smith was at the center of the Legion of Boom's dominant defensive performance. He racked up a team-high 10 tackles, recovered a forced fumble and blew the game open in the second quarter when he intercepted an errant Peyton Manning pass and returned it 69 yards for a touchdown. His opportunistic play made him just the third linebacker at the time to win Super Bowl MVP.

 

 Honorable mentions 
 Miami Dolphins S Jake Scott, Super Bowl VII (Dolphins 14, Redskins 7): 2 interceptions, MVP

 New England Patriots CB Stephon Gilmore, Super Bowl LIII (Patriots 13, Rams 3): 1 interception, 3 passes defended, 1 forced fumble

 Dallas Cowboys CB Larry Brown, Super Bowl XXX (Cowboys vs. Steelers) 2 interceptions,…

full_text:
In the Week 3 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals , a 30-27 Pittsburgh Steelers win at home, Jaylen Warren produced 176 total yards on 20 touches and Aaron Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns, completing five passes of 20 or more yards.

 

 However, this Steelers' pass game has lacked rhythm over the last two games, as Rodgers threw for less than 215 yards in both while completing only 58.2% of his attempts. This is a team that has been reliant on Warren (two straight games with over 100 yards rushing) and the rushing attack, as well as a top-10 defense allowing only 18.0 PPG (tied for fourth fewest in the league). But Rodgers and the Steelers will need to create some explosive plays through the air to match the Bengals. Let's see if they made some adjustments/corrections off the bye week.

 Based on the numbers and the game tape, Joe Burrow is currently playing the best football in the league at the quarterback position. Over his last five games, Burrow is averaging 328.6 yards passing and completing over 75% of his throws, tossing 17 touchdown passes over that stretch. Timing, location, pocket mobility ... it's all there. And Burrow has an elite combination of receivers in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . Multi-level route runners and high-end matchup targets.

 However, the Bengals' run game with Chase Brown is still looking for a way to create efficiency, and the defense, while creating splash plays, is giving up 354.9 yards per game (eighth most).

 

 

 

 Betting outlook 
 

 I would stay with the trends when betting this game. That means taking the safe plays on Burrow with yards and completions, as I do see the Bengals rolling with a pass-heavy script.

 Cincy isn't generating consistent production on the ground (85.6 yards per game), and the Steelers are allowing only 3.6 YPC. Throw the ball here to stay ahead of the sticks.

 I like Warren as a dual-threat option, which allows me to bet his rushing + receiving total, but I'm going to stay lower on Rodgers in this one. The Steelers have been winning with an old-school identity, and it allows them to control tempo.

title: Untold stories of Detroit Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown's German upbringing
summary: For Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sunday's NFL game in Munich will mark the ultimate convergence of his dual heritage. Here are stories that shed more light.
full_text:
DETROIT -- When the Detroit Lions take the field to face the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday, wide receiver  Amon-Ra St. Brown  will feel right at home.

 For St. Brown, Germany is as much his home as the United States. It's where he and his family frequently took trips to visit his maternal grandparents. It's where St. Brown went to preschool (Die Rheinpiraten Kindergarten, to be exact), and where he and his older brothers, Equanimeous and Osiris, spent countless hours on bike tours and fishing trips with their grandfather, Helmut Steyer, who enjoyed entertaining his American-born grandsons.

 

 It's where Amon-Ra (and Osiris) was a standout for the country's under-19 national football team. It's where he has hosted football camps since becoming a pro in 2021. And it's where the Lions star was once asked by an uncle to stay in order to become a star in the other type of football.

 "It's not strange to him. It's all familiar ... everything," St. Brown's mother, Miriam Brown, said. "Going to restaurants, everything is different but for him it's familiar."

 The deep connection and familiarity St. Brown has with the country is because of Miriam. Born and raised in Leverkusen, in western Germany, she instilled her German values into Amon-Ra and his brothers, who are all fluent in German.

 Those values, and experiences, are a part of St. Brown's identity and have always been at the forefront of who he is. As a result, when the Lions face the Patriots in one of the country's most famous arenas (9:30 a.m. ET on Fox), St. Brown will be the headline act.

 More than 80 NFL players who were born in Germany (West Germany and East Germany included) have appeared in a game, per ESPN Research, including 10 who have debuted since 2018. Although he was born in Anaheim Hills, California, few have experienced as much popularity in Germany as St. Brown, who, according to NFL Germany general manager Alexander Steinforth, is the subject of multiple documentaries currently being produced there.

 "He's probably the poster boy for the NFL in the German-speaking world these days," Steinforth told ESPN. "He works a lot and has worked a lot with our local broadcast partners, so it's amazing to see when he's kind of talking to his German fans. He's a really big and important name for us here in Germany."

 St. Brown wears decals of both the German and American flags on his helmet. He says he's fortunate and proud to be so immersed in both cultures, each of which he has drawn from throughout his life.

 "Being half German, half American you kind of get to experience both cultures, and you admire different things in both cultures," St. Brown said. "You feel as if, you know, some things you wish the Americans would do more, some things you wish the Germans would do more.

 "But I'm both, so I can pick and choose what I like from each culture. And I think both cultures have amazing, amazing qualities. But I'm just glad that I was able to dip my feet into both cultures and be around both of them."

 What does Germany really mean to St. Brown? These are stories that shed more light.

 

 

 'Shoot the ball!' 

 Very early in St. Brown's eighth grade basketball season, coach Brian Liles began getting annoyed.

 Liles, who was coaching in the National Junior Basketball youth league in Irvine, California, had taught the boys a pass-first style of hoops that he expected his Titans team to follow. But throughout the first four or five games, John Brown -- the father of a teenage Amon-Ra St. Brown -- was in the stands instructing his youngest son to do the complete opposite.

 "Every time Amon-Ra got the ball, he would go, 'Shoot the ball! Shoot the ball!' After a while, I just walked over and I go, 'John, I'm trying to get him to pass the ball because the minute he gets the ball everybody swarms to him,'" Liles recalled. "'Guys are open underneath the basket and if he makes the pass, we will be able to get an easy layup."'

 

 During the chat, Liles said Brown was kind and immediately receptive.

 He said, "Oh yeah, sorry, Coach. I won't say anything else."

 Liles said Brown held his tongue for the next few possessions. Then, suddenly, he heard him calling to his son again ... but in an unfamiliar language.

 "I'm like, 'Is that German? I think he's talking in German.' And all of a sudden Amon-Ra starts shooting the basketball again," Liles said. "And I go, 'That son of a gun is telling him to shoot the ball in German!'

 

 "So, he tried to outsmart me, but I picked it up."

 Those interactions weren't uncommon for Amon-Ra and his brothers during their youth sports careers. Whether it was basketball, football or soccer, Brown was frequently on the sidelines delivering instructions in German.

 They weren't always well received by his sons.

 "This was in football specifically and my brother was in Pop Warner, and I think he was telling him to do some type of move," Osiris said. "He's like, 'Spin, spin.' And my brother, and even me, we all got annoyed that he kept yelling at us to do something.

 "So, my brother got so frustrated that he would just do the move like when he didn't need to do it, just to do it. He's like, 'You want me to spin? Forget it, I'll spin' even when he wasn't near someone."

 Brown said he learned enough German to deliver commands. He figured Liles, or anyone else, would never know what he was saying.

 "I used that to my advantage, yeah," he said, laughing.

 

 

 Summers in Leverkusen 
 As teenagers, word was starting to spread throughout Germany about the three brothers who lived in California and also held German citizenship.

 The St. Brown brothers spent nearly every summer with Miriam Brown's family in Leverkusen. In 2015, Amon-Ra played for the German U-19 national American football team alongside Osiris.

 Equanimeous, who was a freshman wide receiver at the University of Notre Dame at the time, didn't play, but the younger boys were happy to have each other for the trip.

 "So, we go to the first game and it wasn't that many people in the stands," John Brown said. "I can't recall which country we played, but when we played France, Osiris got kicked out of the game because he got into a fight with a French guy because he did something to him and he said, 'I'm not going to let some French guy talk s--- to me.'"

 Jürgen Siebmanns, team manager of the German junior national team, was responsible for recruiting and selecting both brothers and has continued to follow their pro and college careers.

 "Their talent, athleticism and attitude were not only an enrichment in the game, but also a role model for all players," Siebmanns told American-Football.com in 2020. "It was clear to everyone that both would make their way -- and of course we are all the more pleased when it even leads to such highlights and records."

 At the European Championship in Dresden, Germany, Amon-Ra, just 15 years old and undersized compared with the competition, won MVP honors -- a feat that wasn't surprising to his brothers.

 Representing Germany was meaningful to the boys and the family. And even after all these years, they still keep in contact with former teammates from that trip.

 "We were younger than these guys and a lot of these guys look like grown-ass men," Osiris said. "So, I'm like, 'F---.' But I don't even know if we ever talked about it, but then as soon as we get out there you can immediately see that these guys were at least like a good 10-15 years behind in skillwise when it came to football and we immediately started tearing it up in practice and then games."

 The experience playing sports on an international level was eye-opening for the family but not entirely shocking. When he was 5 years old, Amon-Ra's promising ability led Miriam to enroll him at the SC Hitdorf soccer club, located in the Hitdorf district of Leverkusen. He spent countless hours in the backyard of his mother's childhood home picking up the new sport.

title: Week 10 betting preview: Analysis, best bets, TD predictions for Sunday
summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 10 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
full_text:
Wek 10 of the NFL season is already upon us. We've looked at the games, the odds and available props in hopes of trying to find the best value for bets.

 Ben Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Seth Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Matt Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers.

 Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. Let's get into it.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 Jump to: 
 Bowen's favorite bets 
 Solak's plays  | Walder's props 
 Clay's TD projections 

 

 

 Bowen's favorite bets 
 We'll start with our game pick this week with the Chiefs-Falcons matchup in Atlanta. Plus, I have multiple teasers for the Week 10 slate, and I'll add a player prop on a wide receiver who is creating explosive plays at a high rate.

 Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons 
1 p.m. ET on CBS; Line: KC -3, O/U: 46.5

 

 The Chiefs added wide receiver Josh Downs at the trade deadline, giving Patrick Mahomes a slot target who can create numbers after the catch. The foot quickness is there to uncover. But I like the Chiefs to cover as a road favorite because of the run game and Steve Spagnuolo's defense.  Kenneth Walker III  is a difference-maker in Andy Reid's offense, averaging 23.1 touches and 130.5 scrimmage yards per game. but has been ruled out for Sunday  due to a groin injury, elevating rookie Emmett Johnson to the lead role. Johnson has the vision and elusive ability to find daylight versus an Atlanta defense allowing 4.4 YPC (22nd in the league), while Reid can use the heavy run action to influence linebackers on play-action concepts. Defensively, Spagnuolo's unit will mix late rotation, Cover 2 and pressure against a Falcons offense that is lacking passing rhythm right now. And quarterback Michael Penix Jr . has struggled against the blitz this season (48.4 QBR).

 

 Two-team, 6.5-point teaser (-143): Cleveland Browns +11 vs. Houston Texans , San Francisco 49ers +3 at Dallas Cowboys 

 Deshaun Watson is expected back under center, and Cleveland will have enough answers in the pass game to make plays against the Texans' core zone schemes. The Browns will need more rushing efficiency from Quinshon Judkins , but I feel comfortable with the altered spread at home because of a Cleveland pass defense that matches up well with Houston. In the other matchup in this teaser, Kyle Shanahan can scheme up a Dallas defense that is giving up 26.8 points and 372.7 yards per game. Look for play-action early with Brock Purdy targeting the seams and deep in-breakers, while the 49ers' defense creates issues for Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' passing game.

 Two team, 6.5-point teaser (-135): Minnesota Vikings +9.5 at Green Bay Packers ,  Buffalo Bills -2 at New York Jets 

 The trade for Kirk Cousins should create more volume and production for Justin Jefferson , and that will open more daylight for the Vikings' run game. But I'm taking Minnesota, with the spread being bumped to +9.5 points, because of Brian Flores' defense. I expect more zone pressure here because of the vertical ability of both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , but the Vikings will look to create chaos for Jordan Love . I like the Bills in the other matchup. Coach Joe Brady will have pressure answers for Josh Allen to get the ball out (catch-and-run targets for DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir ), and don't be surprised if the Bills lead with a run-heavy approach to control tempo.

 Jameson Williams longest reception OVER 24.5 yards (-112) 

 Williams has had a reception of 24 or more yards in five straight games. With his vertical ability, plus the dynamic open-field speed he displays after the catch, I like Williams to hit the over against New England.

 

 

 
 Solak's plays 

 

 Pittsburgh Steelers +3.5 at Cincinnati Bengals 

 I unsuccessfully faded the Bengals last week against the Falcons in Madrid, but I'm back again with them facing the Steelers, a franchise known for its strong performance as a small underdog under Mike Tomlin that might still retain a bit of that magic under Mike McCarthy.

 I love the Steelers' potential to keep this game close because they have the sort of ball-control, run-heavy offense that can minimize the number of possessions Joe Burrow gets in this game. Since Week 3, when Pittsburgh rejiggered the right side of its offensive line, the Steelers are third in success rate and first in EPA on rushing snaps; no team has a higher explosive run rate, and it isn't close. When they faced the Bengals in Week 3, Jaylen Warren had 17 carries for 127 yards. Now, Rico Dowdle is back to help.

 The Steelers are also big on targeting the backs and tight ends in the passing game, which is where you want to go after this Bengals defense, and the lingering ankle injury to  DJ Turner II  also makes Cincinnati fairly weak in the secondary. It's a divisional game, and the Bengals are too hot and cold to trust with more than a field goal against a Steelers team off the bye.

 Rico Dowdle receiving yards OVER 13.5 (-114) 

 

 Dowdle returned to the Steelers' lineup in Week 6 and had seven routes to Warren's 27 in that game against the Buccaneers. But he was targeted on four of those seven routes, and since then has 24 routes and six targets to Warren's 22 routes and six targets. The receiving volume has been fairly split since his return, and rightfully so -- Warren has been an exceptional between-the-tackles runner this season, and Dowdle has always been a capable pass catcher.

 Yet, Warren is projected for 25.5 yards and 3.5 receptions, whereas Dowdle is at 13.5 and 2.5. Given how willingly Aaron Rodgers targets the backs and how poor the Bengals' linebackers are in coverage and at tackling in the open field, backfield receiving production should be a strong part of Pittsburgh's offensive approach, and Dowdle is the far cheaper option in what should be near a 50/50 opportunity split.

 Keep an eye on this number live. If Warren starts out the first quarter taking most of the snaps on a couple of Pittsburgh three-and-outs, Dowdle's numbers will drop even more, and I'll start looking for live alts.

 Tutu Atwell receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-109) 

 It's worth wondering just who it is that is going to catch passes for the Los Angeles Rams . Star wide receiver Puka Nacua -- who had 19 targets and 14 receptions on 43 routes last week against the Commanders -- joins Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington on the injured reserve bench. Tight end Terrance Ferguson is also probably out for Sunday's game at Arizona.

 The two primary route runners behind Nacua at receiver last Sunday were Konata Mumpfield and Atwell, the latter of whom was targeted five times for two receptions and 16 yards. Atwell ended the day with 37 unrealized air yards -- that is to say, he had 53 air yards to the 16 receiving yards he actually produced. In back-to-back weeks, he has had at least 50 air yards on 17 and 20 routes, respectively. Given the thinness of the Rams' receiver room, 20 routes should be a floor projection for Atwell, as long as the Cardinals' offense can keep things competitive with Carson Beck under center. Even if they can't, Atwell's downfield usage can get us home on one big reception.

 If you're looking to get really frisky in what should be a sleepy late afternoon game, Rams rookie receiver CJ Daniels to score a touchdown is +950. He's a big-framed receiver, which the Rams will need behind the smaller Mumpfield and Atwell. Worth a sprinkle!

title: Sources: Vikings want to keep Kirk Cousins, talked to QB about staying in 2027
summary: The Vikings are interested in keeping Kirk Cousins as their QB next season, sources told NFL Network.

title: Despite Cousins trade, are Vikings back to square one at QB?
summary: Cousins can give some short-term relief, but his future and the search for a franchise QB remain uncertain.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings drew external praise  and generated internal celebration  this week after reacquiring quarterback Kirk Cousins , a beloved figure among team employees and a player with at least a reasonable chance of stabilizing an offense that has flopped in the past two seasons. 

 Regardless of how the next few months play out, however, the trade guarantees the Vikings will be in a familiar place next spring: looking for a starting quarterback. 

 There is a conceivable path toward keeping Cousins in 2027, but it wouldn't be simple -- and that's assuming he wants to play a 16th NFL season at age 39. Cousins' contract contains three void years from 2027 to 2029, giving the Vikings two options: Pay a $10 million roster bonus and bid him farewell, or negotiate a new contract. Anyone familiar with Cousins' business acumen knows that if he were to do anything other than demand a premium quarterback deal, it would be the first time in his career. 

 The topic surfaced briefly amid the week's chaos. General manager Nolan Teasley said there is "always potential" for exploring a future with Cousins, adding that the Vikings "understood everything that we were inheriting."

 

 Teasley was referencing Cousins' contract, but in a larger sense, it has always been clear that the GM inherited a perpetually open-ended quarterback situation when the Vikings hired him May 30.

 The decision to sign Kyler Murray to a one-year contract two months before Teasley arrived signaled the termination of the organization's faith in 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy , who was traded away in September. What has happened since is best viewed as extended triage after one of the all-time busts in Vikings draft history . Murray got six starts, a tryout hampered by a concussion and a strained hamstring, before the Vikings went looking for their next option. 

 Coach Kevin O'Connell refused to write off Murray as a failed experiment -- "It hasn't been ideal," he said, "but I wouldn't by any stretch say that's a complete thing" -- and it wasn't just coachspeak. Given the injury issues the Vikings have faced, beginning with Cousins' torn right Achilles tendon in 2023, there is a nonzero chance that Murray finds his way back onto the field in a meaningful way this season. But based on his performance so far, it's hard to consider him a realistic option to start in 2027. 

 

 The rest of the NFL's pending free agent class is, as usual, filled with veteran backups ( Jacoby Brissett , Marcus Mariota , Gardner Minshew II and Kenny Pickett among them) and flawed or limited current starters ( Deshaun Watson , Geno Smith ). It's always possible that a starter under contract becomes available via trade, whether it is the Los Angeles Chargers'  Justin Herbert or even the Los Angeles Rams ' Matthew Stafford . Former Vikings starter Sam Darnold 's future with the Seattle Seahawks  is unclear due to his contract and regression this season. ESPN's FPI projects the Vikings to have the No. 25 position in the 2027 draft.

 As a franchise, the Vikings are no stranger to the decision they're facing. Barring Murray's return, they'll field a different Week 1 starter in 2027 for the fifth consecutive season. They entered this season having had 17 different quarterbacks lead them in passing during a season in the free agent era, which began in 1993, tied for third most in the NFL. Murray was on track to the be the 18th, but Cousins would need to throw for only 1,023 yards over the Vikings' final nine games to overtake him. 

 The 2027 decision will have some heavy consequences. Most immediate among them is the impact on receiver Justin Jefferson , whose Hall of Fame arc has been threatened by the team's quarterback saga. Jefferson led the NFL in yards per game (96.5) over the first five seasons of his career (2020-24). Since Cousins' departure, Jefferson ranks No. 25 with an average of 60 yards per game. The Vikings have used eight different starting quarterbacks during that period, and Cousins' homecoming will mark the 15th time they have made an in-season change from one week to the next since the middle of 2023, when Cousins got hurt.

 Jefferson this week acknowledged what he called the "joy" of Cousins' return and said he is "pretty sure" the passing offense will elevate. But with a $49.4 million salary cap hit in 2027 that presumably will need an adjustment, he'll likely hit a natural inflection point this offseason. Jefferson has supported the team throughout the quarterback decisions that have impacted his production, but if there were ever a time for him to exert pressure on the process, it would be next spring. 

 

 Another critical ramification will be the type of offense the Vikings' 2027 quarterback will be asked to run. Lessons from the aftermath of Cousins' 2023 injury remain relevant. There is a narrow quarterback profile with a history of success in O'Connell's scheme. Murray played far below his career baseline, most notably with an 18.3% off-target rate, and McCarthy's confident performances following his trade to the New York Giants have raised some eyebrows among league sources. 

 In talking about Cousins' skills this week, O'Connell emphasized the "principles of how he plays the position -- the rhythm, the timing, the anticipation, the accuracy." Those attributes might sound central to the success of any quarterback, but there is enough of a sample size in Minnesota to suggest they need to be present at high levels for the Vikings.

 Many of the answers are in Cousins' hands. His performance over the coming weeks and months will factor heavily into whether the Vikings remain on track for the postseason and perhaps a deep playoff run. Or will his sentimental return serve as a bookend on an era approaching its natural conclusion?

 That story has yet to be written.

title: Patriots are 6-0 after a regular-season loss under Vrabel: Can they do it again?
summary: New England plays in Munich, Germany, this week. Catch up on what's happening abroad in this week's Patriots notebook.
full_text:
MUNICH -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

 1. Patriots resolve: The Patriots are 6-0 under coach Mike Vrabel in regular-season games after a loss, and they look to keep that streak alive Sunday as underdogs against the  Detroit Lions  at FC Bayern Munich Arena (Fox, 9:30 a.m. ET).

 Quarterback Drake Maye summed up Vrabel's knack for bringing out the best in his team in those situations, saying, "Coach Vrabes always says, 'Try not to ride the roller coaster. Try to ride the merry-go-round.' Keep going around and trying to keep the same mindset."

 A seven-hour international trip to Munich after the sting of last week's 45-27 home loss to the Packers has created a unique challenge. Not to mention the 6-2 Lions are among the league's upper-echelon teams, playing in arguably the league's best division, the NFC North.

 

 The 5-4 Patriots have their bye after the game, but the urgency around the team has been evident as it tries to stay afloat in the AFC playoff chase . If the playoffs started today, the Patriots would be the No. 7 and final seed in the AFC.

 Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson , who has a knee tendon issue that is threatening his availability for the game, has been pushing to play. Likewise with receiver A.J. Brown , who missed the past two games because of a knee flare-up but returned to practice this week and had Vrabel feeling "pretty good" about his status early Friday.

 As for the defense, which was carved up by the Packers in an uncharacteristic string of fundamental and communication breakdowns, the unit struck Vrabel's merry-go-round theme with its approach this week.

 "We've been there before. You get another opportunity and what you do with that is up to us," said cornerback Marcus Jones , one of the team's six captains. "We went back into the film room, accepted the situation of what we put out there on film, and our job is to not put that back out again. We have the guys that can do it."

 Cornerback Christian Gonzalez , the 2024 second-team All-Pro, is under the brightest spotlight. He was targeted relentlessly last week, allowing a career-high 10 catches for a career-high 187 yards, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Gonzalez will need to rebound against top Lions receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown (ranks ninth in receiving yards per game at 82.1) and Jameson Williams (leads NFL receivers in air yards per target at 15.43).

 Asked about the Patriots' resolve after losses under Vrabel, Gonzalez said it comes back to the team identity Vrabel preaches.

 "Leaning on the guys; after a loss, you stick together," he said. "You have a bad taste, so you want to go out there and play better."

 

 Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr was pleased with how defenders responded in their biggest practice of the week on Wednesday. That was held in Foxborough before players traveled to Munich later that night, and Kuhr cited energy, execution, and improved communication and connection among defensive backs as areas that created a "let's get this thing right" vibe.

 The Patriots had a similar situation after their 35-6 loss to the Jaguars  in Week 3 and rebounded with a 29-26 upset road win over the Bills. Can they do it against the Lions in Munich?

 "It's always a good reminder after a loss. It kind of wakes you up a little bit," tight end Hunter Henry said. "And obviously, the way we lost the other day will definitely wake you up."

 2. Travel strategy : Will it make a difference that the Patriots arrived in Munich on Thursday morning and the Lions arrived on Friday morning? The Patriots went the earlier route so they could have a walkthrough Thursday and then more of a higher-tempo practice Friday.

 "Just having done this a few times, maybe how you feel coming over here Friday and what you're able to get done, I felt like we maybe wanted to do a little more than what had been done in the past on Friday," Vrabel said.

 As for the Lions, coach Dan Campbell said he was "very confident" in the approach to arrive Friday. He acknowledged Friday is the "hardest day," as he saw "a little bit of the head bob" from players in meetings, but promised things would evolve.

 "I know every eight hours here, we're going to begin to acclimate," Campbell said. "I know by the time we hit Sunday morning into that Sunday afternoon game, we're going to be ready to go."

 3. Milton's fine system: The Patriots have had seven offside or encroachment penalties over the past two games, and defensive tackle Milton Williams has had enough. He shared Friday that he has instituted a fine of $1,000 for any front-seven defender who commits those infractions this week, with the proceeds going to Patriots support staff.

 

 "I had a couple earlier in the season. I feel like we talked about it, but it's not enough consequences that come with it, other than hurting the team," he said. "So hurt your pockets -- make you think about it a little bit more."

 4. Turnover tale: The Patriots have failed to record a positive turnover differential in all nine games this season, which is their longest drought since 2005, according to ESPN Research. It has been one of the top storylines of their season, along with injuries, and the theme resonated in Munich leading up to kickoff.

 Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels pointed to timing as a key factor in Maye's three interceptions last week against the Packers, saying, "If we see things a hair earlier, it might be a big play."

 Playing a turnover-free game was a noted goal among players this week.

 "It starts with the ball for us. Obviously, we haven't treated it well and have turned it over a lot," tight end Hunter Henry said in reference to the 19 giveaways that are tied for most in the NFL. "We've got to make a change in some aspect and put our foot down."

 5. German flavor: Among the lighthearted Patriots tales from Munich:

 
 Vrabel introduced trivia in Friday's team meeting by asking players if they knew the nine countries bordering Germany. No surprise that German-born practice squad offensive lineman Lorenz Metz had some of the answers. 
 Metz hosted the weekly offensive line dinner and introduced his teammates, who included tight ends and quarterbacks, to traditional German fare. "That was a lot of pork," center Jared Wilson said. 
 Some players visited McDonald's and relayed a surprise that chicken wings were on the menu. "The McDonald's here is top tier," Wilson cracked. 
 Milton Williams and special teamer Brenden Schooler said they were wide awake at 2 a.m. Friday, trying to adjust, with Schooler hitting the weight room in the hotel at 4 a.m. to get himself moving. 
 
 6. A.J.'s faith :  DeMario 'Pop' Douglas  said having Brown return to practice this past week gave the team a boost because he's the leader among receivers, and that has also shown up behind the scenes in a different way.

 "He started a bible study with some of the guys. I'm loving his growth in faith, and I feel like that's been getting us closer," Douglas said.

 

 7. They said it : "We're just always looking for guys that are looking for ways in as opposed to ways out. At this point in the season, 10 weeks straight without a bye, there's pretty much nobody out there that's 100%. We have to recognize that, but we also have to find ways to do our job. And Rhamondre's one of those players looking for a way in." -- Vrabel, on Rhamondre   Stevenson pushing to play through a knee tendon issue 

 8. Maye and FIFA: The Patriots spent three days  at FC Bayern Munich's training facility leading up to Sunday's game, and that had Maye reflecting on the days he played the FIFA video game with his brothers, one of whom often beat him with Bayern.

 "First thing that comes to mind is Harry Kane. Big fan of him," Maye said, before rattling off some players on the roster in a moment the German media seemed to appreciate.

title: Five questions for the Jets in the second half of the season
summary: After falling to 2-7, New York has to manage its current situation and setting up the future.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- A look at what's happening around the New York Jets :

 1. At the turn: The unofficial second half of the season begins Sunday against the AFC-leading  Buffalo Bills  (7-1). Here are five questions facing the Jets.

 Will Aaron Glenn survive the season? Another in-season coaching change is unlikely despite the 2-7 record. Owner Woody Johnson tried it two years ago, firing Robert Saleh after five games, and it backfired. Johnson has a strong affinity for Glenn and wants to give him every chance to succeed.

 That said, Glenn's record is damning -- 5-21, including 0-8 in the AFC East. He needs a strong finish to be back in 2027. Based on their opponents' current records, the remaining schedule ranks 20th in difficulty, according to ESPN's Football Power Index . It includes the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8), Miami Dolphins (1-7) and Arizona Cardinals (3-6). Glenn probably needs wins, and more than anything, he needs to convince ownership he can lift the franchise out of this losing vortex.

 

 Will Cade Klubnik get a shot? It happens a lot in the NFL. A team falls out of contention, pushes its bridge starter aside and gives the rookie quarterback an audition. The Jets appear to be on that track, but there's an X factor -- Glenn's job security. 

 This sets up a fascinating question for the five games after their Week 13 bye: Stay with Geno Smith , who's having a solid year, or give the Clemson rookie a chance?

 Best bet? Glenn rides with Smith a lot longer than the fanbase wants.

 Can Glenn fix the defense? A promising start has turned into a mess. The Jets have allowed the second-most points (127) over the past four games. Much of this falls on Glenn, whose self-proclaimed "superpower" is calling defensive plays. He didn't rule out the possibility of relinquishing playcalling, although that seems unlikely.

 Improvement is possible, as the Jets have only three games against top-18 scoring offenses, including the league-leading Bills (32 points per game) twice. It certainly won't help Glenn's job security if he fails in his area of expertise.

 Will David Bailey win Defensive Rookie of the Year? Bailey and New York Giants linebacker Arvell Reese are the two favorites. Raise this question in a New York City bar, and you're likely to hear a spirited debate.

 Bailey has 7.5 sacks, tied for the fifth most by a player in their first eight career games since the stat became official in 1982. He joins a top five that features Pro Football Hall of Famers Reggie White and Julius Peppers.

 "He's already a star right now," Bills coach Joe Brady said of Bailey. "He's going to be a problem for a lot of years."

 Can the Jets land the No. 1 overall pick? They have a 6% chance, according to projections by ESPN analytics. It would go up to 10% with a loss to Buffalo and an Indianapolis Colts loss to Miami. The Jets own the Colts' first-round pick. The next two weeks will be crucial, as the Jets face the Chargers and Dolphins.

 Buckle up for the second half.

 

 2. This is weird: Smith is having a career year -- half the time, that is.

 When the Jets are in their own territory, Smith's QBR is 60.8 -- his best mark since becoming a full-time starter in 2022. In opponents' territory, it drops to 34.8 -- his lowest mark.

 The 26-point discrepancy is the largest in the league among qualified passers.

 What happens when Smith crosses midfield?

 Statistically, the amount of man coverage jumps from 28% to 45%, per ESPN Research. That means tighter windows. He also faces more pressure (34% to 38%), although the blitz rate is the same.

 Otherwise, it's hard to explain the difference.

 "Believe me, I've examined this hard," said offensive coordinator Frank Reich, who believes defensive coordinators don't start playing different coverages until around the 15-yard line.

 In the end, he said, they must coach better and play better.

 3. Old rivals: Brady has known Smith so long that he can recall his pre-Geno days. They crossed paths in a South Florida high school game in 2007. Smith was a highly touted junior quarterback for Miramar, Brady an unheralded senior wide receiver for Everglades. Smith's team won the battle of the rival schools

 "When I first knew him, he was Eugene Smith," Brady told Buffalo reporters, referring to Smith's given name.

 P.S.: Brady went by Joey in those days.

 

 4. From the past: Brady interviewed for the Jets' head coaching vacancy in 2021, the year they hired Saleh. This marks the fourth time this season they've faced a head coach who was a past interviewee. The others: Todd Monken (2019), Mike Vrabel (2025) and Jeff Hafley (2025). The Jets wound up with Adam Gase and Glenn, respectively, in those hiring cycles.

 The trend continues next week with Jim Harbaugh, who lost out to Rex Ryan in 2009.

 5. Pick six: This isn't a huge deal in the grand scheme, but the compensation in the trade that sent safety  Andre Cisco to the  Detroit Lions  was changed. The Jets are receiving the Lions' 2029 sixth-round pick; it was originally a 2028 sixth-rounder. The reason is because Detroit raised some concern with Cisco's physical, so the two teams pivoted to a contingency instead of calling off the trade.

 It worked out well for the Jets, who still got a hard pick (not a conditional pick) for a player who had been demoted to fourth on the safety depth chart. Mougey has a history of using late-round picks as currency, so there's a reasonable chance that it will be traded at some point.

 6. New trend on the horizon? The Jets did some outside-the-box thinking last week to help their kickoff coverage unit, which got burned for a touchdown the previous week.

 Special teams coordinator Chris Banjo replaced punter Austin McNamara , his kickoff guy, with fullback/tight end Andrew Beck , one of their coverage players. It allowed them to have an extra tackler on the field. The Kansas City Chiefs had four returns, none longer than 29 yards.

 "It ended up being a weapon for us," said Banjo, declining to say if Beck will continue to handle kickoffs.

 Retired special teams coach Mike Westhoff, who talks to Banjo every week, expects the strategy to catch on around the league. He said the new kickoff rules minimize the importance of hang time. If a team has a position player who can boot the ball to the landing area, he said, it creates a numbers advantage because of the extra player in coverage.

 "It's coming," Westhoff said. "I think you're going to see more and more of this."

 

 Beck said he was "fired up" with the new assignment. He never was a kicker, per se, though he did some emergency kicking in practice while playing for the Denver Broncos a few years ago. There was only one glitch last week -- his last kickoff went out of bounds for a penalty -- but the experiment was deemed a success.

 "Give the coaches the credit," Beck said.

 7. The right kicker: Mougey was criticized for allowing popular kicker Nick Folk to bolt as a free agent in the offseason. Initially, the decision didn't look good, as the Jets cycled through a handful of kickers. Turns out that Mougey knew exactly what he was doing.

 A struggling Folk was cut this week by the Atlanta Falcons despite a $4 million guarantee. Jets kicker Jason Sanders had some preseason hiccups, but he settled down and he's performing well (21-for-24 on field goal attempts) at a lower cost ($1.3 million).

 8. Will power: It will be interesting to see if disgruntled edge rusher Will McDonald IV gets a bump in playing time , as Glenn indicated. He needs to be better against the run. When he's on the field, the defense allows 4.8 yards per rush, per Next Gen Stats. It's 3.6 yards when he's not on it.

 9. Did you know? The Jets have lost eight straight division games, the longest active streak in the NFL.

 10. The Last Word: "There's a number of things that we have to fix and get better at, but we feel like, man, we're right on the cusp of trying to break through." -- Glenn.
